Tis an age which has gone past since a new book has begun.
 We began this prior one in Vancouver, which feels both near and far ago. Winter writings definitely laid the ground for it, but the fruits began to blossom during the coming spring.
 Through the age past we wrote ferviously, during the discourses, the histories and acceptance.
 Now a new book has begun, charactized best by us becomnig a man, and now becoming me.
 Who is it we are really? What positions and aims would we accept from the things within them, rather than without. What advantage do we have, virtues to enlight. Where may our foundations grow.
The first of these topics is virtue, for she marbles us in such delight, yet mingles and sways in delicate mystery.
 Foremost is the language used to describe her. For most words reflect something definite or categorical. "Of this is those." That or it's some kind of property, a way it's being. But this latter does not have the fairest acess to properties of motion, or relation between things. And that's what virtue is.
 For in life we are tasked with things, neccessarily and for all things benefit. But we often overlook these demands and focus on the goal, the fruit and the end. And this belies perhaps a warranted confidence and comfortable desire. But it does not hold virtue. What she is comes down to an awareness and submision to the prescence of task, and the more or less accepting manner of amendment, whereby our attending to such task is more or less sufficient for us to be pleased, and by that focused. The ends that come out are more like buds and droppings of a continous harvest. Virtue is for life: goals are for stopping.
 There is the manner of love then, which compliments, or in some cases vanguards virtue, as her upper end; or comes as an effect from a more defined rear virtue --who we may consider in isolation. At any rate, this amiability to task, the appreciation of it, the merry, in the suppleness and succeeding effect, lies a cloud of delight and cheer, and in that care and awe. I once mentioend this in terms of marks, whereby things in such a state would stand out to you and beckon you forth. Perhaps it is still suited. The difference, is that via virtue, our draw is not only born from grounds bade from duty and ease, but contained to that. "It is not so that we reach a point of stability and cheer, see the stars, then fly to them."
 Something I'm wondering is whhy certain things draw you. And whether there is a manner of something being drawn to you. We often find ourselves light and gleeful, for so many scents excite our mind. Yet, certain things pass by, unaware of me, and not exactly presenting themselves to me as to be drawn. Two things have occured in this. One, is I realized that I may form, and at any rate supply, our own love, to anybody and anything. For the love of a woman may have no bounds; and not all open themselves to this. Nor is it entirely proper, given the lenght of such mingling. "None act in so full out ways, only to then leave. The regard though for duration keeps the doors more or less shut less a key is had or invitation granted. Otherwise all would encourage everyone to love them openly and impulsively --for it'd be expected that they just go, thereby warranting a low standard. But committment and stay is the norm, and so not everyone and everything and every moment will do." Love may still occur. Being personal is like this, being near and present. But then lies the wish to be seen and cared for. And in part I don't know why. Is it because it opens you up to love? The pleasure is not just; it's but a moment. As we walk around, we feel this grin, and a good one when we consider the thing invoking this, about others seeing me, being impressed, admiring me, wanting me, seeing me for good and great. "I feel like I'm shining." Why is this exciting. For I admitt, when I walk through a crowd I often feel nervous, like everyone is looking at me, either down, or as though I'm a mystery. That, or I'm chest up, being noticed, people saying, 'oh my'. And glory is merely this feeling, but bridled upon your propiety rather than charm. Yet, I do not actually want anyone to speak to me. I don't want a crowd, or to sign autographs; I care not for theyre time and attneiton. I just want to be thought of.
 And I belive it all comes down to the matter of honor and duty. Which is to say, virtuous oblige to tasks, rather than succumbed ones, where relief and ill-merry is pursued. Wishing to be noticed comes from an imbalance, or at least untuned time of that former manner. For in virtue, who once perked up her head, showing me the green in her way, held me there, and through time and content, disposed me to her conduct and wares. In growing though, you experience often times where you are under the scalpel (so to speak), but lack the footing, or at least heart, to be so fortuitous and ample, and thereby feel beckoned to relief. "I am right though, in my suffering; the path is just. People should look at me. They know where I've come from and am returning to." Such is the mind for glory. Or, "man, those people, they don't notice me, and I'm doing so well while theyre not." Such is the mind of a cynic; who is not wrong, but patronizes others because he is alone. In my experience this came from me knowing more about virtue than deed; and thus upon the richest of successes, not truly having won.
 And then there is that peak of becomnig a man, whereby the slips and turns of that result in a more or less squicning and or cringing stability; as though we know about virtue and her ways, stand by our rules, and are aware of our trouble; for which we concive nor invent some remedy, but stay with the trouble, breathe, endure. Moreover, do we adapt, and rise above the conduct we once thought fit: we give credence to the hurdles around me. Much of youth is defined by such hurdles being a frustration, as though 'man, haven't we won yet! I just want to get over the things I have to do so I can pursue what I want'.
Being a man, oh how it can get drowned in action. And much of what I see is in relying on our manhood, and more or less testafying it; not putting other things up on a hill, as though theyre required. It seems better to look at them as things which would be nice and supportive while you continue to grown and maintain. Then there's those things which flow naturally, such as sums, as though fruits and or makings of a firm and steady state.
Hooey, its been quite a day, a month, a year even. The age it seems is not even faded.
 I see, foremost, that what I want, see, believe in, is a life, literally. Looking at something ahead, being exicted, fretting over something even, this are states, conditions, orbits around things, rather than a life, a flow, a continuity, a direction of progress, endurance and felicity.

 times are different though. Such a state is not tenuable, nor adventageous, for productivity or happiness. What has come about though is that our view is different, our aim, our tilt.  Indeed, one fair insight into all of this, is that the flourishing in life is not so that you may pursue this or reach that, but that you have things around your proper pace. If, in your peace and succour, you see some thing far away, may you shed light on it, bring it close, ready yourself and soften its groove, 'so upon our arrival we fit', all while keeping our pace.
 Perhaps it is our nature as one so endowed and enriched by the matter of pace to not so easily fit with others. For they have theyre own pace, or lack theyre of. And this is fine, and marks the ways of more or less all people. But it creates community though; as though a savanah of buffalo, each going here and there, in theyre groups, with theyre crowds, but amongst one another; interfering not, keeping things on the whole safe, and otherwise respecting the fact that we all share this drive and deed to be on pace. This is reflected in nods while passing by. "Enjoy your own day while I continue with mine." Having my day be mine feels respected and permitted by me and all.
All that being said, where there is tightness in our groin. Not our mind, though the idea of work is something overhwelming and depleting. But our life is slacking due to our lack of running. Simple. And this is so out of worry and fear, and the energy we have to balance that out. Doubt creeps in, and then inertia.
 The isse is not the floor. We've been sitting on it for 8 years now and these issues were not always there. What has happened though is that we actually act like a kid who has homework or needs to go to bed but wants to game instead. Were like that, whereupon our training, we play the whole day. This isn't wrong, and it's not so much that miss other things we have to do; its merely so that given how much we train, the quality of it, that then playing throughout the day demands so much more. And we often don't do that, simply out of excess or lapse in timing, so we bear the load of having worked but then continued being active all day. There tends not to be an issue if we workout and do nothing.

For in work, its obligation is sourced from the nature of things, in that we are animals, and civilized one's who've formed an economy, whereby our present work-type is bound. But this deed upon is made like our need of breathe. We usually take this as something which may be absent. But what about food on your table? This is something that could be missing, but is something we enjoy also. But it surrounds this base of life, that such thing is needed. And having it steadily makes you entirely sure. Some, in this age, or any other, bank theyre satiety on things farther and bound. While a man may truly be happy if is belly is full and with a roof over his head, and that these things are by fortune and equity, or agreeable effort, owned. You may really breathe then, for danger is not at your door, nor begrudgement of this neccessary thing. "I am glad that this shark will not reach men; I am less pleased by the enormous effort to stop him so. But I am painfully aware, or at least inately tuned, to attend to the danger that would be if I stopped. For which I am bound." And the coals of life simmer upon this idea, whereby we loose not our chains but our impingement by them. "Less one be given theyre needs permanetly, or the need go's away."
I sit here sometimes, having more or less done what I need to do, but doing anything more feels waring. Yet, I question whether something easier could be had. Nor do I humour availability that gets embalmed due to our want but not realistically. We expect to much, are aware too little.

 One thing, if I can even form this thought, is to the inevitable nature which appeals to us, yet seems somewhat hollow when assessed. Does your life change? Expectation is built on promise and probability, and too small matters or the deepest of things, so that route lay. This is how our work is in some sense, which brings up the second thing on my mnid. Namely, that we may approach things in a problematic way, where we attribute ours and others life as being conditioned and set; and in that we prioritize the needed efforts but also dear experience: our life as it were. But along this obligate line. Others may be seen to have dinners, or go out on weekends, or even have lunches or convos at work together. But the deed is writ and submitts all these to it; and it keeps on and squeezes out all sense of jealousy or elatement. "For the deed continues on." And my life is tenured as to fit and be sprung by such action. The other way of seeing things is without problems, whereby your own efforts and deeds are accepted as part of your nature, and given leave to be, since they are not elected but more or less custom. So we may be ourselves with those who are nothing like us, for we already are. this manner of life often creates desires which are hard to grasp, for they reflect little of how other people are; in that, they are a)different, and b) not so undisposed. In the former approach this doesn't matter to me, for we are attending to our own differensts, and living our life as is right and wanting around it. But if our own differences don't matter, and were tranquil, then we feel ourselves wafting into the complexion of other people. "For we so easily see all and any of theyre brighter sides." And in many ways this is a very present and breathing expeirence, and one that has no real fault except for history; whereby our natural gait doesn't create such ease within our duties: custom and habit don't suffice, or vice wiggles in. And indeed, in these moments, where we've more or less let ourselves be vulnerable to like, but then feel like were getting deported, 'back to boarding school, to ship up', we feel like were leaving, and thus rustle ourselves back in. But with a sort of affection that was merely our own, sparked by what we saw, but from our point of view. The moral of this, as found with Bella, is that you could just be yourself, and that would have been enough. Again, vice is waiting for a slip, as our tender satisfaction was not in fact the only real motive, or compulsion ready to be raised. Alas, history broke the state, and purity had to resume some other day. Much foolishness and greed gets conjured in this broken moments; as though peace will not be found again. But it will always, and has mind you. There is some perspective though, that in many ways there is an over-infatuation, or at least over-affectioante state, which your peace seeps into; for you let go of the reigns, and by virtue of the calmenss around, allow your tranquility to direct your motion. Yet duty remains, vice lingers, and satisfaction is not so easy to find. That is why you seek someone, to be near them. But this is hard to do. And indeed, awkwardness is the opposite of the right state, for nothing open nor steady can be procurred. But it just seems that our life being so, but with the more genuine mindest that 'of those who excite me or draw affection, that it is merely so', that rather than feel free to drift into that, but to no likely end and at risk of folly, that we speak as we would, but not with much stake in mind. Our understanding of such satiety confines me to the limits and accesibility of that. Which I find, in admitting, puts our life in persepctive, and draws both the deed of it upfront, so as not to take our ball of the prize; but also, with more meaning and pace we make, as our manner of being so attentive and personal is not a limiting factor to who we may be genial towards. And I believe truyl, that rather than succumb to the parsimonous potential or foolish expectation of meaning coming from any which way, that you keep your form, ready your favor, and initiate yourself into social and creative avenues which would fit you personally. These are not things you come across or are privy to by chance relation, but things you find, and invovle yourself with out of some mixture of initiative but like also. That practical philosophy group spoke to me on all levels: the subject paired the elemetns of group disucssion, and it all being organized as such. May petals of truth fall on your dreams, whereby that evening sight of a sun setting in Vancouver, be brought forth into reality not because there is a sun, but because there is somewhere your going: the weather and tidings of which may be noticed then.
It is not right to say that our life is our own, but rather, that life is what it is, and for those who go off and do nice things, or even compell me, be it as I or someone else, that so the road of life lay, and we are always driving. It can not be understated enough the challenge of work, and how it plays on your mentality, as to be pleased with what you have, but moreover, have focus of what is at hand and presnet, rather than what is ahead. History has shown us a flawed hand here, but a natural one. Everyone grows up, and falls and learns, and so has our time in the full part of life been just like this. I was thinking today of an essential feeling, though it's quality is lost. But it had something to do (I wish it were with me) with my manner of liking, pleausre and interest, and how it was not by some rule but some strong fashion; as though we were not dissauded from duty nor bent towards lust and elation, but rather steady wonder and light. I never migrated away from this. Even in our moments of absence, where I saw others invovled and arranged with people, and I thought of the same; who I'd be with, how we'd all relate. But strenght came to fashion; centering on me primarily as our abscence in life procurred. And indeed, this grew our manner of experience whereupon most people left and there was not much but me. We merely heightened what once had so much company, or at least finer tidings amidst our leisure. Little was there, or what was held toil and by that discontent. There was no shortness of worry and shame, as though our experience, however just, was allowed. This all centered on the disturbance of work, in its approach and experience; and the insolidity that its cease would bring, 'to which the turn from freedom back to approach came'. I am mispresenting this sense of shame; for doing as I needed always gave me leave to do as I want; it was just that the matter of want was disturbed by what I had to do. And given that trouble, the contempt felt came from us trying to acquiesce to that trouble, and later on improve the good around (to make it worthwhile). In a word, respect for labor felt unremarkable nor worthy of respect. Hard to share still. And it comes down to that essential feeling, of mighty peace and awe. Easy it was as a child, for we were raised well, as were we good in ourselves. That same pleasure and cool you got from eating well following a practice, gave wamrth and reason to our way. The way eroded though upon our emotional dissaray during graduation, and our reckless disenfranchisment from our mom and dad. Indeed, we had not the calm or novel stability to go through college, nor that of a job. Strange indeed that we became so personal. Yet, it was our wellness that procurred this, as in being so we were proper and welcomed at home. Only as time went on did expectation grow. And indeed, our own comfort in being as we were grew fundemental, and our natural want extended outside our parents bounds. Work felt essential, and was something we dealt with; and upon its mundanity we moved, which afforded it's own satiety. Yet, in that moment, we quickly realized that we were not free, and that work would continue. We felt this sense of freedom, being on our own, yet it was as though the leash were lengthened: still we were chained. And this more or less lead to a moment of aimlessness. We felt not bad, as we were stbale, but we were not happy. Young and novel motions oft create with them a sense of progression and outlook ahead. But as reality settled, or what we in fact werre set for was reached, we felt still. Without an end we turned to gratuity. And this felt unsatisfying, nor made work tolerable. So we cultivated ourself, and as it were, the view of happiness. This didn't stop our choices being made as to remove that burden of work. But so in this the road to propiety lay. For we fidgeted here and htere, to no real acclaim nor tolerance. And we were asked to return to work, no questions asked. And I fought this, finding it unneccessary. The present was good enough, stable, and in the back of my mind, promising. But alas, we submitted, and were employed. Here, it felt as though this mode we were in had no compramise, barring a return to a 'step by step' progression, 'where nature and whit carved the way'. This had no sight in mind, and so we lived in that essential form, of work. And we had done this before, but upon beckoning. In that early time of employment we felt that novelty and foresight, seeing time ahead. But in this, time felt as though this were all it was. Indeed, we held views that saw us some place ahead, marbled in those hidden colors of esteem. But very much so were these just dreams, and we begudingly went through our existence. The nature though of this way became almost self-fufilling, for as we more or less evened out in our deeds, and they felt less like burdens, the actually mode of being so employed felt not like something which in theory ought compell us to see something elsewhere and ahead; nor, in practice, was it so unfufilling or contrary to the goods which, on theyre own, felt not so much disturbed: and indeed they were quite good for me, what I liked.
 From the peak of that point to now, a similar thread has woven along, and that is namely the mystery of our expeirence, and why we care about writing, death, inquiry and the gods, the witcher at that; and this doubt brings in light from other pastimes and wonders, of girls and friend gourps, outings on the weekends, dinners, high finance even. And in that, there lies what can only be described as a maintained tranquility, a happiness which comes now from what is planned nor promied, but from what our choices create in us, to exhibit and imbue naturally. That is perhaps the greatest, but also discouraging admission, that the good we feel is not something we do for the sake of work or in spite of, that the experience resulting is one merely esteemed by its effect being one of causes born in commisery with work (or whats neccessary); but rather, what is good as an experience, purely on the basis of it's flavor and hue, is born from ations which are esteemed as so because of the effect they create. Work, by all acocunts, becomes this thing which, in a mature sense, you acquiese to, and in some sense lean on as something which your ordinadry pleasures corroborate with. For as children we have certain wishes and glees, but they get polished off as responsibility is introduced. As it were, the good of leisure and liberty are not totally encommpassing, as you lack the seen and or felt promise and comfort of a friend, of someone to trust, play with, see, look forward to. These are natural wants. But in our preservation of such liberty, which you hold and are equal to foremost, there lies a disparity between what others have become accustomed to, or accepted, and thus you have less of a place or tenure to relate and or connect. And one of the primary virtues, or at least manners in which one ought take, is not to let theyre liberty become something of a goal, as if it be rightous for you to be as you are but in that suffer in solitude; nor, and this is perhaps foremost, ought you let the esteem and or product of such liberty sprout promises of the alleviating or social sort. "to make our solitude more exciting and thus less lonesome, or to spark the sight others and by that render off your difference by making others more likened and or changed for you."
Worked seemed to come into the spotlight today, as this thing ever pressing, requiring of me, not going away. I think that our own positive expeirence in this gets pressured, and so we ant the attention from others. With Bella, that attention is not expected, but so is there friction, and perhaps disinterest (to say the least) of us being humourous with her. And anyone for that matter. It pays though to be alone, and not feel like were missing, or being kept out. Nor do I find much to envy. I find it alsmost irovokably true that being ourself is what we seek; and that others relationship with you determines whether you may. Even those who I have but a courteous relation with, so may we be so courteous. That friction with Bella does make me feel kept out of certain conversations; but so be it, there's friction. Nor are we that wanted. It is perhaps our own hunger that creates so. For most conversations that we feel this way about come from us being normally courteous; while such convo is about, to quote Amber, 'shooting the shit'. Sometimes a conversation draws me in to do so; other times not. I like to be on that focused and proper pace, for the sake of work. As such convos end. And distraction does not lead to much focus or binding to the work path. Its no big deal, and indeed, being ourself tends to lighten our load. Its just not something for you to grasp, but something which remarks your normal being. It has been 3 months now, and Bella and I are not much at odds ends, but rather ambivolent. I'm fine with that. We really see that if we see her or anyone conversing, such as Tara and Cresha, that we are personally weighed on, as though jealousy occurs via our own want. But we can sit with ourselves and settle. Such is the deed of work well lived, and a bountiful life folded through that. That is the way. One insight is that we often want others to see us, remember us, for us to be notorious and known. This differs from that earlier time in the year, when we would be open, but from ourselves; that latter kind of harmony and tranquility; where all good and needed was in motion, and so we could lavish a little, in nicities and plenty. Now however, it seems like were more harkoned to how other people seem; rather than putting ourself forth, we tend to need a welcoming, or at least something from them. In our calm delight we brought forward small things, and did not over step. But in times past we have been more forethright; our first time at Superstore reflects this. And indeed, it seems like we do so for the sake of being noticed. Yet, such notice comes at our negligence of work and life, and in both committment and effect. As such, were almost hoping to get away from work, to take it off our mind; yet we still live as we do, but hope for ease around, for others to see me and attend to me, as if some supporting garment.
Honesty is the most due process, for all things in need of it are waiting.
 One thought that's come to mind is that of our life, and its way, it's form, its manner. For an age it seems, with inconsistency bringing us away, we've not been just. We've live for the moment, for the day, for the way, and felt plentiful in doing so. But to no avail. Much to do with wellness and great expeirence comes to pass here, in both its accessibility, but also seeming compramise for things thought unfit. But I find, at most, that our time in being so, and cultivating, has not been just. For there was a time where expectation was near absent, and our own prior good deed mixed with ouro irreverance for anything which gave life to our state of somberness, allowed for the sights and development of our experience.
 Through the age though this has never settled as something tenuable, either because it had us be so original that living independantly had no fun nor smoothness to mingle with. By common ways, and ones which we saw as fitting, for pressures of neccessity surrounded us, and perhaps as aid and guide for the good which we ourselvrs sought, 'for a home of our onwn', that we abided such process; but doing so with fidelity and succour for our fine experience, grew poor habits and inclinations; all, namely, sprouted by our worn and leary relationship with duty and things of appeal around.
 Perhaps the greastest of truths rest on a more neccessary factor, an element if you will; namely, the principple of being, the encumbance to live well and through no matter our situation nor feeling. For the future may not seem bright, or may feel dimmer than our vice or confidence curry. But we must still show up, eat well, claim our plenty. At any rate, upon this immutable deed, lies the fairest of insights, the moral of our reflection; and that is, namely, that of all things oppertune, for which staked upon oppertunity, advantage or relief, that so ought these be given actual meaning and substance; for our actions that come about, our intentions at least, only move and (re)position by such decree. And the truth of our time, the looseness of our days, is that the decree we've followed is soft and ill formed.
 It is known that a rich being can be tasted, easily and often, but that such tune gets drowned out by nature's basic commands: to work and, sometimes, be seated. My merriest of prinicples says 'that all I ought do, and what funnels in the measures of must, is all and only that which affords me, or cooperates with me, on that simple quest to live in full and constant comfort. Quality speckles such end with matters of freshness and vitality, but wonder and might too --we care not for a frequent fling with sugar and crumbs'. Law and custom are an odd thing here, for they may need you to profess your understanding of what is requested of you; so that in your liberty you are still becoming of one subject to standard. As per family, I find this to be something embellished from that merry living; whereby in patrimony and marriage you broaden your find: playing that tune in company.
 That is all to say, that in playing such a tune, you may lean into the pedigree of it; something like that at least. But this, to be clear, and I submitt this with no hesitancy, that such tune is so easy, so rewarding, so dear. Yet it get's muffled, as I said. And one response is to identify with the very attempt to play song, and by that, one of your experienced quality. The vice though is that you take pleasure, and usually form expectations, by the seeming virtue of your history with such tune, and by that very attempt. "A good beyond itself, but the idea of it: givig you confidence but also promise."
I simply lack the focus and diredction of moral standing. Which is to say, an informend and well fashioned state, as though against some begging force, and for some uncommon end.
 One notion which is on my mnid is that of work and duty, and how this indeed rubs against you and requires, or benefits at least, from sound action. But this is not to say that without such things, ill-fortune and deeds as it were, that you'd be merry and happy.
 Now I don't wish to say that were merely talking about more or less passive or grazing states compared with those elected and fashioned.
 It comes down to our choie to eat at certain times a day, and certain foods at that, and to be smoewhat hygenic, to sit on the floor, sleep without a blanket.
 What I suspect, is that going without a blanket for instance, does notcibly increase my sleep and vibrancy; yet, the aim of this, or motive, is mixed beyond the pure appeal of that, but with the desires and experiences which such qualities aid. That is, we find more benefit from writing when limbre, and sleeping wel provides that. The snag I'm feeling is that of quality for quality sake, or recognizing at least that limberness in this case is good in general. Perhaps it is better to say that such quality get's elevated in worth by what it aids. So writing better engraves this quality as being so good. For I do feel someitmes that we have lots of energy but not much to use it with. And indeed, things, as it were, collect in our lives as things which are asked of us and drawn by us, and in that, benefited or not by circumstance or willfull forces. Reason tells us what is just, and what we can hope to change, or reposition, while wisdom helps pivot our actions as to respond wherever we in fact are. As we mentioned before, we may take too much refuge in our very experience in acting well, and by that, form hope and promise, and more often than not be too pleased with ourself. Perhaps the deepest of soft virtues is this thing; for it comes rom true success and character, yet can get coaxed into loosing that basic moral sense, whereby there is something needing to be done, for which our satisfaction and anticipation rest upon; and instead, we think to highly of ourself, or feel our seld deserving of reverance or pity, 'for we are someone who tries the mightiest and noblest of things'. Being the one who's written these annals, it is known that the peak of our adolescence was in being frustrated with folk for not being in a way that made us cohesive: we were as such cynical. The peak of this adult forray, or completion of our self, is in our lack of expectation, but want of things, and feeling doubt as to theyre merrit and our reason for wanting them. It was as though, in our completion, where nature took sway, that we felt drawn to things and open to them: as though we could be whoever they wanted us to be: for the vein in the marble was what our practice had once manifested outside: so we could fashion such clay (so to speak) in appealing ways.
So the year has come about rather nicely, though with some hiccups. From the moment we asked Bella out we've felt off, and more or less deflated. Just hard to avoid. The worst element is that work became something of a chore, or at least a point we were trepidatious about. I wanted to rekindle things, or felt wweird and seperate from ignoring her. This made work less gracious, and so we felt moved to think of things elswhere. But this proved hard to do, nor ideal. It is not what I please, given that we are going to work. Nor is it our script to pick up and leave. As it were, we have lines, but our situation with Bella made it hard to read them.
 Why this has been so is hard to say. One basic point is that we thought ourselves fine to talk with her, and act like nothing ever happened. This seemed not so. But the real insight is that as she faded from our mind, and as someone we were aware of or keen to talk to, or aware of whether she had any liking or distates for me, that so did the rest of our life come to fruition. I could see that we wanted things, motion, relief, focus. Indeed, Diablo coming out had this anticipation, and created that natural momentum. But uneccessarily. There is a force from work, and feeling steady is not ill of you. I just want to imagine people are there for me more, and care about me more than they probally do. Which is natural. The conversations you see other people having, or bantering, is no different than what you do, and is that so special? It is merely a passtime.
 And so we moved back in march, have been here since. The novelty is warring off, and the price is a bit too much. By all acocunts we'd be fine to earn a 200+ on top of rent. Meaning, 1 4 week shift for 900, nothing for less, and 2 for this 1000. We could just stay here, and our choice will reflect that as we pitter on. There is not much to worry about, and I'm not. Just trying to keep on top of things. Yoga has come about, though I notice there are preferred sessions when were stiff or tired. Free range is returning, and I find that our yoga helps us directly and with confidence.
 I think what we lack in life is that all mighty continence; which in certain moments seeks passion, while in others it steadies itself against our standard and deeds, and the process of our action. This was in part the issue with Bella, as it interupted that natural harmony and satisfaction which came from the nodes of duty of ahead. This is returning, and we need only get a grip on things. Little shift pickups can really satiate the ambivolence of our stay. I'm fine to leave, but happy to wait for something of preference. No biggy.
 I take the attitude of keeping on. Not dreaming, but pleasing ourselves with the softness of our duty and prescence of people who are, despite not so much firends, but commrades, peers, and folk who I like and enjoy; some even know me. And it is there prescence in something fundemental and ever on which quiets that seeking of something broader or exciting. Our great life is enough.
We've written a million words, and all of them bear the line of experience, and how we prefer to have it. This all comes down to our unique choice to sit on the floor. For the requirments of this extend beyond what was the norm prior, in eating well; and so to for the aim of that is the floor but a richer formation, in both a means and end.
 One of the odd happenings over the recent years is similar to an even older happening, namely the innate, or at least customary happenign, of what you deem good; and it no longer requiring diligence or planning. Yet, in this natural gait, you often run into moments where something else is sought, or you don't so ardently nor sharply exhibit that nature; or, most notably, a mistake, from negligence or ignorance, happens.
 One iosight is that passtimes, be it work or company, buffer your time in being as you please, for it allows you to be not. Often we feel the need to force our experience, for moments that are not so naturally sharp have no where to go but into something resembling indolence. Which evokes passion or further ware. For doing nothing feels poor, and we envy those who have things, and feel ashamed that we don't. Yet, there are right and fair things to do. It is the mnetality though. Not that there are not things good in themselves, but in the space were talking, having something you can look forward to, or count on, remedies the frequent need to rest and let be.
 This all comes back to the recent years, where such things were not present, and so the precedent to be was laid upon me. Oddly though, this did not leave me empty and craving, but rather more reasonable and elite in our custom. The folly in this was of a neccessary and impractical sort, but solid no less. But, what I mean to say primarily, is that we became so much better that we did so much more; and this has become great in both the quanity and quality of our expeirences. Yet the flow of life could not be avoided; and no passion, planning nor industry could alleviate your need to rest. By this choice or that manner, we've no garnered company nor easy itinerary. And so consistently w'd reach points that had me feeling poor, or moving in contrary ways, 'to cease the indolence, or taste for doing something'. Trust is a huge part, as it feels like something is there. And I tread on this notion; for if motion is always what we seek, and expectation is but a promise of something to come, and thereby a remark of your insatiety and unease at doin nothing, then are such things of the utmost importance, or is this immutable need a symptom of something esle.
 What then may we do in our life. For things are so good, as are we, in heart and mind, that we have no need, or less of one, to crave and or affirm some road ahead. Were stricken not with idleness, nor heavily when we do. It is almost as if things are so well and stable that dreams and fancy are beyond sight.
 As rgards health, the only worthwhile remark is that of consistency, and allowing for good things to come to be by right action. Such actions need themselves be tended to, and not done prematurely, out of insecurity or wishing to move. Note that playing Diablo or anything for that matter is spending, and you cannot train so wholly when your empty. Indeed, training allows for work and other things to be less costly. But we still have an account, and you can feel it. By all counts we've flirted with the edge of natural movement; whereby some pushups even seemed laudible. We've done this with squats on two occasions, without much gratuity. Doing free range can leave me feeling a little sore in the neck. But by all standards this is our stiff body being brought out of its lowering stride. Nonetheless, exercise is the trickiest of things; not food; that is quite simple, especially if your finances are in check. Which they are, to be clear, as we are fine to loose a little, and working a little bit extra, plus your gst and stats, makes for a fair stability over several months. Great. And food is about carbs, as oil fills in the calories. Your physical stature, as remarked by your place on the floor and doing things frequently on that, requires the more obscure and demanding task of patience, adjustment, forbidty in principle and practice, and quelling doubt and inertia, yet also smartly and decently obliging the impulse and want to move. One element is that of priority, and allowing that compulsion to move to bear itself when it feels right, and allowing this to be a primary exhibition. For rest is then had, and lighter motion. We must ingest this fundemental thing. For principally, like work, it is needed. But also to introduce and sustain motions, for they may at certain times not be there. And allowing them to come into the fray rightly and well is near essential.
 The form of this is rich in bounty but ceaseless in demand. But, the biggest pitfall, which our pleasure and sanity lean on, is in over doing yourself while in such a state. For it offers such, but falls unber false principles and errors, but almost naturally, for there is no true resting state, merely a lighter one. And we know this in our humour and compulsion, to do or not, to sit or play. Consistency requires patience sometimes. But so is it worth admitting that our life is not to forgiving for this inertia coming back to motion, or incorporating the motion done. We don't really enjoy doing nothing. Nor is there much which is otherwise easy to do. We beckon to the winds that lift our sails, but do so without the calmness that such winds will come later, and that we could restore right now. There is less to look forward to. I think of a philosophy meeting Thursday nights, or soccer nearby on Mondays and Saturday, and some vegan/spirit lunch on tuesdays. Even just messaging someone. For my biggest issue with friends is that I don't have this drive to invite them do something. And for those who do, it is usally our over emphasis on them, and not sitting well enough to merely talk to them, and like them as I do. For interest does not stirr there either, but rather a procrastination-like passion, satiated by the excitment of doing something together, when in fact, a more near and direct conversation with them soothes our mind. What is right comes easy. For we see more, or are fine with it as it is. We seek not. And all of this sounds burdensome and not so fun or rewarding. But it may be. The right thing has to be there. Maybe the spiritual meeting is a hastle and you don't light up about it. Maybe practical philosophy is somehting your really look forward to.
I look at my life and admitt nothing but everything. It is in some sense hard but easy also, as you can say, for insatnce, that we have an emotional connection with Bella. This is receding naturally, and more or less out of loss. But that is the thing going away. And I think of our feelings about her, grieving, comparing, jealousy, and it's all from ignoring, or looking outside the fact that we have this emotional connection. It is mine, and even if she has one with other people, no matter. It doesn't even register that somenoe else is her friend, or she's talknig, for the emotional connection is all I see.

You don't check out of it. So seeing people laughing is appealling but also not of interest to me. I want life to get on, and us be on it. That is paramount, in value and fruitfullness. But emotion, or connection, is that thing, where were being ourself, as so calm and mightily upright, that we imbue what is deep about itslef, and how we take a liking to others. I just have no interest in sitting around, talking, laughing about. This never amused me with our friends in school, nor does it in work. We hold ourself, and keep our personal relationships with us, as life steadily flows. We broke such relation with Bella, and I see this now. Even a month or two after, when Carry mentioned something, or Tara even, saying you never know what might happen, that we grew excitement and more or less anticipation. Yet, these were folly. Indeed, without duty you may think about things to do, but were adults, we make friends, learn of one another, and appreciate our relationship for what it is, rather than somehtng which in our lack or slowness we seek. And if comparability or reason guide us, so may we spend time together. Had we the confidence and calm, we'd ask Simron to go to a movie. For it was just that, something to do, that I'd like to. Reason never stated that with Bella. At least, I did not really want to go, if only for our emotional want beyond this. We'd not want to go to her baseball game, but would feel fine doing so. But this is an absent refelction, as though we were parched and she were water.
Bit by bit our strenght returns, and we grow sense of our past tidings; what seems good, bad, preferred or not; and by that, what is a token of appreciation, but otherwise worth no grip nor misgivings.
 I see inside of me a man who's made a choice, or at least through stubborness and strenght, bent himself to actions and paths that have provided stability and cheer.
 Such ways, or leanings, have made him no friends though. And for an era, or period at least, when this seemed less preferable nor needed, we thought that the issue was one of understanding, and how simply we could impart ourselves onto other people. Familiarity became a relevant term, as differences occur within all of us, but however latched, familiarity softens edges and bears a bond. Some warmth at least. In part this is all true.. But what I see, almost determinately, is that we really don't knnow ourself, and by some accounts, loose ourselves in the vapid possibility of things; yet such inklings oft come when we are but a haze. Not weak neccessariyl, but lacking any substance or form. For you cannot just succeed, nor do people just like you. And we often have but a mirrored complexion, or a wofcting one, rather than behaved or produced; and we invite thoughts and whims into our mind that fit that former kind of being, wherein standard and reason are thinner or absent.
 I look back at the great moments of development, the insights that bore further reflections, 'as if an organizing of some newly discovered stream'. Christmas comes to mind, or the accpetence of Holly; that of work even and our amiability to it. The mere permission to live (not) outside. In all of these time has gone on. And I think were a bit too hard, and by that currently untuned nor forgiving, of the feelings and pressures around at those moments. In the case of christmas it was deemed that this ardent life of self-regard and industry was too much and uneccessary. But this was not entirely true. The spring that followed showed that. It was moresoe our view of things and how certain elements weighed on me. Our writing had to not only reach but preach the stars. As did our industry have to create success and fame, or at least try. Our natural motion had a hard time making way, as theyre were these expecations, from me and others seemingly. Indeed, it was nice to try; but we merely learned. No different than now, where I see that in the tracks of life we have been a certain way, and speaking this way or behaving like that has garnered friends. Further has our self-centered and void view been reinforced as folly. But no great despair is needed. You need merely continue on. Our truest self is a good one, a grand one. It doesn't hurt to have some sense of the day. For it would be nice if you could see something new, be it some thing to do on the weekend, or some game or show coming out. These things add variety and spice to your life.
 But without that even life is always changing, tilting towards the summer, or away and to the fall. And our life even, coming from or towards thing, having some sort of state or manner which on the good or bad end, is deepening or exiting.
 The point though is that despite this novel and or expected change, 'from bloom to doom', so consistency lay. We wake up in the morning, respect the days when this will be early and to work. We walk on days off before anything, and after work on such days. We find it poor to reach our days end and not go for a walk. Why should we be so tired and dreary into sleep? Sleep won't be as well in any case. And carved between is a general mode to the day, where breakfast, lunch and dinner are had. As are there times for leisure and walking, rest and play. That moment following bananas or salad is not exactly our busiest time. And indeed, it does not always please me to sleep or lay down, watching something which is perhaps unexciting. But such is the norm, and indeed, seeing more, novel or not, blends this quieter moment into whats come or is coming.
 On that note, the time of day influences us alot. For if it were winter then the last light would be in the afternoon. Or as spring comes along this blossoms into the evening. But summer sees the light last till what is normally night, and we are ready for bed. This brings with it a sort of scenario, whereby we may wander about in the finality of our day. On off days this can invite a little time afterwards, whereby we may eat. Which is fine, but perhaps we remark upno the lightness of such food. Take last night. Truly wonderful, but we were home at 930. Some bread was fine along with a salad. But we were up past 11. And this is not so poor, but we might take into account the sun setting into 9. We truly ought have our dinner before hand. As we may account for popcorn or potatoes following; yet doing so going into 10 is quite late.
 Its just summers nature; no different than the oddity of winter's short days. But we ought be privy to the rythm of a good day, and respect the matters around us. For I like an evening ride, or one of light. And indeed, this amounts to that late afternoon, where warmth has returned upon the suns angle, yet there is still volumes of light in the sky. As the sun further dips into the evening vibrance seeps in, as the sun is more direct. This is truly an evening ride. Afternoon ought not be batched together with noon, for this is the meekest of times, as the sun being so overhead reduces the color and contrast.
 So, given its a work night, we may go for a merry ride, near the brewery. But this is going to be around 9. And it would seem that all lights are out at that point. We may read, and or write. But it's best time we go for a walk and return home to bed, or quiet down at least. That being so, we ought have all our food before hand. One useful note is that of the relatively settled form of your midday, regarding food, and the natural resting point, whereby we settle, and perhaps into the beginnings of grain. The beginning of the day is a complicated point, but it is clear that once the morning is done, and training has ceased, and 3 walks usually otherwise, that we have our orange, play, and cocner ourselves little with moving further. That harsh condition of eating something prior to a 2nd walk is a clear instance of how even 2 walks comes short. What were trying to avoid there becomes quite satiable following that 3rd walk and orange. Indeed it depends on what you want to do, but it is clear that smoothies and salads are the following period. And indeed, it seems like our blend of starches and grain come following. Today for instance, we have 6 servings of grain. This is not a huge amount, more like a split between one mass serving. But surely leading into days end we'll have room for some bread. And indeed, I feel not for a walk right now, as it's hot, I've walked already, and were pretty tired. Not too rested. So I might just split my grain, go for a walk in the evening, than play, recover, write a bit, further our Age, and have some bread. Maybe we'll go for a nice late evening walk or stroll. Likely a walk going into the evening.
 Such is our days. And I reconcile our grief and doubt with the fact that all things far and ill mannered are not to be officiated away, as though some intrusion. The reality is were not moving. But, in the past, such posture saw such whims as neccessary, as though our composition would always be a little uneven. We are so well though that we don't even need these things; that, and were aware of there ointment-like nature. I find it somewhat disturbing to be so callous and complacent as to dream of someone or something, take pleasure in the idea yet expect not, or have any reasonable sense to, yet, in a better state, such dreams are actually a source of despair, for were more aware of theyre folly. A truly warming and enticing thought is one of socializing; but in and where I see myself fitting in, where it is easy, worth looking forward to; where I may connect and be happy. Such brings order and heat to our day, and similar to work, irons out the mallodies of stiffness and past development. This latter is the tricky thing, for porn and food often stand as such remedies. But I look at more filling things, yet are afar, or just are poorly concieved. Suggeetions of 'you could just do it Ryan', are quite unwelcomed; for you don't understand. And that is it you see, the dialectic of a moral heart. But in standing to this, in as much as I have experienced and otherwise rememeber, 'to keep our infidelities from pulling us away', that so am I subject to the flame of a truly unordered and wandering mind. For I don't hanker down on something as to relieve me of our errors. I am steadfast and stout, seldom anything short of even small movement. But the reach of it, the actual force in my stride, may fall short, and allow for all manners of impression and remedy. Yet I hold to our heart, still drenched in the green of it's way. Yet things around me seem so pleasing, but were in some sense the least able. For we barely admitt nor reckon were without motion. For when we do, all is fine; and some manner of understanding illuminates how the nature of those wants are best served and famed by some other manner; commisery if you will, in your rich and moral heart.
I've a mountain to say. Yet, if I respect the humour in my heart, then little is ready.
 The time has brought me much, but much has gone on. And it seldom harms one to remember this. We moved to Vancouver as a sort of final beginning. 'No more' I felt, sharing my current attitudes, whereby duty was paramount: the rule of life if you will. And we were to abide it. Similar to when we grew some acceptance following Holly, but then moved home, that in Vancouver we abided our resolve, but used our means and character to middling results. The coarse was fine, but there were infidelities in our step. Truly, and I mean this, that we ironed this out, and shaped ourself into a little stream of prosperity. The feeling that aries is that early November sunrise, coming up as we went to work; how fresh and the cool the air was, but our time was fine. I thought for a moment, 'man, it is so nice and calming, I'd love to just go'. But our path drew me, in both attention and grace. "We obliged out of respect, and took refuge and sight in the principal and succour that'd follow. Such warmed and drew me down this path." But circumstance blew me away. Eager were we, or willing rather, but alas.
 One notion that has come to mind is this irreconcilable yet immutable factor of firmness, as came about during our early youth. It seems that an aim was never what I had, and through grade 5 we merely kept alnog, having no sense nor burden to take notice -in however moderate our success was. And so friends came a calling and we anwswered, enamured, or at least warmed to the motion. And I often ask myself, 'had we of stayed, and been in Mr.Patricks class, what'd we do? Would we study? Would our moderate efforts suffice, while we enjoy the warmth of others but lean in with them not. Or would we fall prey, or at least become further humoured, to a negligent and or rampacious degree." I think of DC shoes and how important they were to me. Something felt missing without them, as though we were merely fine with the shoes we had. What factor or condition we were tending to is unclear; but I do know that when I got them I felt so confident. The effect wore off though, to a measley degree. My point, is that this factor may have it's own incidence as regards friends. The ludicrous talk of people doing cocaine was alarming to me a year or so after we graduated. But that line, from shoes to friends to cars and girls; all this required, all this held little care for otherwise. The idea that you may just do both and flourish is not for a man like me. For in that, we are no so well as to succeed in careers and fun. We behold nothing but ourselves. In this though, we may become enamured, or at least unhestiantly drawn to poor things, or lack, as our later youth found.
 All of that is to say, is that from this point on, where time did not have that natural development to either compell or test me, that we moved somewhere new, and upon that, became more or less pressured into some surer form of being. In our prior case we could have been modest; risking deliquince for sure. But we were part of something pleasing, and had good standards till that point. "As life went, I'm sure it would have gone." But upon our move we were not in such a place, and had to then work our way in. Which is not how our prior time came to be. It was from natural circumstance. And our overall manner and strenght lead me into the fray of people, while being myself. If theyre were a group of us, some part would be mingled yet unlinked, while some other part would be boding about, getting into shoving matches or doing something stupid together. They'd be apart from the other part of the group, who I'd be with. Yet of me there was I. We were not mingled, merely wtih. As though there were natural pairs in that mingle, while I was a crowd of my own. There was always someone special: Jasmine, Colin, Matt. I wish Tristan were still here. In any case, we did not mingle upno our move, nor had natural inclination to goof off and ruckus around. I remained I. But this did not create much integration. In our first year we actually fit in well, with Jesse, Kendra, Talayna and akimi,Danielle, Colin and Seb. It was only in grade 7 that I did not find too many I liked. On reason was our class was a split. And besides Scott and Nick, I did not have any real liking with any. In part I was a way that remarked how I'd often be, in that, of the yougner bucks, namely Erik, Josh and Alex, they were theyre own minglings, and center of things; yet I was our own, and in some sense acted a crowed amidst theyre own. It was not like this was people our age. But in theyre case, it was as though the discrepency was more noticed; and a sense, or at least leaning of hostility or un-interest ensued. This reflected our view of Christina and her friends, and the guys around them; varied for sure, from Quick, Gresham, foster, but Sang also. Really didn't care for them. And I found myself, quite literally, on a field trip at Cultas, sitting by myself in the pool. It's one of those odd things, for you'd think I'm just a shy kid with little to say. Yet I'm a man in many ways, unbroke, but alone. We did not click with everybody; we were not theyre friends. And our friendship with Colin and Seb became a little muted due to not being in the same class. I stood though, however alone. And in fact found no shame in liking other people who seemed more genuine and fufilling to me. So called dorks. I recall some odd new years party at fosters, where Colin had come back, doing some coke I believe, or was drunk at least, and he made this loopy appeal to me, to apolagize. It was drunken, and was not this literal thing we needed to mends. But by my count he came back, as though I'd been sitting upright and well, and in all his galavanting and passing remarks, or disregard, that to me, more kind and respectable, decent rather, he came.
 I've just been in this defending phase since then. And indeed, when time brought us something new, which in all honesty was treated with initial aversion, so we got our selves in trouble. For we did not have an aim. That is the weirdest thing. That all of this comes down to how you see and meet with people. The rule in life was obviously imposed, but on that count known to me. And indeed, a broad sense of the good as it sprouted from this laid in me as something worthwhile and true. We felt fair in gleaming such thing and abiding, or at any rate trying. Of honor it seemed. But we could be pulled off the path. Merely being good was a hard thing to do. As we did not have this high mind for achievment, nor some end of university. It was as casual as saying 'one day you'll have a family'. And this is perhaps how alot of us live, some of the time at least. We just do what were suppose to. I just lacked respect or aspiration for the people around me upon our move. I had no qualms prior, and rememebr them fondly. But EME became increasingly vain in my eyes. And so we went to some further school, away as it were.
 There became in me a smallness, a sort of form that we still resemble this day. Truly awful this is, less the world is only your own mind. That is, the general burden of our way became so, that a suitable response was not done in mere passivity. We were indeed passive, but, in our smallness, we used all our capacity to get so merely by. And as a result, we did not excell, at anything. Our natural talents became washed out due to the physical and or applied shortcomings --from doing nothing of the sort. And as the years went on, this manner of living came face to face with the consquence of all these efforts, that we'd go to univseristy. We might compared the potential Mr.Patricks class with that of our potential school. For we grew acquainted with people, and had more satisfaction in our passivity, but perhaps took for granted what such things took; or better yet, given what we had given, what that gave us privalge to do. And error occured, as it often does. The effect, was that through a tumultuous and depressing finally to our secondary year, we did not in fact go to college. No aim materialized to do so. Even when one did, out of the rubble of 2013, we took a seemingly fair and ordinary reprieve to a position that was more hospitable and warming. This did not cultivate any ambition though. Nor did the avenue for satiety satisfy me, or bear resolve. All we had were our friends, but the expense of being with them in a rewarding way was all consuming. And I slackened into distaste: which was easy given the size of the task: disliking it was easier to humour than try so much. So, for technical sake, we'll say that eating enough is not simply about totals per day, but rather, not going too long without eating. And this aspect holds with it a personally driven element. Take sugar. If you have it the night before, then you feel hungrier in the morning; sooner that is. And if you don't feed yourself when your hungry, your body feels famished. Aeorbics and insulin could be explored in these resepcts. But just in general, there are ill effects from going starving/catabolic. You break down.
 So, your aim is to keep yourself from starving. You tend to keep weight on and grow stronger. On one hand you have the sense of this, whereby you ought eat when your hungry. Too many times have we failed to meet this. And there is the element of your bodily condition, whereby hunger ensues; but so in these latter years have we begun to famish ourselves more. On principle perhaps, or of ability rather. But this has lead to weight and strenght loss. Oddly, when your famished, you find yourself even moreso. At least, you don't tolerate being so famished, and the effect feels even worse.
 The key element is that upon famishment and thus loss, you find it harder to train and be, and thereby afford more stability in your metabolism. Moreover, it is actually harder to eat. And practically this has driven us away from eating enough.

 Such is an experience, and upon reflection thought, I often have.
 The most notable instance is a time when I was reading some book on materialism, and it felt so lovely and nice. I was in the backyard in Kamloops, evening of summer, and this feeling arose. But then, per the quote, I tried to organize that thought; at least, this was akin to some sort of doubt or questioning, wondering what this feeling was, as though it ought be in some place as to be deemed well and proper. Why are we so longing for seomthing so unimportant is perhaps the motivating factor. So giving it a place makes it more suited. Yet doing so, as it were, destroys the feeling. Be it in impusle or attempt, pausing on such moment lets the air go and it begins to sink. Which causes affirmation or hesitancy, to return.
So life is a waevin, a web of motion. But in fact, is really just about that, movement. All sound philosophy and moral formation rests on this. For we are always brething, moving, about to, or in states of rest. Take a painter, who takes bright red then the darkest of blues. One is quiet, almost unremarkable, but still flows. The tamest of rivers, stillest of oceans, still have movement. Atomically even nothing is really at rest.
 And so life goes on, and the orchestra of it is what we call living. To be in motion is to live. And indeed, much of reflection comes down to understanding our characters and humours, or passion, for such things are odd motions; different than our breath, our duties, our pastimes. There the motives for these things, but the mystery also.
 And nothing is so mysterious than that of love. Everybody learns to talk to people in ways that are suited and effective. To show up, be cordial, ask questions; you learn this. And indeed, you reach a point where the only thing to say is what you want: but you learn to want the right thing.
 But love is different. For it comes when there is harmony in your motions, and your able to see, as though there's some mark. It reflects the greek term Eudamonyia, whereby it is not so much a relief you want, nor something which your familiar with, but rather in your stable motion, where the ease to see but also form to do so, bears a striking impresison upno you, a dazzle, some wonder, some awe.

Bringing our life and feelings into harmony is an odd thing. For so much has happened, from our move, to leaving Vancouver, to the years prior where wisdom had set in but not in our choosing. And before then, where work held our disdain, and before that, where despite things seeming well, we were quite bored, and, notably, indulgent.
 What I can say then is that at some point in our life we saw things a bit clearer, as girls, jobs, oppertunity, health even, were not these things so near and present, and a root of shame if you didn't just pursue them and grab them. Such things have become objects in my mind over the era. Yet, back in those days, and this was something which came to mind today, was that we had no self-pressure, no practice, nothing to hold us away from people or things; but we had nothing at all. The era that came was one where we defined ourself by the quality of experience, and more or less hoped, expected, esteemed our further time ahead as something prompt for the passions which accrued, given the personal-life nature of our duties.
 And so I sit now, down because of a girl, and similarly so about being seen, and on that count, seeing others. We feel uncertain about things, where we are, where were going; what guides me at any rate. And indeed, you think of those passions that helmed me an age ago, gave assurance at least, such things were in effect soothing distractions, as a moment of lack could look to them as things to come; and we thus moved along. On one hand you have the basic insight that such movement, 'of going along', was not stable or just; and it can be said that the inherent stability, if it were just, would have prompted the strongest of primary insights and adjustments. Easy to say given that we had not been there; and so what may have seemed futile in our ways within this lane of neccessity, could have bent us in different ways than we at the moment thought fair.
 In any case, we have more or less lived without these expectations; not so much in humility but in an embracing of our dearest goods. On one hand, things we want, as Peter Parker would say, became more open, as we felt less disposed to things who's value and esteem closed us off to such wants. As it were, these wants, which I can better describe now, are so as to rest in us oppertunely or in attraction; meaning, that the ability for something to happen was not squashed down as improbable; and things that actually do draw us are given a chance, or made towards. Indeed much our reflection and inquiry over the years, coming to pitch currently, is so as to notice the manner of our ways, and what elements and fashions are reaosnable and just, understandible at least; for we may see that some activity or person cathces our sight, and the only thing holding us back is lazyness or some other occupation; at least, we often find there's a heavyness or filled-up state to our mind, for which something new, and as is often the case, something strange and revealling, bears difficulty on our part in embracing. There's a nerve at least. And through our days, and those recent even, we've made an excuse.  Nevertheless, such things have come about, and we are in most ways more open, calm, substantive in our expectattions, and humble in as much as were not. For the good and to the better there is no question. But I am concerned that our moments which at one point had a fools padding, are throwing you off without it. For it is important, or healthy in a way, to keep on moving. It's just the case that we feel slow and dull in our tracks; and things which our more engaged mind would see, peer upon us to the effect of doubt and shame. Some of these things would trouble the Gods, in seeking the most obscure yet delightful friendship; all by the cheer and harmony in your heart, as to speak so freely yet happy. "Without wanting, nor worry, no luster and grough." Part of being a man is in both remedying the minor pitfalls upon slipping, but thereupon settling in and being merry of your actual gait, your place, your happening; for such dear things come to pass then, but through a forward acceptance. We often find ourselves grieved with what were giving up; as though passion is tugging at us not to let her go. These are the hardest of stings, akin to that disparity of feeling even the slightest bit immature. For the development of maturity is so that you bring your errors and seekings with you; and you become merely more humble and able; which brings peace and confidence.  For instance, Maurya gets +2 happiness on the altar and theyre unique buildings, and then that of the villa and arean --certainly the later. They also get it on barracks and libraries. I'll note off the bat that the step pyramid requires a intrinsic happiness yeild, while the mud hut simpyl can't be built on rought terrain. The hill fort, which is quite fantastic, requires rough terrain. The influence post has no requirment, but only 1 can be built. And it does give 2 influence during celebrations. So not too shaby. The food and gold one are not clear to me. This speaks to the balance in a non improvement/culture game, where you benefit from hill forts and diplo buildings, to the point where you may see reason to invest in the suzerainity for that purpose. It is by my count easier to put in hill forts in a city for you can build them, then it is to buy them in a town. And you wouldn't want to in the first place. Given that, you may be unsure where to put a city in your nearby lands. Where there is rough terrain there is production; and indeed, resources are easily grabbed by towns, and don't offer beneefits themselves; for they get usuable across the empire. By that count, barring unique buildings --mauryas gives culture from mountains-- you are looking for tiles that will support your production buildings, science, gold and food, and that of culture and happiness -which is ever so important. One note is the oddity of monuments and villas, which hold influence as a base yield. This is quite precious. There is experience required for me to say what future buildings will nicely fit, or can go elsewhere. But in any case, it is easy to sea that food, science and happiness can just be overbuilt. The intrinsics are not essential, so you can find thee according spots for such spaces. And the point, is that the land is most essential, in that, given fresh water, permanent resources for adj. and rough terrain, and rural space too, depending on your purpose, that so a city lies. And indeed, you can have as many cities as you want, but you must invest; and so good ones are those which you naturally wish to pursue, as a better settlmeent. The limit of such in terms of the resources required, is what maeks you quesiton whether something should be a city
 It is hard to manage your views when the changes from age transitions occur. You have less settlement limit, and most if not all the increases you get are removed. You start exploration with 8 and modern with 16. You can build El Escorial for an extra, and take corona civica; in the moderan age particular this is better, as you've likely already converted so many cities. One important note is of ideals, in say a city location, or just a worthwhile spot, and how you may progress towards contesting such thing. A independant surrounded by a bunch of reosurces warrants a take over, but maybe not right away, given the resources. Early game rewards haste, so getting less ideal settles out is preferred over a better one that will take much time. You have to weigh that fact. And at any rate, as your looking around the world, certain spots can be contested by water, be it against CS or other civs. One element to your strategy is that of alliances, or good relations at any rate. There is a triumph that gives 5 happiness per alliance; and surely those who your either a) the furthest from, or b) bordered in a facorable way, in that you would want no aggression from that side, and by that token, seek no expansion there, so is this prime for an alliance. Also, those who they'd go to war with are likely around them, and so if your on theyre flank, then besides giving up potential trades, your not in direct contact with that foe. For the sake of extra happiness, which in effect is settlement limit

It seems an important note that the settlments you put down are the same regardless of time. So if you go over your settlement limit in exploration but mitigate it with happiness, or tmeporary settle limit even, the fact that you were just getting a temporary buff is not essential, as you still have the settlements. Certain settles may be more valued based on what they provide, ie. treasure resources. But the actual use of a settle and its relation to the coming increase in settle limit, which you may artificially reach through policies in the prior age, mean nothing more than the balancing for having those settles. They are whats important, as they give you land, production, scuence, which gives you space to slot resources, make gold buildings and industries, or to make wonders, improvements and slot grea works, or to hold more dominion, and by that count, have productiv and strategic access to taking others; or to literally concentrate your yields to, gather innovation and reach the stars
 Its part of the game that it will reset twice. In doing so, you need to consider that buildings of a similar type will be built over in the following age. And some resources are less reliable, for sure in some cases, such as wool, clay, rice, dyes, most of the bonus resources in fact. Things like iron, camels, incense, most of the city resoruces stay in place --though cotton also stays. It is also important to consider that wonders often can be built as though they were distrits, and that as the ages go on your going to have more specialist slots and more happiness to justify putting multiple in. So planning settlments with this future in mind is important.
 Cs can afford production on rough tiles with hill forts, science on tiles with natural happiness, culture on flat terrain tiles, a influence boost per settlement. Consider where there is rough terrain and forests, for these will likely hold your long term improvements; and consider what you may put on them. It is not so adventagous nor neccessary to get settlement limit from the expansion or military city state. Instead, you can get extra food on your gardens and baths, which are one of the few yeields that scale with the ages, as your growth keeps going regardless. And production carries over from improvements, and hillforts give +2. You ought consider where some great city will be made, and if a military CS is available. Secondary cities are often enough to warrant this.
Consider this question: why have 17 settlements in exploration? Your just going to be over when your in modern? One factor is this. Lets say your happiness accomodates you being that far over in exploration; say your at 15 limt and have an average of 10 happiness per settle. You can afford this. The question, is when I go into modern, and the limit goes to the stock 16, will I afford that? Cause maybe I am at 20, and I could afford that in exploration. That's alot of settles mind you, and indeed, one of the triumphs gives happiness per alliance. I can't speak to the happiness availability going into modern.
 This actually raises a good point, that one of the friction points of going into exploration is that we don't know much about gonig into modenr. What we'll have, if we want to keep our religion, if were surely keeping all cities as they are. What triumphs are we going to choose, given our expansionist or tourism view. Culture for instance may work well with the Ming, as your rewarded for having so many fortifications. But you also have other elmeents, in relics, wonders, CS improvements, and celebrations. Some of these happen naturally, but perhaps were not emphasizing relics, just what we can afford to slot.
So I mean to play as Tecumseh, who benefits from CS, in providing combat to infantry and ranged, plus 2 dominion per. This does carry over to my pleasant surprise. The shawnee are a great exploration civ as they have a solid warrior who gets buffs per empire resource, and they get +2 production per tundra, desert or plains tile --I hope this works as advertised. They also get +4 production on nav rivers, which is niche but pretty nice. They get the heralded 50 boon towards CS conversion, which is quite expensive. Siam has the ability to insta convert CS, which has nice but not neccessarily needed effects. Were converting them for dominion, but for the sake of victory the immediacy is likely not too essential. The CS benefit mind you gives combat score and production, plus the little boons. We may also slot in mementos that enhance these elements. starting with Greece seems essential, or at least heavily advantageous, to get extra combat on infantry and the CS boost. Theyre Parthanon is also quite nice, with culture and base influence.
 It feels fundemental that we'd grab a villa and monument, noting theyre use in further ages. It is tricky to know where they will not be overbuilt; the altar seems inconsistent. The arena is also a boon, as it gives 4 happiness, and the garden also. Were surely going to overbuild our production and sicence buildings; I like to put barracks and library together, then overbuild them. And we may not have time for academy and ironworks.
