A prelimary email that states we found something and are looking for feedback, with some preface'd points that can station the rhetoric you'd otherwise use during the paper. I find this a far yet true promise, eager in my creative mind. The work has been well.
 And lastly, as for reading, there are in fact many essayists and writers; Thoreau may not be to my liking, but a man named Hazlitt was surely. We may add means to explore and save such pieces. Bringing Anna to the back grass has been nice, but our tablet could also do well.
For brevities sake, France is playing Paragruay, who then plays the victor of Canada and Morocco. USA plays beligum, the victor playing the winner of Portugal and Spain. The winner of this will play the winner of that prior bracket. Likely Spain vs USA, perhaps Portugal, and almost surely France.
 Brazil plays Norway, the winner of which plays the victor of Mexico and England. Argentina plays Egypt, the victor of which plays the winner of Switzerland and Colombia. Likely Argentina vs Colombia, perhaps the Swiss, and Brazil is apt to beat Norway; England and Mexico is a coinflip. Of those two teams, the victor between them and Brazil is likely to play Argentina.
 As a finale, its likely Spain or France, maybe Portugal, though I don't think they'd beat France. Mexico could beat England, and perhaps Brazil, but Argentina is likely to move forth.
What can we say, except for mixed emotions, feelings of loss; yet of regret, it's wofting away, leaving our heart and soul. But what's left is not so secure, nor certain. It's as though we are free to love, but unsure where to; and this brings back memory of pain that left us.
 In part, I am reminded of the way of things, of this perpetual motion, this constant state of flow, and that in many ways, all that is good comes from some abandonment of 'ignoring rules', and seeking and or delighting in that which comes upon things benig well. As though our troubles and oblige are forogtten. That, and ironing out the rought edges of our conception. The matters here are not what's essential, merely our form within things. Nothing is so pure, nor so special, nor are we high above, nor others below. Its this thing about our lives, lacking what we can hold onto, yet lacking also the rule which makes all things unneccesary. They just are.
Just to mould a bit of substance, one clear issue, or overestimate, is on our own view of firends; and not so much as regards other people, as thoguh we shouldn't feel so jealous based on what they have, but rather our solemness and critique, per what we feel like we should have and are missing.
 For most people talk about something. Age groups and similarities spur this. We talk with Alex about Destiny, Oliver about Soccer, Jacob about walks and the weather. But then there's just friendlines, humour and familiriarty, which ends up being about nothing. Indeed, you may say something about yourself, but often this is not of interest or available. Few really speak this way. Be it vain or not, Bella does this quite often. But I think we exagerate what this means.
 And overall, I think there is a softening, a tuning, a curisoity and foundation to living. But it comes in this proper process, where things good and bad are rightfull sighted. Often, it is those ghosts of our hearts whisper, or the call and or zeal of honor and 'rulelessness', that has me hoping for and expecting, or despairing of what's absent. This fixates our view, in shiny or drowning ways, and we loose our general appeal and enamour, and somewhat trust, as though were bored, tired, grieving, which does not invite nor produce in ourselves much warth or sociablity.
So I like the idea of beginning with the principle. The idea is essentially to present what a repeating seqeunce is via the mechanism of clocks, or the reoccurence rule, then to show that this effect occurs in volumes, and within families.
 The idea of the fibinocci sequence is perhaps not formulaic, as it is literal, in that you start adding 1,1,2,3,5. The idea though of starting with those terms and adding subsequently is what needs clarification. It is hard to speak of 'add two starting terms, then the two foremost terms'. This idea is not so simply defined. 'Akin' to the fibinocci feels right but this whole aspect needs to be more straightforward.
 Comparing a cardinal/ordinary line with a reoccuring one seems useful, as it speaks to the clock like nature. The notion of a binary line, whereby the values are always 1 or 0, yet the 10th term may be so, per the index, but at any rate be of 0 or 1. Clarifying the objective value of 0 or 1 with the position is to our aid. Speaking of this clock like mechanism is the token to further demonstration. It needs to be clear and concise, and need as little elaboration as possible. One element that brings us further is the idea of linking the purpose of a point to its explanation/cause. If were speaking of adding on a clock, rather than outline what that clock is, use a method of clarity per that clock so much as a further point (which the clock serves) to almost complete the point of the clock at all.
 In esscence, were adding terms in sequence, as though going around a clock. I feel the idea is clear enough that a standard 12 hour clock need not be used. Though, this seems to be so that were holding off on the elaboration of ranges of clocks, and the letter system for double digit. Given that we are not introducing the assumed operations to begin, we can literally use whole terms, and perhaps use a 12 hour clock. The principle is no different.
 One element which I still struggle with, as though the aim of this whole process is unclear, that we still feel like we have to prove the principle before assuming that the volume of findings can be shown.
 One way to do it, is so far and simple as the principle is to show, that we could make a literal claim, that of such principle demosntrated, where it extends to, and that for demonstration purposes of that, we may instill our reasoning, nomenclature and notation. For at that point you are truly saying, 'this thing I just showed you, there is much more, but I need to present it in this way, and use these terms to refer to various areas/domains'.
 For it may be said, that of a starting state, whereby initial groupings of terms are added subsequently [and of this foremost sort], that doing so as though on a clock will create a point of repition, whereby the initial state is returned to. Within each clock, or rule of reoccurence, and within pairings of terms, ie. doubles, triples etc. that within each group the point of repition is the same. We call the range of clock a class and the lenght of pairing order. So within class nine 2nd order (doubles), every variation of starting states will repeat at the same point as others in the group.
There are things in our life which may drag us down, like loose sails or a rustry pipe. But the abscence of these does not suggest where we should sail. By all counts, having such things motivates us to do ceratin things. Whereas lacking problems creates a pace of peace, one where you forsee no trouble or plight, and thus move through life unhindered nor reserved. We don't say no, but not often are we asked. This is the nature of things. One's place in life can create oppertunity and friendship; but growing up is in part tough, for you are becoming yourself. And circumstance may bring you away from materialziing that. And indeed, whatever friendship or oopertunity you lack, so you know yourself, are bold, rich in candor and trust. Life brings us back to steady motionns, and in that, we find our stride, donig as we want, aware of what brings us to what we please; and indeed, instability from the nature of growth throws us sometimes, to and fro, and part of growing is in adjusting to this, finding yourself more sure and set, 'able to be yoruself in that real way'. The world you see, the sight of your eyes, the fanciful view that toys at you, these are all able to be checked and remarked upon, whereby perspective marbles your gait with circumpsection and probability. Steadyness is the awareness of these things mixed with no grip, for you are doing as you please now. The matter of love is not something which comes from feeling lack but rather an urge towards. But this feeling is often born from our most base and formless self; and we often loose who we are, and forgo the bounds which that can afford. It is about me after all, not what other lack, 'so that you may better in not having more'.
I have wants sometimes, feelings, lust, and they overcome me, move me. And indeed, this is not istslef something of great importance, as your not really in this state all the time. Whats worth noting is that we may feel despair at missing whatever provides our desire; yet we pay too little resepct, nor have a realistic sense, or generous one, of what such thing would be. Your wish for sex cannot encapsulate your view of somebody. And indeed, you can still like the rest of them, but is there any part of that actually does? What are you doing that you like which relates to them? I think of being creative, and how someone else who is creative is great to share. I like that person. I like that I can share my love of the sun with Matin, or Guild Wars with Andy, or RE with Alex. And you have these little connections with people.
 I just think there is a lack of positivity in regards to your actual like, and the construct of your life as remarks this. For feeling ought not guide me, as it speaks to what is either unaccessible or uncommisery to dearer goods. Were not so absent as to have forgone the strenght which propiety affords, and in that the ease of duty and felicity of leisure. Those are our fruits and we cherrish them highly. I think in part we've come from times which felt somewhat unheaded nor clear, and the time when we'd return to work was one that saw me bracing the deflation of our goods, but thereby not being so open; and much glory and or infamy ensued. It is true that when we were in Mariner that we had our own bracing effect; the difference though was that we could sink into the nature of oru way, in it being fair and fundmenetal, and thereby not poor to respect and commiserate to. Consistency felt easier, and thereby we became more fruitful; as though we were pleased and trusting our heading. The manner which we try and force upon our bracing state, within a temporary state mind you, is what in fact begins to rise and fashion when you let things be, for things of real substance take shape. And it is a broader point that all things tend to collect with one another, and the peace and pleasure of work deepens, along with our free time. And from here, the updrafts that create that substance and fashioning have both an increased source and spring, but also 'weezer' which roars the flames. "Such occurs when the labor of work is felt less, and your liberty in it is bound true." And one fair result of this is the abscence of preperation and trepdiation. You merely be, questioning not that you can be kind and merry to people; and within that you feel not that you are unwelcome. Littlte bits and bats come up, particularly within the eventual slow moments of the day. But like all things what surrounds and alights comes through.
 These are the words that mean something to me. Not worrying of Bella, as if that was about anything. Perhaps we were flawed before, perhaps we coudl have been friends. I recall starkly that our truest peace was in that we no longer cared. It was only in our inability to be steady, but not otherwise still, that we lept forth; and from the resolution which our wounds bore, that upon a promising spark our inhabition did not trigger. And indeed, much foundations of thought came to pass, 'as though theyre seemingly high merrits were in part wrapped in flawed or eager emotions'.
 And so I sit here with broad circumspect, so bountiful in our life that I can speak to Seneca or Emerson with great respect, and of that, feel theyre warmth. Very high esteemed of me. But I really mean to say that we have a geniality to us, a tenderness which is not so bold nor so quaint, nor squishy and of that imalleable to the cracks of the past or hope of the future. Our views and proclivities are forming, to be more solid rather than over-thought or anticipated. The world as I see it, of Ridge and Vancouver, people at work and the very job itself, to our leisure and custom around, it is like a platform, where the nature of the future is not so far off, but instead joins with the present and past, as to make a more complete unit: affording nothing more than a steady sense of movement, rather than reaching. Were merely being, good right now, blossoming in our cares. It is so nice to be writing of sums, and remarking upon our work is itself a fair delight, for it all feels true. Indeed the aim is flimsy, for the part of confidence I need is too mingled with the fair side of promise; where nothing entirely makes sense. In part it is because I feel barely able to make a solid dedication, as much of what actually brings me to such does so with motives of a more firery and esteemed sort.
Our emtions come from things. A test brings stress per our feeling of it; but it is moreso our view of it, our understanding, the stake and our grasp on the matter; and this brings disease.
 And what I found, and often forget, is that the greatest of things, the fairest of experiences, comes from a relatively solid and bright position, whereby your mind is embellished from things that make it well.
 I find that our thoughts often lead us to realize how well things are, what there is, what we like and care for. So we start with more or less with an initial plea, that given a starting state, of two terms, and added couply in subsequence, that if we do so upon a reoccuring line, compared to say a cardinal one, that the starting state will return. The point can be made that this claim is not so absolute; but the starting states that don't apply have not yet been discovered; or are generally of volumes beyond sensibility.
 Given this, what we can do is alter the range of the line, 'adjusting the clock so to speak', and within any such range, change the extent of the starting state, and thereby degree to which it is added; ie. with two starting terms we added couply, or thirdly if there are 3. On top of that, per the range of line and degree of starting terms, we have the variation/combination of such terms. And within all of that, we recognize not only that at least up to class 20 and order 5 that every variation of starting state will repeat, but that, for each combination within an order, in a certain class, that each given starting state will repeat at the same point as all others.
 In reflection, what I find intriguing about all of this, is that to say everything succinctly requires that you say more than little. It may be vanity, or trepidation, but saying more feels safe, as you feel convincing. But the reality is, that we want to show how a starting state repeats using the reoccurence principle, how to classify the variation of these elemnents: class being the range of line, order being the extent of starting terms, and sequence/combination marking the variations of such states, or a class and it's orders. We then want to show the equinimity of repition, whereby all states within each order of a given class, will repeat at the same point as all others in such group.
 The idea that we are taking some couple or trio etc. of terms, and per that extent summing or adding that many --meaning foremost, and thereby progressing with the new addendum-- is it's own wording that could use shorthand. As well, understanding that triple and couples of class 9 repeat equally; but that this means that the couples of class 9 repeat equally while the trios have theyre own point of equality. This is in fact the distinction, or thing needing shorthand. The trios of class 8 don't overlap very meaningfully

It is the rising efforts that fair the most difficulty, as they are not defined nor concrete, nor easy to come by without an aid to such definition. What I find though is that life, when lived, flows naturally, and takes to the simple offerings of this sort. Saying that there is some form or manner in which such aids be brought by is near exhaustive, and not so neccessary. It is similar to practice, where in that case, we speak of bar work for instance, and how it is important and useful to do, as is core and running, but that the gains we need, in vain even, are achieved through a per week frequency, and not much more. I've instilled, or just recently established a yoga practice, in hips (for hamstrings and hip flexors), yin (often had leading into our work week), a flow session to emphasize downward dog, and warrior, to bring ease to our lunging. Prana is also being considered. The point of these practices is to instill and cultivate a prescence and standard of such movmenets; no different than the strenght offered from our training practice. This yoga practice is not suspect on it's own, but its accomplice of rising efforts, or minor ones we'll say that reflect less of a regiment, but rather a ordering, or better put funneling (via an aid) of our want and whim, 'as to move as we please or feel need to'.
It is interesting, and nice, that as we think about 'having something say', as though, were we not to, that it'd be because we were sleepy, or just too stricken to put out our thoughts, 'that they were all clumped in', that so when we do have thoughts and they come out free and smoothly, that so is it the same for interests, wonder, excitement, pleasure and peace, sense and security, confidence and comfort.
 In general, I see that the practice is there to instill and maintain our condition, and to serve as a reminder but also mark ahead. But this cannot be all, for we often have want of doing something, or, in tandum sometimes, with a feeling of need, as upon returning from work, and today for instance, we just did Chill, and it was nice; but we may then feel we need to treat our legs. And these aren't harsh efforts, nor much confusing. Theyre also not a practice, or something you have to plan or look to. It is like food, in that you know the pieces and slots to place things; our general view is such. And there may be neccessary matters, per a practice or training, or something clear point where this or that food is needed. But we may just look forward to doing chill. Active matters may garner less clarity in preperation, 'outside of practice', but we may still do it, if only when a moment to concieve effort and rise comes about. Such is the point of an aid, that it affords ease to that volition, and gives structure to it, so it is beyond a moment, but more akin to a sequence. The breathe most dearly benefits from this.
 And the points in which I need things are quite vaired, and although unknown in theyre limits of possibility, so are certain ones clear. Coming home from training, we often see need to tend to our shoulders and neck, and allow our body to rest, in the hips notably. A great point is that following work we often find need to tend to our legs; we may just want rest, 'for which Chill is nice', but we may also want a twist, and rub our feet. The point though, is that this is something we often seek following training. Less crucial it seems, but something between want and need: nice. And so what satiates our need following work may also welcome itself following our slightly different want upon training. And all things work like this. But we ought prioritize what those certain moments need. For we may use the morning sessions in the evening; but they should be formed for what the morning seeks. And indeed it is often not much. Per the aid, it is far more to do say a twist or a brief transition of morning seated, then to do this on your own. The aid brings focus, deeper breathe, plus a sense of clarity and comfortness: as though your actually doing something.
It must be girls, who strike my mind with so much fancy. Who else brings grievance? Do you really pitter over the ruckus and bantering of Mo and Paul? Do you feel lesser? Perhaps it is a perception, or sense, that if girls are invovled, that such thing is more value'd. I don't believe in any case that anyone has such a feeling or view.
What I'd remark upon food is that it is quite varied in what it can offer, and by all counts, is not the limiting factor. Indeed, such factor surrounds our fatigue; and so much as we are short of respiration, so does our diet need to change. For aerobic capacity allows us to make use of slow-absorbed energy, while being fatigued benefits from that which absorbs faster. The options are not vast for each. Potatoes are quite starchy, and indeed trouble us in theyre wholeness when fried. Boiling may better do, when strucutre is important. Bread similarly has this softening effect, yet is sometimes what we need. And it may be that we need whole bread, as in blue silver hills, or bread that is less fiberery, such as buns. Wheaty bread, such as that whole wheat from langley market, or the itlian soft bread foremost, is filling to a rather sullen degree. Quite unideal for any kind of rigor.
 In any case, it is clear, though sometimes put off by what happens to or needs to come prior, that leading into that days end, out of 8 usuallly, is prime for some collective of grain. Namely, split peas are soft and pair great with barely, and quinoa remains a delight. Earlier in the day we benefit, from a nourishment standpoint, of lentils and edemame plus corn. The practical effect of this is not so damning either, and indeed, when I think of the movement we should do prior to this, it is so that we are able sit more easily, and at any rate breathe more vibrantly during our digestion.
A root instance, or center if you will, to our thoughts, seems apt.
 Simply, if we have the view, and the kind of sense and regard, that people around me are there to be impressed by me and take to me (sexually or in infatuation), than we surely are coming from our own heavy self-perspective, as though all that there was was what sat around me, while we were the primary center. "As though the world were dark, and the only thing visible were from the light of me." Whereas, if we are moved and kept by a sort of place amongst all people, where we are not so heavy in our selves, but more open, giving, amicable, and from that, parsimonious and flowing with each and all, than our hold is not so seeking nor possessing. And one conflict that arises when theyre is debate over the two, is if we tend to the latter, then we feel as though we are giving up what we hope to possess by the former; moreover, we feel in that case that what we seek is somewhat owed to us, or natural to have, and thereby we feel envious thoughts of those who may possess them, and we feel pithy at our lack of trying. Further, we feel this sense of scrutiny and shame over ourselves, as though we were giving up this more challenging route for one more broad and gentle. "Why give up on the pursuit."
Nothing really matters more than the reign of our life, its view, our past, the path of it and how its come about and moves further. All can be explained by this, and much of our uncertainty seeps from it.
 One notion though is that the effect of such path, in the present, is that we feel exposed to certain truths no longer worth living by. That, or we see aspects of us which are unformed, and not taken at heart like other things. Vice seems to have influence over these elements, 'as if they are more persuadable'.
 The whole of my life, though a little obscure, can be described by a stature, a strenght, a kindness and cheer, but a seperation, distance, uninvovlement with things; and in this, many qualities of of such state came to be, in cynicism, aversion, a bit of selfishness, and high esteem. We found some soverignty in this when life became untenuable, and from there, we've been more or less happy, but relatively alone. And it was not because our inability to be social, but that we did not like many people. And one senitment that feels true, is that we felt quite detached and different from the whole of people, that those who we did like were not garnished as friends. We held an esteem and anticipation as remarked the whole, but were not calm and definite enough to merrily be, and in that, form more particular connection. We have and we did, but none of it every felt deep. The issue really, is that much of our confidence and expression came from our center, which was quite formatted as to be personally austere, but in that, outwardly esteemed. I found it easy to connect but not really to bond; or perhaps it was the other way around. The point, is that I felt that there was always part of me, the heart at least, which was hidden; which lead to a certain feeling of discomfort, and consequent to that, a lingering pressure that eventually moved me to somewhere new and less weighing.
 This choice though, or these choices, to remain untenured, lead to subsquent moments of similar standing; where connection would form but would not take. And all I can say, is that what has changed in the later part of the age is our fixing of principle and way, especially in the world of things. Our views of nature and god, government and war, health and liberty, money, and soon woman, came about. And what occured, is that we have found ourself ready in ourself, and not perturbed by the differences of others, in theyre contrary enthusiasms as mine. People expell what is welcomed to them; and how we like to expell ourselves, naturally binds. That, or theyre is humbleness and courtesy, general community too I find. And this is where all lives and swells, as you feel sure and free in yourself, to bond yourself with more people and in a meaningfull way; and of those more casual, it is not upon our exhaultion or confidence, but more fair and relaxed emotions and sociability. We are young in this, for we are so personally formed that surpassing the natural firmness (that contradicts the intertia born of solitude), that simply time has not gone by where this was so. An age it's been of being ourselves, but only to me. And gradually things do change, but again, nothing has ever stuck. Now I feel in a far reaching flow; one which is home to things which expell all feelings of loss of wanting, 'for some place other'. But we also feel in tune with oppertunities and care of substance, and general fortune. This is the novel swells of lifes natural up and down; but we are merely reminded, 'as though someone wise were in fact king, and we drew some pleasure by the grace and constance of having such crown.'
So Nature is a sweet and cozy address. Not too long. Similar to English traits, in that it is meant to be read bit by bit. Each part not being too long. And there's just new things to find here, more thoughts, embers of ideas.
 The American Scholar has always been a favorite of mine, but is not what I'd like to focus on. Some of the addresses are quite long, and I recall some of them not hitting me as I'd like. The Young American and Conservative feel like pieces that could offer us something. And for each, it could have just been the day when we read it. Theyre all quite well, and fairly different the more specialized essays. Theyre broader speakings, and thus hold more room for impression.
 The first of Essays is Self Reliance; which may be all to rewarding and consuming on it's own, but is worthy no less. When I read this before 'compensation' stuck out to me, as we were quite idle and looking for words that elevated our solitude. But the one of Love, albeit suspect of far reaching sentiment, may hold a branch or two of insight and inspiration; friendship even moreso. "I'd be happier if the latter showed me what we lack and what things could be than of the former. I don't know myself, or accept things so gratefully, enough to feel as open as love needs. Yet bits of it squirt out, and run on swirving and tired grounds: and the knot never takes." Prudence is an interesting one. Not something I feel the need for, but of interest on the face of it. Circles, Intellect and Art feel both relevant and potential for inspiration. As the idea of enthusiasm feels like this near yet unmeasured aspect, which could run quite complimentary to more personal acquintence. "OFt it is the mystery or obscurity of things which draws negative feeling, not so much what you actually do or do not have. Its the uncertainty of whether that is just." Intellect may align with our calmer and reasonable views. We mentioned that there is always a step ahead, new qualities to give light to, a way to see things and a form to have that breathes stronger, stands higher, all from an point of greater competence and ease. But so of our intellect, as regards more novel or basic pursuits, so may this bring out our mind, and afford a blend of umph and simplicitiy. Then art, which may tie all things together, combines the aspect of fufillment and expenditure, and thereby station in life and your manner of amends.
Theres this thing about pleasure, that despite not being so poor in some things, is in itself not worth much esteem. For it is not equal to 'what we like, or want to do'. At least that latter part is quite seperate.
 Pleasure seems to be in something you have, or consume, or dream about. It comes from our loins, our seeking heart, laughter to. And indeed pleasure is found around, but it is often hard to acquire. At least I find myself seeing things which would please me. And the perspective on this is hard to rightfully avow. For we may say, 'all pleasure is bad, our desire is off'. Or, 'these are amongst those pleasures deeemd worhty, yet we cannot obtain them. For we are either ill-equiped, under-develooped, subject to chance, or unable to spend the time and resources to do so. That, or given the nature of that pleasure, there is much around it which I am either averse to or uninterested in.'
 One of the troubles I've had in our adult life, is that we still live by our own, rule and stead that is, but also in experience and delight. It may just be age, as older people aren't often any different, and I find it easy to connect with them on theyre own occupied level. But it is yougner folk who have more enthusiasm and playfullness; within work this seems like a desired quality, but just in life to. Yet it is revealled to me that your just a bit too drawn to the gleam of it, per the pleasure, and similar to porn, or seeing someone beautiful, with someone else, there is one ember that sparks part of you that has a hard time keeping things un blazed. And as the fire reeps, you engorge that one aspect, a bit naieve and unfamiliar that theyre is so much more. For indeed, my life is not burdened by pleasure it lacks, but by pleasure we see and long for. We are well fed, but upon a smell find ourself starving.
It is a simple fact, when even the lightest intent is on my mind, or at least tamber if you will, 'as though every wisp of wind would pluck our tender string', that so we see all that is in front of me, and innate to this, are the things we ought to, which we have, namely in eating through the day, moving as to facilitate movement, and indeed, borders of regards, in when we sleep, 'be it on an off day or not', and likewise if we mean to game, go for a ride, get something done, like training. And what I find is that nothing is really sought from me when were in this tune. Much of the pleasure which we reach for, or feel somber about not having, enters someone elses mind, but not my own. Much of its ticket is to one who has nothing to do. And indeed, I feel that way sometime; but memory is a guiding star hear, as there is something to do, whether we know it, and so being swayed to do what is ill or uneccessary because your out of tune right now, is not so welcomed. Surely the string looses its flourish during the day; and part of learning is in fairing insight as to what a) you can do in such moment, b) what can strenghten the string as not to become flat, and C) what is neccessary, essential, principle to begin with, so that if we are flat, we at least know what to play, and may use our whit and whim, 'our humour and hue', to move towards something known and near. When were off though and unsure, or unchecked in our mind, than even the farthest away thing feels close, 'as one without breathe would see air on another planet as pulpable'.
One of the odder notions in life is that of oppertunity. For it comes with certainty as a child, as though we have no need to consider the reality of things, and can just dream as our trajectory permitts. But as an adult you find that certain things are not so accessible, and if they are, it does not excatly jive with other essential things, or preferred ones.
 Indeed, nothing is harder to describe than the balance one can have, in theyre grand but also personal duties, and how when blended whole, leave one feeling as though everything is dealt with, yet they have no work at all. It is a smooth life, one with pace, and indeed much comes about, in little relishes here, little efforts there.
 And I'd say that this life can be fruitful, but it is not contigent on it. It is parismonious, progressive, natural, and merely growing, as a tree does with sap, 'whereby it hardens, forming a wider shell'. And it feels that the basis for your stability, or smoothenss rather, determines wherher you really are free in your process. For if not, and your like a child who is given things, which is itself a temporary status, than it is hard to truly be pleased and drawn, for goods that flicker themselves from virtue, liberty and reason. Indeed, as morals come from the heart, and take fashion frmo our resourcefullness, 'as though our umph of morality was a problem we wished to solve', that so in our umphs of sums, treatment, the moon, or things of effort, or love making, so our time and attention is spent. But it comes from the heart, our interest, our way. And such movments, or beats, are most agreeable when they arrive from a balanced state. For it is not about grief or criticism that this or that motive is shouldered off, but rather, when it comes from an absent of things we hold preferred and true, then the pull we have outside of this feels like were being moved away from such things, and the condition which it invokes. For such a tune breathes and speaks of all things at once; for nothing is sought which cannot be, nor should be held back against. It is like a machinery to puts out what it can, and thus anything made is by definition a timely and welcomed good. And there is so much. But when the gear is off and something comes out, 'falling half way up the track', no matter what it is coated in, nor how much we feel drawn to it, 'given the nature of the track, and how it is we who remark it being on or off', that so do we tremor at the thought of consuming it, for we accept the status of the track which produced it, and thereby distance ourselves from the harvest of a straighter path.
My thoughts are quite well. I must admitt there is a slight intertia to my mood, regarding Bella, pleasure, the imbalance of our want and seeking people.

So quaint are the amending efforts with those of a pleasing and sparking sort. Life really comes to sway, and things of the past, be it feeling or error, polish off and dissipate theyre grime. New ones come in, new friends, new memories, more strenght and grace for what lies forward: peace in whats occured, happyness with whats been, where we are.
In many ways it is just easy to say things are well and move on. It is known that thoughts come further about, as do shifts in feelings and views, fancies and pleasures. Though, it is worth noting that certain choices made, as perhaps born of this lack of friendship, or that confused state of love, 'whereby you seek the former in order to satiate the later, when in truth the mere prescence, and trust of perpetuity is enough'', that so we errored, and upon the basis for which we did so, the effect did not well incorporate: and we left.

I cant ignore this relatively clear thought, and that is, by our own grace and stride we feel sturdy and of cheer; yet we don't always exhault this to all people; generally only those were familiar with.  Let us look into our memory for today.

Perspective and ease settle in; and not in a distancing way, 'as though you were sinking into yourself, but away'. Tired am I, and perhaps a fool to write. For what could I better garner than some rest, to allow my mind to settle, experience how it really is, and if firming is needed here or softening there, then to do so, but upon a more circumspect and rigorous state. Right now were weary, tired, spent.
 Yet I have clear thoughts, and enough focus to retain our path of the day. Perhaps were only weighing down further; but I feel this makes room for those truer parts of our mind to settle.
 For one, today was a good day. There was challenge, but rightfully so, for truth came out. Nothing negative. Something which came to mind, is that pleasure, or this sort of happiness in seeing people, is an ever fickle, and often overemblished status. We are not so solid or true beneath. Perhaps none are away from this. But something did occur, a sort of grace and honor of our duty and way. Not so it was deemed small, nor us stronger; but that it was itself true, soverign in its call to commisery. By that, it is our task to respond; but it is the fairness of the oblige, the understansding of who we are, which gives rest; for our appropriate fills in all. Time can allow this. But it is the confusion of who we are and what it means to be, that causes grief and gruff. And by all counts, when pleasure is wanted, upon labor and wearyness, and something pleasing is knotted in you, you see the passivity in which you experienced other sweets. When they are there then were fine. But we are not in fact so well, underneath. And we know this. No love can block out how we really are. It just gives room to look past it, or fret not if its on your mind; in particular when circusmtance would squeeze such aspects out of you. But this remarks the condition of our way, the amends we must make: the need to stand tall. But other elements come about to. We like to write and uncover, to experience and look forward to. It is hard to think when your in such a state; and indeed it is much easier in the first hour or so. But when you slacken, and notice more, it is hard to conciliate. And we take it in, seeing ourself, breathing air, peacefully I might add, into those brightest portions of me. All worry and lust, fear and comparison melt away.
If we add groups of terms together, subsequent in the range of such groups, whereby the furthest term is removed while the newest is added, that doing so on a clock will a) return to the starting state, and b) do so as all other combinations of terms of the same kind of group [range] and clock [type]. Never has a sequence of this sort failed to meet this criteria. The reason is unknown, yet my familiairty with to process leads me to suppose that by cutting off remaining value, 'per the clock', that by some nature this leaves us with what we have.

The clearest thought in my head is that there is no problem. Group dynamics are extremely tough, as inconsistencies early on magnify themselves later. If its a small group you can tie up loose ends so to speak, but often in a large group this is hard to do. And disputes, or ruptures between people can be even more weird, as each side goes to one other area of the group; but the one who is more initagrated often goes to the bulk of things more easily.
 One element of my life is confidence, which is not so much about exhaltion, but being ourself, by our daily intent, our ethic and or direction at work, as some sort of internal but also outward (via our surrounding life) imperative. And the surer this is the happier we are. For we make friends more easily, and acquaint ourselves, via some form of courtest or address, to almost all else. And this comes rather naturally, rather than through eagerness or excitement. If our enthusiasm is different we keep along, nor are we grieved by the relations other people have.
 What I mean then, by there being no problems, is that your never ousted from the group. There isn't even really a group per say. Consider how you talk with Andy or Carli, and imagine, or establish it in your mind, that other peopel are just talking as they find easy: for such talking, when its easy, is very pleasing, laughter being like sparks of such flame. The matter then is whether or not you find ease, and sometimes I do, sometimes not, and be it this or that way, so do I personally alter.  This is what I mean to say then. For much of my life is spent on false oppertuinty, and seeing other people who find ease amongst one another.  The trouble I face, and it is not so that I lack the commrdaery and friendship that could be if I were otherwise, but it is the grace, peace and rest in our self respecting ways, whereby liberty, virtue and freedom of mind are rooted in and embellished; and the objects which draw to me, and values at that, are not burdened by being things that are not so comparable. I have learned, for instance, that you need not tell someone your life story in order to solidify repor, but that you may tell them something comparable to what is essential to you, that your vegan, or eat healthy, or do yoga, or read; no different than how you game.  One primary thought was that of pleasure and aims, or at least anticipation and plans, they bascially comfort you and ease you into doing nothing, and feeling fine where your at because it is pleasing.  One weird element is that of porn, for in my deepest recesses I seek what I am seeing, and find myself thinking of woman that way, and feeling off that I cannot procurr that. But I've learned how, and in part it is from merely living this way. We can address ourself, swot of unwanted or unvalid thoughts of what we lack or should do, and be as we need, remark upon all there is which this includes, and of interest to, but in that, live where we are, of home, town and company, without remorse or regret. Often times it is the greatest trouble to not be yourself, because you are tired or seperarte from yourself, and from that, bear down upon it and not be so calm and open. It is tricky, for you may not in fact find much to incorporate yoursewlf with. But one, speaking with people may be done on a personal level, and this removes even the notice of more enthused or childish things. You don't even care. Plus, if you are high and well, then you sit on the edge of such conversation like the rest of them. I view it as though the pressure to be ourself without deference to others or exhaulting ourselves, that we let there be weight upon me that our 'performance' otherwise reflects. And this was a hard balance, and in this way or the other was the impetus for us putting Bella out of mind; it also was where the roots of our fancy for Amon, and Bella later on, lie. It is essential to rememebr that our plea, or at least resolve in being here, was that although a river was near to a larger and more plentiful sea, we were still a fisherman here, and we could adjust or our rope and balance out our place, to get what was available. By all counts it was not bad. And the mountains in this cove were nothing but marvelous. I think that you and Bella are knotted by the best and worst parts of your mind. And all because we were hardstrung to do this, with some reverberations in our slightly leary eomployment a year back, to asking Bella out, to our revival of even the slightest grace in all the strenght we have, and amidst this marvel of studious and or wonderful things, that all of this is so that we were not an adult.
So roads offer more to those with the eye to see things. For one, just stop, and walk, or pause, for the right angle. On the bridge going to Pitt, or the Burger King spot. And indeed, it is nice to go somewhere and sit and see, and indeed the west side of Larry Walker offers the greatest east view. But all around there are roads with angles and openigns worth our time. One such direction is going through hammond, down the back waresely road to 203rd, then comnig down 203rd to lougheed; and going up lougheed is nice itself. And we've experiecned this going across dewdney into Westview, down that back country road, and into the newer developments that take us down by the GMC. These routes are avaialble to all who'd gleam it. And again, go to Vulkor park, pause for a moment, then go on. And indeed, far 203rd extends from this, as does Pitt field which we don't take advantage of enough.
The pistons in my heart, the steel in my mind, all to an end of grand quality, or perhaps chugging along.
 Often I find myself struggling to remark upon things; and I see it as though there was this mechanism, some kind of motion, as may reflect a tamber or hue, but also direction, oriention, magnitude, and that such was how any given principle, fact, memroy or value was defined.
 There are rods which have not been moved for a time. And an odd thing of writing, that it tends to only speak of things you don't know. For the Gods, there is little which unerves me or lingers fancifully, 'making me curious'. And so reiteraitng or speaking to some small aspect is a challenge, as the whole is at rest, 'like Victor in his tomb'. And this is a good thing.
 But what I find is that we are still lacking things essential, or fundmental. On one end you have the blatant fact that 'such regards' are not so needed, as reflects having little to say, and that it is life and experience we care for. The lack of helming this leads to a rather unflavored nor checked character to our desires, and we feel ill in our pleasure, want of things that are not by any adult or substnatial degree ours. There is a false freedom that occurs by anothers provision, and you feel fine to let life come some other day, while you sit here, at ease, but also idle, and in response, you feel more consented to remedying pleasures: insincere ones, of the mind, of falsity or concept. Porn is the harshest partner in this.
 In any case, the flipside of this is that our life is in fact oppertune; and we tend not to have the stability, or harness in life, as to establish our self in such desire, when we are idle, or, as in those cases of given provision, unable, nor smooth in how able we are, to tend to such idleness by mending ourself. For such a state as would come from mending is a flowing natural one, where our desire sprouts readily about. It is but the constancy of life which we may be out of tune with, and thereby, via the force of labor and deference (when our fortune is not ours), that we fall away from that felicituous gait. And indeed, our life is our own so much as our ability and dream to effect our desired outcome is ours to both aim for, adjust to, relish, and proliferate. Swelling below is that odd statement, whereupon anothers shelter, that you feel unwelcomed to care for yourself, in the way that your felicity requires. It is perhaps only our parents who elicit this. I find a comparable feeling also when thinking of friends, or any who were close with or open to, that of our excuses, wearisomeness or concern, that we feel reservations of many a quality in sharing with them. It is not, by our parents or any close to us, that we feel odd or unwelcome in pursuing what we want, but rather in complaining, or struggling to reach it. Perhaps the end is stated unclearly, and by those counts, our most charmed remark is that 'the fruits of felicity are not a position to reach, nor product to meet, but rather a dance, a stride, a flow of grace and prosperity: it is a form of experience, that merely captures the embers of its experience, and folds them in as textures of its identity'. When we say that our life is about flow, and that we mean to live well, rather than well off, that we are saying in that something more than that we care for a quality or manner of life, but that we don't prioritize nor relish a house, nor fanciful travel, nor the dreary mundeandness of common touring; but instead, we wish to write a paper on the repitiion of starting states when operated on a clock, as do we wish to traverse the geographies of various objects: clouds, mountains, paleontology, constitutions and government. And I breathe in an delicacy of wonderful sights, of the performed sort. Withcer, Next Generation, Blue Planet 3, early Easy Allies, Beginner Servers, Bardown: so simple and common are they dear to me. "The imagination flushed inside me from experiecncing phantom menace, or the coruscant night." We struggle though, for twisting our hips, unwinding our shoulders, 'resting our eyes', is an ever obtuse thing; no more definite than the moon; each being but an output, or texture, of our manner. Indeed, the root of modern philosophy is in tactifully, but stewardly, speaking of the way in which we live paired with the objects born of that, or essential in some cases. For work is our life in a way, and as such this can be seen. But it is a sport, a performance, a test which a good sleep and sharpened pencil can satiate, when we regard it as such. Short of this, it is something other.
 A province of thought could be that pleasure, or the comfort of our experience, is quite fundmental, and stearing of our attiude and amends. It can be quite closing if we most often experience struggle; and we bolt down, lube the edges, and then remedy however much strife we experience.
 In brief, we have never lacked an expeirence which was unsatisfying enough for me to feel like anything extrordinary was required to reach it. Nor did my adolescence recieve any peruading impressions as to what could elsewhere be received. I always felt enough to do what we liked. The nature of our duties though became less creative nor occupational, 'as passing time in French class sometimes felt', but became more laborous; and the people around became less of my friends, for we were not invovled in recess or sports; and I did not care for cars or music as they did; and girls were this euphoric siren which blended the nature of our attitude and deeds.
Two thoughts on my mind, one from last night, the other this morning.
 The former is about objects and sentiment, or rather manner in things, whereby you move in a certain way, for a certain ideal, as though bonded to the nature of the state, but you then included, or at least sprout objects, facts, principles to an extent. And these often collide; as you find yourself loving, but a person in that gaze fills ill put. Our view of things then change.
 The latter thought remarks that idea of elementary school, as though it were our duty, sufficeint, but also pleasing, as we could just be there, comfort ourselves as we can, but surround ourselves with friend and company. Yet, this is a very still life, as though nothing is ever to change or move, away from this kind of life that is. And we just bolster it up. As the nature of our duty is not in fact school but work, we have larger gaps to surround with comfort and remedy. This is a weird feeling most young adults probally feel. But then there is another way to live, where you are not so beholden, situated nor complacent to a position, as though it will always be there, but you press on, move with intent and pace; and not to some end, but in your manner, with objects and things on your plate: the texture of your manner and gait as it were. What comes to mind is Vancouver and how we oftne imagine it as this lighter, softer, warmer place than here in Pitt Meadows; and we often included notions of love, promise, gallantry, as though to make our position more pleasing. But were stopped, to some halting end, merely a fairer one. Were not living our life. And indeed, this has been our impetus for an age, and our greatest times, where liberty stood on our own grounds, that we saw perhaps what comforts we had, what friends were around; as were we thrown by love, and perhaps to an end which was all to submiting to mere position rather than life; and then in moments where life was being lived, but with nothing really but some other on your mind, for which they did not humour our proposal for further bonding. In any case, we felt that life would move on, and as thought clear, 'as though a promising or tender thought that came across our mind', we simply let it come in and warm us, but then pass us by, as we were living now, occupied, our mind suttle yet bent, all the while we tend to ourselves. If people are doing this then it is in theyre own way, naturally, and so whether we do it this or that way, or with these or those things, so we are part of the game. And such a game is an ever present one; with no lunches nor breaks so to speak, merely a tilting of the helm. The sun for instance, glitters our day, but then upon her set, offers a moment to relish her final hues, but then ceases her daylight, and suggests to us that we turn in for the day. We may listen or not, but per sleep, which we need, and find affiable in the dark, and in relation to all other fixed things that occur in the day, that so do we humour this tunr of light for something which we respond to in resepect to sleep and rest, 'and days end'. All is connected, and it would seem that the greatest of these moving lives is where this is so. Indeed, it is often beholden to propriotous goods that allow this; and we often get caught on intent, or an absent of 'often taken for granted pleasures and conceit', whereby our practices are not so robust or known, yet our momentum is per the fruits they more or less provide, keeping us to such strata in things, but without sure fire ground. Keeping there though, we see the things needed to hold us. Much of my adult life has been about a calming of this arrangment, so that our priorities are not so sturdy yet narrow; and instead, we may live high, but amongst all things, friends and company, pursuit and awe; and via practices which are strong in theyre heart and princiuple, as opposed to the past habits which were so defined and fixed, but only affored specific supports. Our training for instance, has always alluded me in being something suitbale and constant, but otherwise welcomed and sustaining. Now though, per all things, a single day of practice suffices, and we do very well. I find myself worrying little whether we look good; and I am trying to take my mind off the fact of whether we look particularly healthy or not. There is so much to do beyond the minor confidence or esteem in this; and the qualification to impress or want even to draw people, or feel included; such is a small point, and not to an end which your more complacent mind could see. Such is the trap of love; that it often says, 'turn off your pistions, relax your heart, loose your life and way, and just be with folk, coalescent to what they think and like'. This is its own way of being bonded and affable per the life that such strata invovles. Its no different then yours.
 I feel perhaps blinded by other people merely living theyre own form of life, and that ours is not in principle any more signifcant or special. Why this is so is that we are not in motion of ours, nor flourishing with it, and so others feel above me. Better put, when I am not so mobile or active in ours, I see others; and often they get clumped up, whereby alot of them feel joined, while I sit here seperate from that. Have you given thought to all those in Kamloops, or Vancouver, or at Superstore in Coquitlam or Walmart in Maple Ridge? What about every family in Pitt Meadows, or every employee. Were not so immobile that a province further is worth regarding. "Theres merely more land heeding the suns shine."
I left for Kamloops with a bag of gold that I did not know I had. We settled there, remained active and relatively astute, but the place of our life, its meaning, our activity, fell to ware. And indeed, we came to ourself in the following fall, writing some of our dearest things and making our set of Battlefield videos. We broke down also. It compares to how we are now, something we feel and have felt for some time, but remain steady, or off title perhaps; but back then, we had it in our mind that certain things were a certain way, and that we could count on them. But as is common, a moment of love broke me off, and had me truly looking at myself. I'll come back to this feeling, or this view of things that we've brought forward, but I wish to move past that moment, and say that the time that followed, albeit inclusive of things born of a new resolve, were relatively the same. And the idea was that we came to ourselves, but without the pretensions which offered promise or affirmation. One element was our health, and how we spent a great deal of effort, at least intention, on our aesthetique, or appearing healthy. It was seldom easy to just do what was enough. And indeed, this has become simpler over the years, but our tolerance for only doing what we need has lead to vulnerabilities to inertia. One slick bit of friction is that trying a little, as to make up for natural inconsistency or oddity in nature, runs up against this sensitivity to do even more. A little feels like not enough, even though it is exactly the solid amount I need.
 All that is to say, that we had a very tender and balanced view of things. I think we were still a bit unprepared for things to come. But indeed, having reached the heights of that some two years later, I can see that our previous sense was not so far off, but that it was merely too unrigorous for the deeds ahead. For what I've noticed is, that upon labor and the more fixed path of life, that you feel a tremendous amount of effort required on your part. And because of this, you find yourself not liking everything; as your too worried about yourself. It is an odd thing indeed, for my insight over time was not that you could merely connect and or reveal such cares you had, and from that, not feel so hidden and or disdained. Rather, you just learn how to be open for open sake. Sharing that we like yoga, eating healthy, things like that which in some shape or form reflect what is essential to me, allow for us to bind with people. It has nothing to do with our response to pressure; these may be shared, but theyre so near and specific, that our relation needs to be such. But, we still do yoga and care for health, as we do games, and these things connect you so far as the depths of such eleemnt fit into the depths of the available connection. Too often we imbued these pressures, but then let our enamure and excitment, or buzz, carry us to be eager and enthused with people. But this was not really a source of connection but satisfaction on our part. And indeed, the flipside has occured, where tending to ourself without such flaunting or vanity, has me not so tailored to that satisfaction; which often flees away, as much of it is born from us being so eagerly there. But it keeps not. But, in being more steady, we form more meaningfull connections; not ones that reach, or mirror that other kind of buzz, but ones that you trust, where you feel free and ready to be yourself, known in your heart and principle.
 When we started work last year, we softened into this mindest with a fair bit of ease. But not with all. Certain people just did not come to sight, and in part it was because we were still so focused on ourself. It was a bit of a stale and rigid process, where we knew not to be so eager, and at worst, admitt and or humour expectations from it. But we felt not so fufilled as such. We quickly became affiable and close with some people. But our effort just found its groove; and who was easy to talk to we did, and who wasn't we did not. And we felt off about this, naturally, and we were perhaps eagerly courteous. As though to smooth off our sense of seperation, so I could just proceed.
The primary thought, of our life perhaps, is that we tend to ourselves in a great deal of ways, and via our time as children, we do this at pleasures perril, for we sanction ourself off; or, as our adulthood has shown, make it merely a higher bar for us to be present with people. I've learned the hard way what happens when you reach that point, connect, and perhaps in a state that reflects the charm of that threshold (a high point of excess); but then upon our personal lapse, we fall either alone, or make haste ahead, 'as though to keep what we feel like were losing'. This happened when we were suppose to stay home for two weeks during March, and we had just started talking to Holly.
Early in the year, near its start, we had resolve to content ourselves with work and let life plod along. We found ourself rather pleased and with company, and all that stood in our way was this drowning sense, which our own place would mitigate. Upon reaching that place, I failed, and fell into a iron stalemate. We did not eat for a week, and felt some oddity of lostlessness. For I still sought to move, yet it seemed so far away. But by all counts this plea was not so fundmeental, but one of prefernece; as though 'sure, we'll stay for the summer, we just need this change of scenery. Yet the summer was not important, and in fact, only drew us because our life was fair. But it was not exactly bounding; nor in tune with many of the things we felt some larger change were required to meet. It was simply strange to feel so still and idle, for the prospect was one for mere continuity; yet we felt so unable to be continuous now. Such was the fabric of our live, merely wanting to improve, but loosing the strands which held it up.
 I recall this feeling as I was walking with tristan near the bus loop, and that was this sense of being where I was, present as I wanted to be, but without the rule, the standard. We have always held true to ourself; perhaps just not well enough; though the foundation which exhibited itself in Vancouver still remained; and its elements can be more or less described, and indeed influenced us in our latter time at Kamloops, to an extent during last years spring, and seemingly to a rather steady and comfortable flourishing in this early year. But I personally felt stopped; as though remaining at home, yet with the intent to leave, which by all counts was a fair aim for oru interest in being present, yet ourselves, made our intent for ourselve rather troubling. It is a similar feeling when your PC breaks or performs poorly; and had it been at a state which was an improvment you'd feel fine, but it being a regression makes it hard to swallow. What occured though was that we humoured the thought of not being ourself at all. For the response, as lingered with Holly during Covid, was one, where given the halt in our 'ideal change', that in remaining where we were, that we'd have to turn into ourselves in order to mantle it. True, we could reach the moderate stability we had during our iniative to find a change in place as to allow it to be improved. But this felt unappealling nor tenuable. It was a spiritual whiplash. We choose not to do that, but instead, humoured the position in which our stability offered us to. You see, everyone is themselves; and when theyre tired or busy have not much to say, nor are open and malleable for connection, or communion --beyond what is crystallized in the depths. Now I have historically had a hard time being in such place, for we held so much worry and or practice, that we barely poked our head above. And when we did, we found ourselves unstable, as though we were walking for the first time, slipping all over the place. That, or we just didn't have the momemntum or fluidity to make any real substantial effort or union, given our slight excess. More or less we have grown; and further by the day. Hard it is so see how easy it was. But sometimes our enthusiasm for having such excess was misplaced; as starting last year, we found ourselves excited about being open and able about our loves, but not our ways; and this latter sits much closer to the line of union. In part, those loves are what you bring forth; and we came from that.
 I recall rather fondly the month of Decemebr; or better put, the time following Christmas, where we played Dragons Dogma and Baludrs Gate. Something to note, is that despite our comfort from Bella, it wasn't all too substnatial, nor was it rested on meeting aynthing more. By all counts it was a novel change from someone who, like Morgan, was a deafening spot, or one that brought more inertia than movment; but second, is that it was just nice and pleasing, as it is with Alex and Andy, Joey and Oliver, Chenoya to and the gals, and Victor. The point, is that our resolve was one where we could be ourselves. I think in part, as we felt when moved in here, 'and looked at ourself in the mirror, all sexy and hot, but no where to go', that we felt some simialr kind of promise; as though we coudl have Tristan over at our house, and we dreamt deep down that perhaps Bella to, or, further, Amon. This was reaching outside of our contentment and ease. For life was clear during those months; for Christmas brought joy, but we then felt like it was time and oppertune to move, and we then played Baldurs Gate. We felt solid, and able in being ourself. But like all things, we did not pay much respect to how things wuold naturally settle. Perhaps we would have felt this way regardless, and that it was in many ways but an acceleration of your eventual want to ask Bella out, or feel lost without it. Feeling down just prompted this, as did her saying no force this realization of ourselves, that we are lost.
I wish to do a bit of a critical analysis, of the reason to move to Vnacouver, our finances, as may speak to our need to, or rather haste to.
 What comes to mind is meetups, as theyre are so many across the land. The walking group and John Henry speaks to me, as I love the area, and the bout is not much of a hike. The practical philosophy group, perhaps niche in its kind, is a definite gem of things; for it is in person, I believe thursday evenings, and just a solid thing to go to. When I dream of the best day, or greatest life, it is one where, with the setting sun, you go to such thing. And you may scooter there and back, or transit a little. It reminds me of going to PT class, and how we'd stop far back and walk across town.
 As for our finances, we are pretty equal in our gait. Were working 3 and 4, which brings us just over 1200, which is ample. We are spending some money, perhaps a little too much on food. We've bought Kingdom Come, which was a short yet sweet experience, and we bought Ark, which has been worthile; as I've learned that being friends with someone, like Justin, is really about keeping in touch, and you can always say hello. We have many things from Amazon, all relatively small. Most are going back soon, though our big water cooler needs to go back before the 26th.
My mind gets caught about Bella somtimes, and in all reality it is merely about our own energy, our own vigor, and how sometimes it feels too unsettled around her. The soul fact is that we find ourself trying to be eager and enthused, as though to elevate us; not something which continues through the day. But when she is there, my wish or comfort in being so lessens. And on one hand this may evoke false or exagerrated feelings of views about her, as one who evokes this lethargy. On the other, it really just speaks to how you are with any person who you don't know, and how your naturally compelled, or moved, to be less eradict, compared to how you are with Andy and Joey, rather than Hazel.
 I find our time rather ambivolent. But this is a good thing. Wounds are healing, and foremost, our handle on things is becoming firm yet suttle, nor are we so swayed. Principle to this development is this removal of our sense, or at least less rigid response, which ellicits this feeling that other people are more important and that you are not. Perhaps it is just the buisiness of the day which throws me sometimes, or slackens our ability to fit in. Remaining calm though, which happens quite easily when it is not so busy, settles everything in. And something I find very oppertune, is that Bella, being a unique member, is so as to be somewhat difficult to talk to. I spoke with Anthony today, as do I feel genial with Hazel. The point is not how we are, as though this should anchor you, but that you are free, at liberty. Were not so amazed by what other people are doing. I think in part they are there, as though some side of theyre life, but that where they are is not so satisfying. However well theyre life is around this, it is carried with theyre work; and whoever they are with at work, so theyre work is there. This is not so important though, just something I noticed. Especially so when you are friendly and medial with all people. This is brought further by being part of the store's day. And again, its not abaout anchoring; this is the moral. In that, you are kept, as though to feel inevibtaly secure. While a more liberal and sturdy approach, that does not grip, is merely with, unafraid, bringing our true self. The time keeps on and we all leave. If theyre are jokes to be had, I dare say I care not for any who have them. For those who I am closest with, it is my least favorite part. And time just goes on. Max even said, 'i'm a shithead'. That is what makes them less adult like, in theyre complacence to theyre shit. As in all things, eyeing down and trying to define what something is merely firms the distance you are from yourself; which indeed, requires its own kind of form, but only that which allows you to be free, not compelled, not ignored, nor sheltered from. We are theyre through and through, to all. And appropriatley as things meet. Which is the case for Bella. As we are not so strange and unfamiliar, as we are with Hazel or Anthony. We have a weird history. And it is not for me to ploy nor be coy in wishing for or lamenting about us being friends. But our freedom may exist. Like a wet towel the water rings out.
I don't know if there is any real truth or right. I am not defering to optimism or uprightness either.
 One notion is that things are not as easy as any moment may make you feel they are. Comparison is not a useful tool here, despite revealling something about ourself.
 In any case, it feels at the core of things that our struggle, or uncertainty, lies at that point where things are well, we are free and fine, but we feel somewhat seperate from things pleasing. Our whole life the extent of this has reached far and wide. Whereas now it is almost near to me. But the insight, or reflection, is that this notion of things being well, is true, but that you should go forward and make your dreams come to be, or engage in pleasure, looks past the point that there is still much to do, and that such things are not so easy. In fact there the most challenging of things. Not constant in theyre toil, but in theyre adherence. Which by all counts is a sign of progress, where you do these things naturally, and flow with such manner in your stride; whereby there is less doubt and more shine ahead.

This could change mind you. Though, these elements are not so determining. It is really our neighbourhood, our environment. So I've thought of a fairly lovely way of describing the starting and advancing states. Some thanks to Gp.
 For one, you may start all talks and establishments of first principle, with a (7,7), as to work with a 12 hour clock, as its known, and the first succeeding state is (7,2). Perhaps the addition isn't clear, but it works with the accepted standard of clocks; anything short of 6,6 will not do, and equal pairs just seem nice.
 What we say, is that we more or less operate on this starting state but using values of a clock. Stating it as such means that our result is not whole or natural, but based on the repeating terms of a clock. Illuded to or intuited, the height of a clock, which you may harmlessly state as 12, brings the value, as obviously above 12, to some proceeding value from the start of terms that rise from the climax of 12. Tis obvious, or easy to illustrate that 7 plus 7 in this case is 2. And that from there, we take this new result, or sum, and combine it with the preceding term --the top value in the prior state. That, or we may say that this succeeding state removes the oldest term, or far one, and pairs the remaining one with the sum/result of the prior state. 1,1 -> 1,2 -> 2,3. I like the idea of saying there is a starting state of certain groups of terms. The amount of terms marks the group being a couple, trio, quad etc. Given this state, we add the values on a repeating number line, or in other words a clock. In effect, if the sum is higher than the height of the clock, then you return a value that respects the repeating nature of the clock. This is the operation, and I find it more or less easily sits with the matter of the starting state. Advancing the state, given this operation, amounts to taking the oldest, or first term of a group away, and appending (adding to the end) the resulting value of the prior state. This is the nature of the sequence: state, operation, advancement and or successiion.
Let us pretend then that were making our full statement. Not description mind you, but proposition.
 Given a starting state, of any comobination of terms, that suming such terms with respect to clock-like values --as though on a clock-- using the result of such sum to advance to the next state, whereby such result is appended to the set of terms and the first removed, that upon progressing this way the initial state will be reached.
 Given the nature of the state, it may be a pair of terms, or a trio, quad etc., and may be acted upon by this or that length of clock. Within this, all combinations of terms per each type of group, will exhibit this repeating behavior, and with equal effort. This shared behavior is equal in kind within different measures of operation. "Pairs in clock 9 and 10 all have theyre own corresponding rally point, per the clock."


Take a pair of terms as a starting state, and advance this state by adding the terms together. The new state will remove the oldest/first of the prior terms and add the sum of them. Such result ought be determined by clock values, which is to say, if the sum of terms extends beyond the height of the clock, then we start counting from nothing, and use that value. This value, combined with the latter of the recent state, becomes our advanced/newest state. Doing so will see the initial state return. This behavior is so regardless of clock type/height, amount of terms, ie. pairs, triples etc; and all combinations of terms per the clock height and group size will repeat. Moreover, within each clock height, all combinations within a given group size will repeat at the same point. All pairs of each clock lenght will rally in theyre at theyre own according spots, as will all triples, quads and so forth.


Take a pair of terms and create a sequence by adding them together, removing the oldest/starting term, and appending theyre sum/result. Proceed by this order, but following the reocurrence rule, whereby upon a set value, if the sum of the state extends beyond it, then we count from 1 till we satisfy whats remaining. Doing so will bring you to the starting state. Morover, you will find that all combination of pairs, per that set value of reocurrence, will repeat in the same amount of steps. Further, that they will all repeat at a shared point in at all such points of reoccuring value. Different thresholds mind you per each value, but within each one, pairs, triples, quads and so forth, will all have theyre kindred rally point
If I were at liberty, than I could make a podcast because I wanted to, join a group or organization for the pure moral sentiment, or try this or that, or study.
 What is our aim though? We think perhaps it is an ultimate, and perhaps sentimental ideal, of proper discourse, and that it is less so about us being heard, but actually imparting what we believe to be the thing which can affect change. Much of our reserve, or auseterity in thought, comes down to our own ignorance of how things are operated, but also in deference to how it is pithily viewed. I actually think that if we could sprout a more reasonable perspective and conduct regarding government, war, death and the gods, that some sort of improvement could be made. In part, as unclear or decisive as this progress or benefit is known, then we rest on our knowledge of things, and how the way they operate is not so monolithic, but quite localized, varied, calm. Odd things come from odd connections with one of the many branches in the higher strucutre, or between to individuals who cross paths.
 I find myself though, similar to sums, or our study of anything, our health even, leaning into steadyness, and letting these things be; were confident how they are and that they'll be, but the manner in which they do seems to come from our liberty, which is brought by nothing more than the harmony in our deeds, and the sweet rigor in our stide; to have such thoughts, work on them, and bring us to act. Sums has become this in the recent past, where the idea of sharing it, though lined with some procrastination, has been moved on with deliberate intent; we've been learning what to write and say as though we were sharing it, and by all counts, the composition of our technical thoughtt has more than doubled. We also told Matin about it, quite well so far as we could, and the idea came to mind that we'd share it with Justin. The ppint is not that they offer some reward or prospect, but that by our liberty, we thought of the effort on the whole, tended to that, and through clarity, felt eager and at ease to speak of it. That is our sprouting line. And indeed, I find that the actual amend to email it is a small yet mountanous task, and one that could perhaps use its own development in composition. But I also see, that such a thing is pure liberty, rather than something which we are otherwise happy to just do on a whim. Its that feeling of gambling, or taking bets, that your happy enugh now to concived a reward for trying something; but you fear not if you don't get it because your happy. This disconnect here is that your not so compelled to do it so well; but in contrast, you also may do it well enough, or at all. And these feelings come and go, as we are more bent towards this latter motion, where the quality of the piece is more emphasized, as we are not so ambivolent about the possible reward, yet at the same time a little callous in our excitment. It feels more like a steady pursuit, that is not riled up by some esteem or remarkibility in the work; and so it is not some shot that we are clearly oppertune to take. It feels like we have to do it well. There is an underlying current of promise, but it is more interwined in the subject-matter and experience, rather than glory. `
