There is a peace in my bones, a softness, wholeness, sweetness in my heart, where no remorse, envy, worry, nor unsteadyness lie.
 This feeling is hard to convey; or better put, hard to stand by. As I find myself seeking other things, moved by this or thrown by that, positively or negatively. And I don't know why such peace is of succor, and if the means to it are laudible. It feels like were giving things up.
 I've been on some dopamine latley; minor really given our past, but relatively we are being splurged with it. And I find myself nervously excited and pleased. And some things come to mind, which we are overconfident about, or perhaps somber at the reality. Or of things more clear and reasonable, I still feel almost distracted by them, and overly enthused and set on them. I am aware of our peace though. In the past, when i had those more excited feelings, they either made up for, or at the very least surrounded a rather empty feeling, and so we had no sense or rest or good beneath or enamured way. Now I have that, but it is not so alive, nor are we with it. Its as though I went to a dance, was with someone I loved, but was chatting with other people. And it is one thing to have the nerves and or anticipation which omes with the latter, and not being so moved by thbis for you know who your with; and when your with no one, this fancficul notions have no room for doubt, or you see how folly they are and how absent things are. But were not with our partner, and I miss that. I'd rather not chat.
 One of the reasons we've not writtne so much as of late is because we are not so privy to the clouds of intrigue and or idea that woft above our solid ways. Were to focused on those ways, and not so keen or inviting to what puffs about. Tis an odd form, or manner of happiness, that it tends to open itself to things that are not so baked into itself. There is a reality, or point rahter comparing to what I said, that when were inundated with pleasure and satiety, that we move and feel in tandum with that. The vice in this, or folly, is that you overlook your constitution, and forgo the peace and liberty of that, but also stability; and so that great feeling you have which spurrs want of fun and friends, is like a spire of such good, but brittle at the base; and when the moment of that ends, your back with yourself; and much inconstancy lies there. In any case, I find that it is not firends nor fun nor oppertunity which is poor, but the root which it comes from. That we ought be a certain way is not something were judging, only that of our peace, our solidity, our manner and hue which prompts and succours in awe and felicity, so I remain there. And this is short of dopamine, sugar, porn, twitter and tik tok, nor any of the ideals of commentary or expertise, or humour.
 My whole life it seems has come about this way. I won't leave, nor fall into a path that has things I seek, but from a root which is dumb. Our entire adolescence, or young adulthood, 'which is youth applied', has been in being so undumb; yet reality did not line up with our confidence, and cynicism produced, as did acquiesence and acceptence of natural difficulty. But liberty ensued, as did creativity and our ability to produce; and further, be open, amiable, extending out of courtesy but into comradery and friendship. We swim, do yoga, play games, eat healthy, live this or that way. Were quite known then, and interests and affinity guide us together naturally. A wonderful thing truly. And it binds us in our integral ways; for we are really being ourselves. And it is not so much a vice, but perhaps a mark of this inherent promise, that good things are coming, as we feel further open and well; that so do other sparks of oppertunity and interest arise. "The farther and novel bits of the atmopshere gleam light also when we are giving mind to the possibilities near to us. Perhaps those former are but a farther dream; but commiserate no less with these nearer ones."

So the state of our paper is such that we have a good form to the principle, in that we have a starting state of two terms, say 1,1 and we create a sequence by acting on such pair with addition and a reoccuring principle. In effect, the former notion sees us create a subsequent state by combining both terms, and keeping the head one, so it would go 1,1 - 1,2 - 2,3 - 3,5. The latter effect though fashions the manner in which we combine, for the reoccurrence principle says, 'that upon some determined range, or height, that if the combined values exceed this, we begin from 0 and count up till we satisfy the excess'.

For some time I've felt sad about Bella. Her smile is so sweet and her innonence is rather endearing. She's so bundly in her confidence and nervousness, I just feel sour about no longer being her friend. But what makes me cry is the shame surrounding this, the conflict, the weirdness, and how this a) makes me feel hard pressed to live as though we were free, 'for we see some strife ahead', and b) we no longer see our liberties and pleasure with other people as so fufilling or accessible. In part this is because of the first reason. But it just brings me a doubt, and innervates me with conceit about our confidence and expectation. Which admitteldy remarks something beyond me, 'as though how we should be, or ought move, growth wise, is set for some place different than we currently are'.
I find with our emotions and thouhts wiling about, that it takes some reserve on my part not to engage them, as to give them form, and bring more understanding of them.
 It seems we talk of things when our emotion or hesitation has our normal foresight and fancy clouded. What occurs, is that we wish to be at peace, so these things may come and go, take root and form, or not, while we remain merry, soft. But if there is some problem, or some sense of being out of sorts, or uncertani of things for which we are resolved, then we find it hard to be free and at peace. We are left to affirm or keep busy, which we don't always want to do.
So the tenure of my life feels clear and simple to expose. For breathing in such light sheds all precariousness as, for one, it shows you other things, similar, that no longer hold you so tight, and you see how comparable they are to whatever toils you now.
Often these moods of mine, our sense, gets somewhat detached from our ability to feel warm and loved with those around me. Let's name them. Mom, Dad, Jess, Mavis, Nova, Grandma, Grandpa, our family. Then there's Justin, who has always been a close friend. We walk different paths, but he heeds me and I him, and he is a fellow man. Victor is a new friend, though we center around Path of Exile. He is literally insane. But I like that. Tristan knows me a bit, so were merely pals. Joey, Andy and Alex are good work friends. We talk about games and vibe well. Tereas, Carli, Carry, Kim and Tara are the ol boots, who I get along with well. Chenoya and I are not close. She is a bit different than me, but we get along. There are many people I like in our store, who I have either some repor with, or just get along with, amicably. Paul, Anthony to an extent, Jose, Max, Alli, Hazel, Rohan, Amitt, Crisha, Sebastian, Alex, Prabh, Amon, Reza too. These are like the other trees in the forsest who you don't sit by, but are there. They make the woods what they are. Then, out on the floor, there have been a whole swath of new people, some who I am with some form of repor and friendlienss. Charlote, Emma, Andre, Remil, Teresa, Dorothy, Janice, Lori even. And Jacob and Oliver, both who I'd consider a friend, alnog with Brielle. And there are many people who I am in tandum with, namely Heather, Alex, Samyransh, Susan and Renee, Bonafee, Rose, Michael, Arun, Krissy, Nick and Loveleen, Rafi, Felicia, Donna, Allie, Abby now, Joe too, and perhaps Debbie. I forgot to mention Will, who is a decent overnight guy who I jostle with a bit. Then there's dawn, who is quite nice. All these remarks center on what I am part of, what avenus of passing or engaged community I am invovled with. And there is Kathy from clothing, is who is very nice, and Max of course,. That is our life. We go to Yoga from time to time, and the group there is quite fine; though it centers around an indivudal practice. Similarly for the leisure center. I also feel a warming glow from Maple Ridge, and slightly different softness, as though cotton, from Pitt Meadows. Tis a lovely home.
What a turn of events since our days in Kamloops and Vancouver. Those days were very much on the up and ups of a new mentality, or at least siutation in life, whereby we were content and aware of our activity amidst duty. Moving north had a stiffling effect, as we continued being ourself, but to no real avail. And the shortcomings of being outside duty, in the room it afforded, seemed superfluous and short changed.
 We moved down in the prior fall with the full intent of moving to Vancouver. One thing that nothing can really overestimate is the difficulty in things. Think of how hard it was to move where we currently are. And appreciate how challenging and emotionally hard it is to see someone everyday who you wish to talk to, but feel ashamed and akward in amending not to do so; for you don't perceive them seeing you. It's quite tough. And we are back to be oursevels, in this near world. But much throws me astray.
 Something quite challnging to remark on, is the conditions which we were once in, and how them being more defined, yet limited, made for an oblige which was more or less successfull. This success was not so stable; as being at home always felt temporary. Twas hard to find peace at any rate. But making a motion elsewhere is very exposing; and you feel quite vulnerable and unsure; as were bound to when returing our scooter.
 The hardest part of the past six months has been this unavoidable sense that oru goal was to get past the current scenario. In moments where motion felt good, I felt it far easier to meet our stability, and feel no need, or haste to move. I feel far more content now, but its been uneven, espeically through the spring.
 This has made our itinerary and practice quite unwoven. And in part we've made some friends, or had some fun at any rate, and tried a few new things; which has a familiarizing effect. But were a bit off in our needed regards. I think it a suspect view that your goal is to do all you need as to do so as though free to do anything else. A resting principle on this is that anything within that freedom need not run contrary. It is a not entireyl well stated yet impinging view otherwise to say 'that such things may just not be available, beyond our care'.
 I think we forget, and perhaps it is inconsistency, which we rightfully pay for by our off amends, but so understandibly as such affairs are naturally fickle and ever developing, that our house is nice, our morning privy to softness and light; and the midday equally; as a good food or motion becomes ours, so a new insight, such as the combination of riding and walking. The afternoon has room for places nice and fun, and the evening and sunset too. Tis a land around me. And we feel fine, great in fact, and lavish in our writing, our reading, some study, Civ, games. Our stretching is in fact robust, though it tends to pillow over when we loose grip on the interfaces improvmenets, and in tandum with that, neccessary additions; such as the release of our hips and legs, and variety in our longer resting/sleep moments. Squats seem fair and leave me well. But I find that gaming, with Justin or Victor, is quite waring on me, and when things aren't so fufilling, I find myself unsure of things, as though withotu us looking so the compnany drifts away. They may be there still, as comrades at least. Tristan has been like this since his return. He is quite nice. I should respect him more, and the lads around me, as to gain some sight of how the lasses ought be viewed.
 Little advantages when it comes to food are always welcomed. Tomato and sunflowe remains the premiere breakfast; a small beefsteak is readily oppertune for our off days. Ice cream is delicious, but milk+banana+ dried fruit is comparable, and cheap as can be. We've been eating more as of late, but find ourselves somewhat lacking of food coming out of the afternoon. A salad, or light veg is the anwser. Our total consumption is important, and having some sense of what we eat on the whole is important. But eating regiarly, which is to say not going large distances without eating, is itself essential, and in mayn ways, so much as our posture in things is concerned, is all that is essential. At least, when can attest to how well things have been in years late. All were doing is remedying the source of pain in that approach, which is not eating routinely enough, due to a lack of laudible opitions. Tomato has helped in the morn, as has ice cream become a standard additjon to fruit. Dates and trailmix afford a mighty boost to our midday, and salads are a pre dinner finisher. Such regularity ought afford us the humble satiety of our grains --whereby our regularity suffices beyond some esteemed total.
I had this thought near the end of work yesterday, where I was simply coming up to Bella to ask her something. Eager but not earnest. I really was filing out the notion that we could speak to her about work. But she turned around and responded, 'please just leave me alone', as though she had felt like I was trying to approach her continuously. And I felt that there was some room for this idea, some merrit to her response, as though in our own mind we were in fact trying to be something.
 We've just been trapped on the other side of things, where we could be more ambivolent yet graceful, as we are with most other people. I was reading back to a few months ago, early June I think, and I had this thought that we were becoming amiable, and could just be. I was under the influence or impression that we were all well and buddy buddy, but that there was no animosity. Like I could trust her. But the issue with this is that I think you were taking for granted that you could be pleased with such relation, as though you could be happier than the sitaution sogguested. We can be happy about Joey for he speaks to me and I him. But when we say little to Bella and vice versa, what is there to be happy about. Yet were pleased with the siutation, as though there is some sense of positivity in that were no longer in the red. Yet nothing is there.
 And I find myself thinking htis and that, not wanting to make declarative statements. I just want to be. But she is like a piece of fabric which keeps coming loose, and so we never quite settle, as though we need not be afraid. Our thought is not dwelling on her very much. Yet there is this essential nervousness, or hesitancy, in running into her. It's as though were so free and away when outside of work, that we find it hard to act as though it were improbable that we'd run into her. And what would I say? There is just that loose fitting, which by all counts needs some understanding of how things have been, how we were and are in our own minds, and at that, what you really want. For we can relate something which happened yesterday, where we heard from Chloe, and were so riled with aniticpation. Yet I found myself thinking that what I really wanted was to be so drawn and certain about something I really believed in, and that would furnihs and align with the things I elsehwere care to have. This sort of notion allows the fabric to be where it is, and not get too fussed upon. It is like our computer fan, where knowing there may be an issue causes way more worry than the noise were hearing. And similarly with Bella. I have adjusted in our mind what it means to commune with her. For there is a weirdness, and oddity. The hardest and haziest perspective is one that simply says, 'if were not friends now, then so be it. Why act or try like its anythign else. Just behave and act according to this way'. At heart this is what I am going to do, even if it pulls on me in weird ways. For I find trouble in letting myself breathe and anticipate the folk around me. For is she part of that? Well no. Yet I find our own lack of happiness can feel somewhat bare in its attempt to find warmth and comfort in that true company; as though she makes it hard to be less yet feel supported. She makes it seem like that support isn't really there or real.
 Ultiamtley, something has happened, and something did happen. Beliefs are not secure or useful here, so mentioning what we percieve or reckon is her feeling or act in all of this is unreliable. But I know on my end that we broke our time together, and in being so earnest have perhaps made it hard to come together again. And the point is likely, or in part, that had we been more fine to accept things and be more indifferent, and settle in our amiability, that so would this be ok. Repor couldh have perhaps ensued. But we tried to do so intentfully, and crossed a boundry likely. It is weird that from 3 weeks in to 3 months later we've experienced what seems like hostility or amiability. I recall one morning where I was standing near the door and she came into the departemtna and said good morning. My heart tells me that this is a responsive but also intending recognition, as though to bear remarks and vanquish the awkwardness which comes from not regarding one another.
 There is just too much of a point to this. All my fault surely. She never wanted to be pulled into this. And again, strange and encumbant of me, but you think of that first day, and it was not so hard to concieve that our diversion of one another was neither a) absent and unpalpable, and b) not strictly from having asker her out. This feeling persists. And in part it may be on our end. And genuinley my resolve is not to sulk or ignore, nor be ambivolent. I must live. I need only regard her in ways that are fitting for how close we are. I think in part it is about considering how seen we are by her, and that as much as we are not, then we don't try and make her, or see her ourself. That is the abysss of neutrality here, where I am barred not by the past, as though I should, in a sense, 'move on', but were also not trying or afraid. Were just properly responding, and unperturbed, or at least requing very little steadyness, to be pleased with and accept what prompt there is. For I know in this case, that who else sees me is not affected, and who I see ought not change either.
It has been a strange few years. We left Vancouver, driving up the free way, a bit rainy. And I recall reaching home, seeing the lit front foyyer, mom to greet. me. Then we had our bed set and all was well. Those first few days were like any move, where so much was on your table, that your standards shifted. This compares to our current place, and getting onion rings. But once you come back to life, its like finsihing a sick day: back to things.
 It is strange thinking of last year, and that stretch of time playing Dragon's Dogma; how well we felt, how secure, how safe. And then when we decided to move, playing Baludrs gate felt swell.
 I have too little energy to share this, but we have known and abided this sense of requirment, as though the quality of life we wanted was in need of soemthing. And doing this in tandum with work, or duty, has been a dance of the most revealling sort. When were dancing well, we often find it is our duty which is great, but not our living. The precadent of work removes this preciousness of life, and so it doesn't feel wrong, just a bit heavier. But the norm at least. We tend to accept this, and see any life as an appreciated excess. When we concluded our choice to move, it felt as though that means for life was abound, and so the manner of work and things felt very light. There had always been this weird balance, as though this prospect was in conflict with the tenuous and private nature of being at home. Amending to work felt hard, as the way we'd do it in scuch scenario tended to come at the expnese of any sense or confidence in living. Having moved, I find a similar issue, though of a richer sort. FOr at home we never expected nor saw anything beyond ourselves. And so the simple avenue of being at home, but with work always coming, made for our living to either be swell and appreciated, or a bit flat, but something we had to deal with. Now, in being more free and focused, we are not merely ourselves, but rather more open and entwined with things. We have more control but don't use it. This has been nice and is great. It shows me though what I care for. As it may be easier if your doing something which is easy and well, so you don't mind any finer variation with that; as comes with friends. But were so reigned by the soverignty of our wisdom and heart, that this prospect is often unbalancing. We make room for it, but only so much; and one unfortunate effect, is that our limitations there don't persist the activity were doing together, and we loose that frequency. I have learned something about this, that this is not some weird or strange enditment on the relationship. Just a matter of fun. As it was with Matt, we just let go, never to speak again. Whereas with Justin, who has been simialr, I know that I can keep in touch, or call out of the blue. With Victor even, who was a play mate of mine for some time, has grown a bit apart in those respects; in part because of me, most likely in fact. But he is still there. There is part of me which appreciates this, and is not in the mood to return to that state where we expect such relation. Similar with Justin, where I just haven't felt like playing huge amounts of Ark. But were still there, dabbling. My personal investment in POE has naturally dropped, and so there isn't much bringing me back in. And we went to garden with Victor and Vienna and that was nice. Part of me wants to go do this more often. But it is more likely we'll just do it some time again.
What I find is less a convinving or reminding notion about ourselves, but a grateful one, one that brings sight to the cheer and promise that lie with me. How wonderful it's been going to Jordan; how great it will be to have Roast Broccoli and Potatoes tomorrow, fresh fruit to. But we forget this about ourselves, as though it were something in fact not so easy, or at least not provided by living in a approrpirate way. For I find that certain things ought be done; but this is only so because there seems indeluable things to do. We often find ourselves on the outskirts of our mind, seeing things which would be nice, things other people have. "Simialr to waking up in stupor, and feeling jealous of those who require this not." There is a rainbow road of difficulties we all face: one color we share, and if not, another. There is a hue in this or that way. And even if one is absent of things, or even present to great ones, so peace and flourishing lay as this prompting thing. And like one in a relationship, or with this or that, if your doing what is required of that, for that which is most holy and (in that) prompting, so we envy this not, but learn, appreciuate, respect, for we see our own.
 But we remind ourselves often of this fact, that of those who we may imagine as being well in this or that moment, that we remind ourselves that they have other things to do for we forget this very aspect in ourselves.
 And all I'll say, in this current day, where much is known, much is seen, and balance is relatively solid and properous, that so we lack that cruicial insight to the nature of life, what it tickets us with, 'for which we should check our emotions with'; and not so much what it offers, but rather what you in this context natrually adore. For we are moving creatures, who delight in and or lust towards things in the midst of either coin or chains. But there is a garment of gravity, so to speak, which positions us all; and all of inquiry's best comes when we can properly state the cause of such condition, but in that, with equal propiety remark upon this ever moving nature of us, but how it is not only served in balancing itself to such deeds, but is in fact better. For our life, however well or not it is, lacks the comforts of food, a bed even, and struggles in our attempts of this to feel seen by other people; for in our own efforts we don't give enough sight to people else. Our confusion in life, for which the end marks our young adulthood leading into a full state, has brought a effect born from the consquent inertia and or instability(and its pairing with privalege or ill-sight and wisdom), namely in expectation born from the still valor of our prior deeds. But we know not where it seems, and write about this incessantly. And it is because for an age our actions were not in service of our experience, which is the mark of all. And because of this we lived in a life of waiting, shortcuts, or change of mind. Fickle and vain indeed. But the root of our adultlife has grown a heart, and this acceptance of ourself and deed has coallesqed into a marvel of simple task and vibrant liberty.
 I think we merely lack defintion of our time in these riches. For I have so much to bring; but it is not for anything more than who I am. And this is quite the tricky element. For why do I care about the cosmogyn, or spectoscopy, or industrial governments and war memoirs? It is not because of someone else, but for no less a reason than I relish the sun, or the moon, or light pooring through the trees, or the music of Skyrim, or excitment of finally seeing GTA; or the satiety in Civ finally coming through, and the substance of filthy's games. These things remark life. And indeed, arousal and foreplay, festivites and banter, this are like concentrated forms of life. But they often take you out of the flow of things, and bring your mind right there. It is hard to be there is all I can say. For I know, as one who has not sacrified all there general time for such moments, that such moments are but part of that broader time. The point being that even if theyre there, the rest of time presumes; and there is just some false confidence or hope, ir weak wisdom, in seeing other things as well due to the effect of these conentrated moments. This serves only to look forward to these moments.
 Were getting distracted though. All that seems true is that we have an enormous amount to give. And this is not exlusive to anything. Our time, right now for instance, is quite engrossed with the new areas we can walk, and the time of daying being like sauces to try on these new base foods. I think that the notion of morality comes when we feel we have something to offer other people. But this feels like art in a way, in that your want to dance, or thought of doing so at least, comes from not being able to experience what you want now. Art is the process of making it easier. And morality is the same process but for caring. I am too much to remark this. But we know not the world, our life, our time, the manner of requirment which we often espouse but lack any grounding form of. Exercise and diet continue to allude me, and in part, do so based on the manner of our gait through life. Which feels a bit undieal, or unoccupied when it is not more bolted down. We may be ourselves amidst affiliations around me, but without these, we feel the effect of not being affiliated otherwise. Such is that feeling of Dragon's Dogma, that such thing brought such delight, and we were all to pleased to have treated the tasks of me: for this grass and sunshine, 'and far of light at the Checkpoint' was in esscence our liberty.
 All that feels present to me is doubt. Are people different than I once gleamed, and are in fact flawed, or just unsure of ourselves, the nature or, better yet, reality of our way; whether it is in fact something, 'does dearness exist'. Are these words of mine redeemable, and if so, what part of you is uncollected or ill-willed, as to make you seek and or each for things 'in order to make up for the lack of motion in such state'. Are we living a life, or are we hiding, confused, practical for our own sake but odd, obscure, less suited or compelling, for things which would surround me if I weren't doing so. If we have humoured and strode from the bounds of philosphy and reflection, is our attempt at this merely well in form, rather than wisdom? "Are we successful theives, glorious in our own time; and full of hope and distraction for such occupation is unwell, unfitting, outside of prosperous and communal realm?"
This slower momemt of mine reveals ceratin things, certain anxieties. I chalk it up to breaking up with your girlfriend, and doing something else to take it off your mind. But the problem remains, and you feel it when your occupation passes. I feel this way now about work. And it is not so much about Bella, but rather people on the whole. For I find myself there with everyone listed in that recent piece; but theyre not so much theyre with me. We meet in the middle; but if were not there, then there is nothing. And we've not much beside that. Where does the issue lie then? Is it in the matter of our community, that it is born from work. For we are not doing something we like together. We merely work together, and become affiliated, and wish well for one another. Is this different than going with a group to watch sunset. For it is elective, leisurely, and by that, simple and effective in it's own right. Whereas work feels like it needs to be place where we meet people. What are we doing otherwise. For it is not small manner that we may feel like we've outgrown the place. Yet in our striding moments, there is much to see, and we can appreciate things. I think were just a bit swole, on our own, cantankerous about things. Our want seems to come and go, and that affiliation with people changes from regularity to mere acquaintence. Trying to change this is odd.
 There was something about the end of last year that related to our final moments at Mariner, where we could accept the routine of our life, its challenge, its nature, our familiairty. Last year we merely amended to honor that, and make it more feasible by attempting to move. In the case of mariner we had moved; and with Simron even we were essentially at peace, ready to let things go. I was fine being ourself, for we had needs, were occupied, and were satisfied at that. Coming back to this store has been tough, as you left more or less loved but not in esscence known, and so upon returning, there was this standard of being welcomed and apart of things, yet still not known. And one phenomena which occurs is this sense of being a stranger; and how in mariner I could walk in without the hope or requirment to see or greet people. For life was all about in every persons way. Whereas at this store it feels like were often in a huddle, in tune. And I like that rythm; but sometimes I don't want to be there, and its as though there were a chorus that are suppose to join, but were unerved to sing. This overtness brings with it a sense of thsoe who don't wish me to join the chorus; or worse yet, those who are not in fact part of such composition, but instead have theyre own medledy, which we are not part of.
 One of the soul issues with feeling this stupor, or discomfort in our hips, or idleness in our mind, is that we find it hard to be comfortbale with things. For they feel like theyre passing us by, ceasing theyre oppertunity, forgetting us. It is hard to sit here and be like, 'in truth we are fine, we are known, we are seen, and that one or two people who perhaps see you less than you'd like, and at any rate someone other more than you feel fine with given how little your noticed, that this doesn't take away anything'. This is what we experience; and indeed, little flaps fiddle about, as the objects which they reflect don't go away. Our 'usedness to people' is what changes, and we feel more comfortable, known. Yet, in becoming more comfortable, there is less room or validty (and thus belief) in those measures which often rear themselves to overt being uncomfortable. Yet, without such measures, we notice deeper issues and uncertainities. It was easier last year to lean into this sense that we were present, that we could be. That when we went home, we could do and be as we please, and return to work able to do as we want. People have moved on in my mind; but that is in part because we are not in our right mind here. For they never were there; we were just ourselves enough to permitt some exholtion, some confidence, some place in things; as though we were boistrous in our sense of being known and appreciated, and could draw on it, assume it, eat from it. Wheereas now we are not so assumptive or consuming. We are only more gentle and proper in how were present. Yet this is quite hard, or at least revelaing, for when we are below this, which is quite easy to do, or harder than if we were buffed up through volition, then the reality of people becmoes present. Indeed, we'd felt this reality before, as though our actual state was recognixed, or inhabited, upon our moments of stupor,
Is it safe to say that running, for instance, requires a great deal of discipline. For the actiion itself, for most, may be something that you are in the habit of donig, or will yourself to do; but by all counts you just return to normal living. For me though, we go back to the floor; and being there can be quite taxing, when your doing things; and indeed, our stature may provide for this, but it is limited; and when running, which in its own right affords some stature, but rigor too as we have laborous work, that we are in some sense asked to ingratiate such effort, but respecting that its effects upon us are there. Not igrnoing your bodies natural rythm is paramount, as are definite stretches and or points of recovery most useful.
 We live a life where this sort of activity is heightened, and we partake in leisure and inquiry of the highest form. This is how life is in general, as we all work, but some of us have more leniance for play and occasion, and standards at that. Our simple life is one that is stable and just, but in doing what is needed, and what wonder this affords, so do we require proper amends; for the tasks, however small, become unstable, or at least damning; and our time piles up, 'as though the channels forward are clogged'.
 It feels safe to say that by years end we had this palcement, where what was needed of me was in harmony with how I wished to be, and we could focus on that. The gift was that in being so dear and focused on ourself, for we could not afford nor were interested to do so, given that lacking such would deflate the grounds for our vibrancy, we were also joined with a coallescence with people and task at work, and more or less justice at home. Weirdly, we found that in order to lean into this, we needed more ability to focus and have control. The news grated my mind, as porn does. And that sense of freedom we had when our parents weren't home was contrasted by the time when they were; where I had a sense and sight to do as was needed. But something changed when we moved. For we found ourself, whether in appeal or response, humouring the quieries of other people, and along with that, humouring our own. My dad asked me what I had done so far this year, and I responded, 'I tried yoga at Pitt, which I had forever felt off to do, started going to yoga and the gym and swimming at the rec center, which was no struggle, but became part of our habit, and we also went to restorative, which was no struggle but perhaps a sign then of being so calm in being outward. We went to a wine making party at Carries, and was in fact enthused to do so, and then got affiliated with those girls and joined a garden. We made friends with Victor, playing Path for some time, and recently hung out with him and Vienna, which I intiaited. Justin and I have also been talking for a month or so, and we've handled this quite well. Our interests may not directly align, but we can stay in touch, and play with one another when the time is right'. These are fine things, but remark my life being a bit unwell. For in none of these have we lost anything, but perhaps gained something which was not suited for what we were missing. I think of our motive for gardening and what stood out to me; I hungered after it in fact, getting Tara to take me there. For it gave me something to do, somewhere to go, and people to be apart of. Why this was needed is hard to say. For in part, I think our greatest struggle is that what we need and are graced by is benig consistent with ourselves. Making war with the forces which would have our liberty and vibrancy melt away. But this requires diligence, immediacy, fervent committment. And this can run contrary to what other people need. And the part I find most struggle with, is that if I reply to things, to do them as invited, I am more able to comply then I've ever been before. But I find myself afraid to return to myself. I find it easier in fact, but almost feel rude if I am not affording further intention. I almost want to forget about it and continune with ourselves. Perhaps the nature of our affiliations is so that without feeding into it, it slips away. That is the promise of a group, in that it stays, and allows you to take part, and mind your buisness elsewhere. It is not to be fair an issue with revealling our buisness, or saying no to further things because of what is fitting for that buisness. It is more about this self-doubt and conscientiousnes about not trying to take part in things. Like when we went to the painting thing, we sat there for 20 minutes, and was ready to go, as we had dinner and sleep to get to. I felt fine leaving, but it was weird in a way, like I had to make an effort to get out of there. In part it is about the people your around. People who you'd share your health concerns, your time with yoga and swimming, and how this orients your routine, sleeping well in general. This is a form of you that your baser interets reflects and can be expressed in communion with other people. For so long we've felt like we were living with a disguise; I feel this way when I merely want to have some trail mix, or worse yet, do upward dog. I found the moment to do it, but I am not open or enstated about it otherwise. Which is perhaps a token of how hard things are, that I find some things neccessary, as one does with eating breakfast, or something at all, but along with that, there are just things I want to do. It is not essential that we stretch our arms, but it is so beneficial and invigorating; and the natural force of work makes this so desired. But its weird, and not every situation is warm and welcoming. It is like squating; it would be odd to just do it. But again, if you were excited about it and showed your reasno why, or that you cared, I am sure people wouldn't mind. But it is hard to make such things knonw. This is what I mean yesterday by Art being that which faciliates what you cannot so easily express. I have always found there is room to be yourself, but that it can get a little overhwelming. As its not an issue that I cant downward dog in the department, and I have to tactifulyl do it in the washroom. That is an odd thing we prefer to do. But that we eat well or swim or do yoga or sleep well, these are things which are reminsincent of our general princiuples, and can aid in directing other peopels view of you, and thus how comfortable you are in being who you are. That you need this, want that, are worried about this or the other.
 Truth be told I did not like talking with Tara anymore. She is an older lady, a little crass and foolish. And our centering factor of the garden was whithered by carry not being invovled. So I just lost interest. But think of Justin. We responded to playing Ark on Sunday with admittence, for he asked, and so be it. But we need not change for this. Ask when you want, and if he's not available, then either he will ask at some point, or the affiliation will end. But were still friendfs. For you may call him still, despite him being busy, and talk and this or that. Same thing with Victor. When something else comes up we'll be bonded again. But were still friends. Just like me and Tristan.
 My movement regime is complicated but rather clear. We know we need a hip and upper body release. Period. We also know that we need a stretch for these, like hip openers and corked hand twist. We need long resting positions, for sleep namely, with allowance for prone and supine focus. And we need lunging practice. Deep squating and boat are critical poses that afford so much promise, that our ability to make guided practices just for them is a boon comparable to 'riding somewhere to walk'. I find our chaturange and standing are a bit off; I know not how to fold, nor have I ever been able to do downward dog. Regularly doing these allows us to experiement and become familiar. But our method has never afforded much maintence. The notion of pracitce has come up, and indeed, for 2 months now it has given me an evident strenght and stability at work. Yet were falling apart, and I can feel our neck starting to crumple, and our hips feeling quite tight. I feel the greatest advent in our life is to partake in running, or natural activity. Pushups, pullups and squats are perhaps useful in that they afford some rigor, for which the labors of our work require. But limberness there often affords what you seek. And such strenght training is quick to overshadow our lifting prioritiy; which only has me weighing down. Indeed, the limit of relying on such activity is in offering grace through the day. It is not about saying no, nor being unadaptable, but having the sight and intent for a path during your day; in that there will be htings to do. It is nice to have all this free time, given our time on our own, and to think and heed all things around; but this makes the fluidity of that natural path rather diffuse, which can leave you feeling worn and reserved --as though you anticipate more to come. This matter has brought us to seek things in life which would be fufilling and cooperative, or at least fitting, for such priority and sight of mine. There isn't folly in this, but its uneccessary. You may be as you believe in now. We'll make friends with people when it is truly called for, but not out of fear of being friends no longer --or affiliated. I think it time we return to that ripest of states; one which fell by the wayside when we errored early this year. Bring yourself under this context to place which in abscence, makes you sour and reclused; nor should the contrary response of being eager and outoging make up for this. Bring yourself with all your might, proper in candor, but not only in the kindness of such custom but in the duty, the order, the respect. Let no one shove you off from this, or make them selves impressionable as though they are or that you should be. Life is just waiting otherwise, or it is rich in things that can be suckled on till dry, or tended to with the promise of expectation, yet ignorance in what it takes to 'invigorate that'. Many a couple has been in love then married, only to find that without nurturing the love, that the indefinnte offer is dry.
I make the small point that our current tenure at work has been one where were full of disguises. And as this cover falls off, it is moreso frmo our acceptance of things, and letting the work around me enclose me a little. The reason to work, as though we were a prisoner, adjusts what I expect. Whereas before we found we were doing all these odd things to keep our head afloat, above the chains so to speak. But, as the year went on, and these thoughts came aboot, we found that this position was not so inhospitable, and actually quite rewarding. We still held our life, but let the peak of it slacken, while we snuggled into our work. The committment to this bore us a feeling we had felt at other times, namely, that if we were to live right and well, we needed to let go of our tight grip on things, and allow for time to move on, and thus principle ensure; rather than control and preperation. But our ability to be so naturally principled felt a challenged, as our home felt like it had borders and demands placed upon me; things that just made it hard to be.
I just don't know how she sees me. If there is indifference, or in part a sensitivty, as though she doesn't mind me or care, but the thought of me being kind to her is unacceptable. In truth, this is not the case with most people. For those who we wish to, like Hazel of all people, we notice ourselves being off, and how unwelcomed or neccessary this is. But someone like Angel, who I realize were a bit too kind to, this does not bother me. So I slow down there, and can afford to. I don't want to be afraid to see her. Not to endear her or make a connection, but to pass by, not feel like we are forbid from noticing what she says or does. She is quite outspoken in any case. Part of this is about our own heart not being so swayed or swooned. In part time just must go on, and indeed, had this been our approach prior, there would not be this elephant hanging above us, forcing what is for me any real sense or confidence that amiability can create affiliation. The toil is in looking at her from a point where we are, but with the knowledge that things can not so easily move further. The impetus then is to not look at all. Which is strange. For we may feel eager with people else. Wait for that moment which always comes, and fretter not if it doesn't, or passes. Reach not for it, lurk not for it. Just know that you can be as is needed when this most open of moments is satisfied. For much of my reserve in this comes from times past those moments where I lean too far in. Let it be enough for us, for that root ought be there. Which is all we want: not this or that, or her, but to be there. It is hard when when things are already in motion.
What is the gift of virtue? What are we given for being, as it were, adult, or definite, deliberate. We have abandonded any sense of ignoring rules; and by all counts ,when you tally the hours and days, our life has been fine. But there is a pitch to it, a disguise, and we are a bit ill placed in things, for we do not know enoughb about ourselves, nor feel so acquited with other people. Time creates familiarity, and you are happy to be as you are, not overly seeking, not overly afraid, but merely seen, known, welcomed. And that is all good by most accounts. Yet were prone to feel lacking, as in those quieter, or staler moments, where the things which feel they could be present if we werent so stingy, or adult, came to pass. Indeed, we've had wrong, or unjust deliberations about things that would ease our time and offer comfort for our adult way. Yet such way felt too centered on itself, and by that, what was being served was more or less a progressing rather than steady state.
=======
Tis an age which has gone past since a new book has begun.
 We began this prior one in Vancouver, which feels both near and far ago. Winter writings definitely laid the ground for it, but the fruits began to blossom during the coming spring.
 Through the age past we wrote ferviously, during the discourses, the histories and acceptance.
 Now a new book has begun, charactized best by us becomnig a man, and now becoming me.
 Who is it we are really? What positions and aims would we accept from the things within them, rather than without. What advantage do we have, virtues to enlight. Where may our foundations grow.
The first of these topics is virtue, for she marbles us in such delight, yet mingles and sways in delicate mystery.
 Foremost is the language used to describe her. For most words reflect something definite or categorical. "Of this is those." That or it's some kind of property, a way it's being. But this latter does not have the fairest acess to properties of motion, or relation between things. And that's what virtue is.
 For in life we are tasked with things, neccessarily and for all things benefit. But we often overlook these demands and focus on the goal, the fruit and the end. And this belies perhaps a warranted confidence and comfortable desire. But it does not hold virtue. What she is comes down to an awareness and submision to the prescence of task, and the more or less accepting manner of amendment, whereby our attending to such task is more or less sufficient for us to be pleased, and by that focused. The ends that come out are more like buds and droppings of a continous harvest. Virtue is for life: goals are for stopping.
 There is the manner of love then, which compliments, or in some cases vanguards virtue, as her upper end; or comes as an effect from a more defined rear virtue --who we may consider in isolation. At any rate, this amiability to task, the appreciation of it, the merry, in the suppleness and succeeding effect, lies a cloud of delight and cheer, and in that care and awe. I once mentioend this in terms of marks, whereby things in such a state would stand out to you and beckon you forth. Perhaps it is still suited. The difference, is that via virtue, our draw is not only born from grounds bade from duty and ease, but contained to that. "It is not so that we reach a point of stability and cheer, see the stars, then fly to them."
 Something I'm wondering is whhy certain things draw you. And whether there is a manner of something being drawn to you. We often find ourselves light and gleeful, for so many scents excite our mind. Yet, certain things pass by, unaware of me, and not exactly presenting themselves to me as to be drawn. Two things have occured in this. One, is I realized that I may form, and at any rate supply, our own love, to anybody and anything. For the love of a woman may have no bounds; and not all open themselves to this. Nor is it entirely proper, given the lenght of such mingling. "None act in so full out ways, only to then leave. The regard though for duration keeps the doors more or less shut less a key is had or invitation granted. Otherwise all would encourage everyone to love them openly and impulsively --for it'd be expected that they just go, thereby warranting a low standard. But committment and stay is the norm, and so not everyone and everything and every moment will do." Love may still occur. Being personal is like this, being near and present. But then lies the wish to be seen and cared for. And in part I don't know why. Is it because it opens you up to love? The pleasure is not just; it's but a moment. As we walk around, we feel this grin, and a good one when we consider the thing invoking this, about others seeing me, being impressed, admiring me, wanting me, seeing me for good and great. "I feel like I'm shining." Why is this exciting. For I admitt, when I walk through a crowd I often feel nervous, like everyone is looking at me, either down, or as though I'm a mystery. That, or I'm chest up, being noticed, people saying, 'oh my'. And glory is merely this feeling, but bridled upon your propiety rather than charm. Yet, I do not actually want anyone to speak to me. I don't want a crowd, or to sign autographs; I care not for theyre time and attneiton. I just want to be thought of.
 And I belive it all comes down to the matter of honor and duty. Which is to say, virtuous oblige to tasks, rather than succumbed ones, where relief and ill-merry is pursued. Wishing to be noticed comes from an imbalance, or at least untuned time of that former manner. For in virtue, who once perked up her head, showing me the green in her way, held me there, and through time and content, disposed me to her conduct and wares. In growing though, you experience often times where you are under the scalpel (so to speak), but lack the footing, or at least heart, to be so fortuitous and ample, and thereby feel beckoned to relief. "I am right though, in my suffering; the path is just. People should look at me. They know where I've come from and am returning to." Such is the mind for glory. Or, "man, those people, they don't notice me, and I'm doing so well while theyre not." Such is the mind of a cynic; who is not wrong, but patronizes others because he is alone. In my experience this came from me knowing more about virtue than deed; and thus upon the richest of successes, not truly having won.
 And then there is that peak of becomnig a man, whereby the slips and turns of that result in a more or less squicning and or cringing stability; as though we know about virtue and her ways, stand by our rules, and are aware of our trouble; for which we concive nor invent some remedy, but stay with the trouble, breathe, endure. Moreover, do we adapt, and rise above the conduct we once thought fit: we give credence to the hurdles around me. Much of youth is defined by such hurdles being a frustration, as though 'man, haven't we won yet! I just want to get over the things I have to do so I can pursue what I want'.
Being a man, oh how it can get drowned in action. And much of what I see is in relying on our manhood, and more or less testafying it; not putting other things up on a hill, as though theyre required. It seems better to look at them as things which would be nice and supportive while you continue to grown and maintain. Then there's those things which flow naturally, such as sums, as though fruits and or makings of a firm and steady state.
Hooey, its been quite a day, a month, a year even. The age it seems is not even faded.
 I see, foremost, that what I want, see, believe in, is a life, literally. Looking at something ahead, being exicted, fretting over something even, this are states, conditions, orbits around things, rather than a life, a flow, a continuity, a direction of progress, endurance and felicity.
 This is what I've done for 10 years. But the rules have changed. At least, our view of conditions has. As we at one moment or the other thought home life was suited for us, and that the temporary nature of it was permitted. We balanced this untenuableness out, and frustration over it not being so, by seeing what our home life would make as something prospective. "Let me be here permanently and good will naturally follow." The motive was pure, as I just wanted to live freely. Not at home neccessarily, as our dreams profressed, but free.
 times are different though. Such a state is not tenuable, nor adventageous, for productivity or happiness. What has come about though is that our view is different, our aim, our tilt. It is not for those ends of freedom: as though such times would procure something sustaining and wortwhile. It is more in line with our attitude during Superstore, where we thoguht, 'why we want those ends is so our freedom may truly be; rather than a semester. But, working provides that. It always felt so poor and drowning, but no longer. Its sustainable and our goods are enough. Epictetus was right, as was I'.
 This has been the greatest change to our days, this slope downwards to real things, real people, real potential. But the mark of manhood is in ironing out all things that bring you away from such acceptence, and thereby stabily applying your mind and might to things further abound. Trying new activity, putting yourself out there, merely partaking in someones company and friendship.
 By all accounts we are a man. But not with wind in our sails, nor a firm beat in our heart. It is as if the model is well carved and true, yet the apolstry on it is droopnig and torn. The peace that would mark us being a man gets turned into regret and longing, jealousy too. And we overlook the path out of this for seomthing of reduction, as to invalidate our syymptoms by remarking upon theyre disproprition. "As though one were sick and hallucinating, but in that, sought to apply reason to theyre confusion and fright, rather than adjust theyre view so it was innately stable: whereby the sights were something you could accept."
 Where such peace comes from is not what is to be instilled and insisted, but rather, what is bringing such piece away. For we already are, in our choices and principles. "Only when theyre off do we enforce them, making up for what is in slack." The proper aid is one where we simply speak modestly about that which needs tightnening or to be brought back into fruition. Some things could use our help more or less. But its like a flipper that has a nail in it. Don't worry about making the flipper go, it inherently does. Remove the nail and its fluttery flips will become firm ones. And you know what those are like.
 Where our mind and inquiry should go is into those fruits, prmomsies, ideas, and or commiserries, that naturally sprout from us or strike our mind in our peaceful state. Our proper pace that is. This is where formation is needed, and indeed, worms out the rot from past idlness. It also removes some confusion, whereby in the best of moments we feel like we have no sight of things; or what we do see is believed to be false. Put some real color and form into things.
 Indeed, one fair insight into all of this, is that the flourishing in life is not so that you may pursue this or reach that, but that you have things around your proper pace. If, in your peace and succour, you see some thing far away, may you shed light on it, bring it close, ready yourself and soften its groove, 'so upon our arrival we fit', all while keeping our pace.
 Perhaps it is our nature as one so endowed and enriched by the matter of pace to not so easily fit with others. For they have theyre own pace, or lack theyre of. And this is fine, and marks the ways of more or less all people. But it creates community though; as though a savanah of buffalo, each going here and there, in theyre groups, with theyre crowds, but amongst one another; interfering not, keeping things on the whole safe, and otherwise respecting the fact that we all share this drive and deed to be on pace. This is reflected in nods while passing by. "Enjoy your own day while I continue with mine." Having my day be mine feels respected and permitted by me and all.
All that being said, where there is tightness in our groin. Not our mind, though the idea of work is something overhwelming and depleting. But our life is slacking due to our lack of running. Simple. And this is so out of worry and fear, and the energy we have to balance that out. Doubt creeps in, and then inertia.
 The isse is not the floor. We've been sitting on it for 8 years now and these issues were not always there. What has happened though is that we actually act like a kid who has homework or needs to go to bed but wants to game instead. Were like that, whereupon our training, we play the whole day. This isn't wrong, and it's not so much that miss other things we have to do; its merely so that given how much we train, the quality of it, that then playing throughout the day demands so much more. And we often don't do that, simply out of excess or lapse in timing, so we bear the load of having worked but then continued being active all day. There tends not to be an issue if we workout and do nothing.
 It is like food early in the age, where it was challenging so we gave it time and attention, and everything else was like a blessing. Now, we are so good in principle that we don't handle it deliberately with care. But with the re-introduction of work, the more suited training for our activity rather than heavy eating or insecurity, that we actually haven't earned the amount of activity we do. At least, inconsistency occurs and we respond in vulgar. For there is an amount given to us that we may use, in activity. But we've in the year or so prior made the mistake of doing more than this, not resting or pausing. In part something easy to do is what is suited, yet we don't have much which is satisfiyng on that account.
 Our life has to submitt to the things needed of, and find balances and regularity to sustain that, and otherwsie change, or face the ware and tare.
 Running is essential. Were not doing though for it puts us under load, and we feel unsure otherwise. One way of looking at it, is that our activity is not easy, and so going under load then returning to activity has consqeunces if were elsewhere ill-fit, namely our recovery, finer training and eating. Chores, work and other mess are included.
 This is actually a very live account of us, in that running is what puts us under load. Work does by nature; but it also is like a God damning you and you receive but a small scar. And indeed, this is incorporated in things, and accepted unconditionally, while running is something we may shy away from out of whithery fear.
 Stability comes to question. For eating is not trial, nor stretching for the most part. But in one you have the resoruce requirment, and thereby preperation on top of that, while the other has more confusion and dissaray. Running comes naturally as something clear. Working out had the opposite effect, in that it felt so under load that we felt confused at how much we should allow ourself to do.
 Which brings up a critical question? What do you need? I can speak to what would be useful and advantageous. But, our insecurity is not a real factor, as it only comes from not doing anything, and feeling the sure effect from that, but true sight of you doing nothing. That's all it is. Motion makes such things fine. There is the routine of work, and the every pressing nature of it, and riddance of ware. This speaks to a limit in terms of duty and custom. For I truly wish to write, see Baker in the blue. I do. But this come painstakingly and in contrast to other neccessary things, like work; and so we feel poor and waiting. Yet, our view on work is not a solem one, nor a thing of greif or frustration. I understand its title, it's worth, the good in it, the trouble to exepect and effort required; I also see what weight can be alleivated by removing poor choices, and how a familiarity of this success breathes a steady experience into work. What occurs is the most wonderufl of things: peace. For in work, its obligation is sourced from the nature of things, in that we are animals, and civilized one's who've formed an economy, whereby our present work-type is bound. But this deed upon is made like our need of breathe. We usually take this as something which may be absent. But what about food on your table? This is something that could be missing, but is something we enjoy also. But it surrounds this base of life, that such thing is needed. And having it steadily makes you entirely sure. Some, in this age, or any other, bank theyre satiety on things farther and bound. While a man may truly be happy if is belly is full and with a roof over his head, and that these things are by fortune and equity, or agreeable effort, owned. You may really breathe then, for danger is not at your door, nor begrudgement of this neccessary thing. "I am glad that this shark will not reach men; I am less pleased by the enormous effort to stop him so. But I am painfully aware, or at least inately tuned, to attend to the danger that would be if I stopped. For which I am bound." And the coals of life simmer upon this idea, whereby we loose not our chains but our impingement by them. "Less one be given theyre needs permanetly, or the need go's away."
I sit here sometimes, having more or less done what I need to do, but doing anything more feels waring. Yet, I question whether something easier could be had. Games feel like this, as do shows, or vids. But it is kinds of these that are fitting, in that theyre new, or easy to digest. I don't feel like watching Thrones now, and watching OWl just feels a bit too passive. We wander a bit, thinking that we might have a friend, or somewhere to go. And this feeling seems more about our abscence rather than merrit. For looking at our life, it is most important that we have one. And there are neccessary and desired forces that form this. And indeed, when i'm in such state, and remembering and seeing ahead at that, I am pleased, and feel both right and honored to be such way. Much gleams ahead. And indeed, I see that what is avaialble is a future or mean where we make friends of our own. For we in our shortened freedom could not really be ourself; yet did not compramise either, or seek what was available. I wish to and find no folly in keeping to ourself: but we must be just. It allows us to be so. And time has not really been where that could be. And indeed, when I think of things easy, things which gave more life during our quiet and solemn times, I don't see much near. Nor do I humour availability that gets embalmed due to our want but not realistically. We expect to much, are aware too little.
 So it is a balance, in saying that life may offer me such things, for all theyre pleasing and wanted ways. And fitting of such. But so is our actual life the center of our harvest. It is not to say, 'gather those fruits and friends or potential won't be sought'. We just wont seek it with haste or parchedness, nor loose our mind as to the prescence of such things now: motion removes doubts and follly.
 Looking back at today, I saw such great gentleness and peace in doing a bird session, or adrian's chill. I see that yoga is not some monumental thing, but akin to gaming. There is a motive of good, for form and rehabilitation. But it comes through like walking, in that it is fair and needed, but naturally sought and brought. More or less. Yoga is similar. There is not always something to do. I feel, for one, that we have too much stuff already that is not really serving us; overloaded, unorgainzed. Remove it all. Peace is all we seek. Something easy, in the morning. It need not be anything but what you want. Sometimes there are higher interests, and holds and warrior, core even, stand out as the things we seek. Find those. But cater to your easier interests, for the morning, mere standing, recvoery and mid day sleep. Just listening to someone while you lay back and breathe is what our day needs sometime. I think we often make the mistake of directing our self and organiznig based on body parts or pose type. When in reality it's all the same. Its more about the manner of training, be it flow or resting. Chill is a great example, as you merely sit, side, then lay back, knees to the side and cobbler. This may be what you want after work, or you may want something more upright and flowing. Freeman's standing sequence is a great example, as your just on your toes a bit, firey, and generating warmth and breathing, While Adrian's brain power is more calm and easy.
Writing doesn't always benefit from centering on one point and trying to make sense of it. It os more often that we beenfit from speaking of real things, and using such happenings to highlight that more pointed thought in our mind.
 For starters, when I saw Bella today, or dealt with the grief and emotion that has become familiar to me these past few months, I realized, or felt at least, this room for positivity and ease. But, similar to that instance in materialism, and our momentary questioning of it, 'in our delighting in this', that such feeling went away, that so in our postive view, I could see a demand on me, or at least a inert sensation that ran contrast to this cease of worry; namely, that our wellness was of the matter, and that by being pleased for her and not minding her leaving our sight and mind, that so did our own life become highlighted.
 Naturally perhaps there is an impermance to this. Though, one feeling that just occured was that of our squinting and stiff state; whereby, that scolindg notion of doing things with other people was not in fact so pleasing; for just as I overt from scootering or playing, or anything, because were in a more or less down and recoverying state, that we don't in fact want to do those things which we often find ourselves feeling guilty of, that our interest or potential to do so is off; when in fact, it is merely we who are sat outside the winds of activity; for which the one's we truly care about are absent. And this is fine. And my point is that the imperamance of our life is fine to. Yet, we feel off. Which, in all effective manner, remarks the terrain of our heart and soul: our feelings and understanding. And by that, some feelings are exaggerated, or over-tuned. Such as in the case of our feeling for Bella; when in truth, our cooperative and cheery delight was enough. But we got sucked in.
 And so in all things, I find that remarking the past and defining whatever is (now), tidies up the lands in our mind, and affords a) less sensitvity to heightened impressions or impusle, and b) tends to soften, and over time lessen, the matter of such volitions. "To which, we are with less expenses and a bigger purse: able and less obliged."
 Oddly, I found much satisfaction talking with Amon. Something about her was respectable. And indeed, I found that in her expression, there was less assuming, and not something overly projecting yet vain. I find in younger people this is often how we receive theyre expressions; yet it is quite over-tuned. And our own volition can create such sensitivity (from our lack). Such feeling, of being in fair motion, and by that, not so struck or beckoned to other people, but happily indifferent and collected, in commradery to; such is so nice.
 My life is truly one of grand design, yet mightily suttle. The truth is that all the things which spring up our god like ways, are in fact so stouty and pure, that we sit with them, at ease and soothed. Theyre nature propels me and satiates me to a point where theyre brevity is not produced. Theyre grandness has me pleased. But we often, in the past least, been subbject to theyre extent during times of ware and stillness. For we have not else to do. Indeed, our adult life has pronged itself under this remark, as this life we have, gazing at the clouds, breathing in the sights of wind and flowers, is very much mine, and in most times, enjoyed with none but our own company. Qualififying this, as though it were reasonable and enough, is a scent that lingers from those days prior to that realization mentioned. Recreation is a pure form of this. I wish to find and seek more social and or creative forms of this. Some recreation would be nice, be it yoga or soccer.
Just saying 'there are two things on my mind' brings me into a twirl. Too squinted are my eyes, too narrow is my sight. To write though is to lay things down; it becomes easier.
 One thing, if I can even form this thought, is to the inevitable nature which appeals to us, yet seems somewhat hollow when assessed. Does your life change? Expectation is built on promise and probability, and too small matters or the deepest of things, so that route lay. But shouldn't it become of us to be steady in these matters, and not go in so eager, nor premature as to the actual effort and confidence to show up and be? Moreover, to let things go, and have the interactions come about in theyre natural rythm, balancing with your own rythms? That is the fundmenetal point, and take away from all things commonyl social; that they form routines, familiarirty, and general friendship. I think what we want, in a reasonable sense, is to make a friend, feel knnown, connect with people who not only share some semblance of value, attitude and spirit, but also interests too. Moroever, they are apt to be people who I actually like. One reason I've never wanted to smoke with certain people is that I just don't like them. Josh at any rate, depsite his more costly manners, was still someone I enjoyed smoking with. So going out with people, to dinner, for frivolity, for a day, let it be some I like. But my position on the matter is that such folk have to be met. The motive to be online seems more serving for industry and community, but not real connection; as your to be drawn out in infamy or notoeriety, 'marking yourself to be seen'.
