But, for such personal things, where I fit and meaning is had, I take the position, or sit with the stance, that it has to be sought, and primarily through meetups. No different than online being the spring for dating. Yoga, to be clear, is not this substantively, but is rather a mixture of spirit and recreation. Similae to work, time may go, and this or that form of friendship may take. But alas, it is meetups, or things alike, where the whits and whims found in the spirits of college occur; where discussion and activity prioritize themselves with certain manners and motions; and in advertising themselves as such, issue your interest.
 Something that comes to mind is the time of day. For what I see, in Vancouver, is a very nice morning, or early afternoon following work, in the spring. That area is very intriciate (and vast in being such), and so having that spark of allivation from work points you in all manner of directions. And I see perhaps a friend, but more than likely a thing in the evening. To come home, rest, see it forward. And indeed, the selection is ripe, rather than ill-grooved. There is indeed this kind of attitude, in the same manner as youtube; whereby that has it's direct and pulpable means, but require effort and committment nonetheless. Elective actions are within this group. And indeed, that attidue is one of approahc, or method, but so our mentality lies, in that we expect properly, keep our head high as to be drawn, but not overly eager, nor blatant. Try and take the heart of things, and let the worth of it on that whole carry you towards and through; relations happen naturally; be it in this or that matter; those more meaningfull come because someone is the right fit. We ought, to wrap this up, in supporting this elective aim, deepen our life in a way whereby we can well be oruselves. The balance and harmony of it in check, moving forward, nothing sagging. That is all you really can do, in your principle life. Of which work, leisure and practice wind. In many ways these elemnents require foritification and nourishment, while those elective ones require more or less steadyness, as to put yourself out there and accept what occurs. This is how our work is in some sense, which brings up the second thing on my mnid. Namely, that we may approach things in a problematic way, where we attribute ours and others life as being conditioned and set; and in that we prioritize the needed efforts but also dear experience: our life as it were. But along this obligate line. Others may be seen to have dinners, or go out on weekends, or even have lunches or convos at work together. But the deed is writ and submitts all these to it; and it keeps on and squeezes out all sense of jealousy or elatement. "For the deed continues on." And my life is tenured as to fit and be sprung by such action. The other way of seeing things is without problems, whereby your own efforts and deeds are accepted as part of your nature, and given leave to be, since they are not elected but more or less custom. So we may be ourselves with those who are nothing like us, for we already are. this manner of life often creates desires which are hard to grasp, for they reflect little of how other people are; in that, they are a)different, and b) not so undisposed. In the former approach this doesn't matter to me, for we are attending to our own differensts, and living our life as is right and wanting around it. But if our own differences don't matter, and were tranquil, then we feel ourselves wafting into the complexion of other people. "For we so easily see all and any of theyre brighter sides." And in many ways this is a very present and breathing expeirence, and one that has no real fault except for history; whereby our natural gait doesn't create such ease within our duties: custom and habit don't suffice, or vice wiggles in. And indeed, in these moments, where we've more or less let ourselves be vulnerable to like, but then feel like were getting deported, 'back to boarding school, to ship up', we feel like were leaving, and thus rustle ourselves back in. But with a sort of affection that was merely our own, sparked by what we saw, but from our point of view. The moral of this, as found with Bella, is that you could just be yourself, and that would have been enough. Again, vice is waiting for a slip, as our tender satisfaction was not in fact the only real motive, or compulsion ready to be raised. Alas, history broke the state, and purity had to resume some other day. Much foolishness and greed gets conjured in this broken moments; as though peace will not be found again. But it will always, and has mind you. There is some perspective though, that in many ways there is an over-infatuation, or at least over-affectioante state, which your peace seeps into; for you let go of the reigns, and by virtue of the calmenss around, allow your tranquility to direct your motion. Yet duty remains, vice lingers, and satisfaction is not so easy to find. That is why you seek someone, to be near them. But this is hard to do. And indeed, awkwardness is the opposite of the right state, for nothing open nor steady can be procurred. But it just seems that our life being so, but with the more genuine mindest that 'of those who excite me or draw affection, that it is merely so', that rather than feel free to drift into that, but to no likely end and at risk of folly, that we speak as we would, but not with much stake in mind. Our understanding of such satiety confines me to the limits and accesibility of that. Which I find, in admitting, puts our life in persepctive, and draws both the deed of it upfront, so as not to take our ball of the prize; but also, with more meaning and pace we make, as our manner of being so attentive and personal is not a limiting factor to who we may be genial towards. And I believe truyl, that rather than succumb to the parsimonous potential or foolish expectation of meaning coming from any which way, that you keep your form, ready your favor, and initiate yourself into social and creative avenues which would fit you personally. These are not things you come across or are privy to by chance relation, but things you find, and invovle yourself with out of some mixture of initiative but like also. That practical philosophy group spoke to me on all levels: the subject paired the elemetns of group disucssion, and it all being organized as such. May petals of truth fall on your dreams, whereby that evening sight of a sun setting in Vancouver, be brought forth into reality not because there is a sun, but because there is somewhere your going: the weather and tidings of which may be noticed then.
It is not right to say that our life is our own, but rather, that life is what it is, and for those who go off and do nice things, or even compell me, be it as I or someone else, that so the road of life lay, and we are always driving. It can not be understated enough the challenge of work, and how it plays on your mentality, as to be pleased with what you have, but moreover, have focus of what is at hand and presnet, rather than what is ahead. History has shown us a flawed hand here, but a natural one. Everyone grows up, and falls and learns, and so has our time in the full part of life been just like this. I was thinking today of an essential feeling, though it's quality is lost. But it had something to do (I wish it were with me) with my manner of liking, pleausre and interest, and how it was not by some rule but some strong fashion; as though we were not dissauded from duty nor bent towards lust and elation, but rather steady wonder and light. I never migrated away from this. Even in our moments of absence, where I saw others invovled and arranged with people, and I thought of the same; who I'd be with, how we'd all relate. But strenght came to fashion; centering on me primarily as our abscence in life procurred. And indeed, this grew our manner of experience whereupon most people left and there was not much but me. We merely heightened what once had so much company, or at least finer tidings amidst our leisure. Little was there, or what was held toil and by that discontent. There was no shortness of worry and shame, as though our experience, however just, was allowed. This all centered on the disturbance of work, in its approach and experience; and the insolidity that its cease would bring, 'to which the turn from freedom back to approach came'. I am mispresenting this sense of shame; for doing as I needed always gave me leave to do as I want; it was just that the matter of want was disturbed by what I had to do. And given that trouble, the contempt felt came from us trying to acquiesce to that trouble, and later on improve the good around (to make it worthwhile). In a word, respect for labor felt unremarkable nor worthy of respect. Hard to share still. And it comes down to that essential feeling, of mighty peace and awe. Easy it was as a child, for we were raised well, as were we good in ourselves. That same pleasure and cool you got from eating well following a practice, gave wamrth and reason to our way. The way eroded though upon our emotional dissaray during graduation, and our reckless disenfranchisment from our mom and dad. Indeed, we had not the calm or novel stability to go through college, nor that of a job. Strange indeed that we became so personal. Yet, it was our wellness that procurred this, as in being so we were proper and welcomed at home. Only as time went on did expectation grow. And indeed, our own comfort in being as we were grew fundemental, and our natural want extended outside our parents bounds. Work felt essential, and was something we dealt with; and upon its mundanity we moved, which afforded it's own satiety. Yet, in that moment, we quickly realized that we were not free, and that work would continue. We felt this sense of freedom, being on our own, yet it was as though the leash were lengthened: still we were chained. And this more or less lead to a moment of aimlessness. We felt not bad, as we were stbale, but we were not happy. Young and novel motions oft create with them a sense of progression and outlook ahead. But as reality settled, or what we in fact werre set for was reached, we felt still. Without an end we turned to gratuity. And this felt unsatisfying, nor made work tolerable. So we cultivated ourself, and as it were, the view of happiness. This didn't stop our choices being made as to remove that burden of work. But so in this the road to propiety lay. For we fidgeted here and htere, to no real acclaim nor tolerance. And we were asked to return to work, no questions asked. And I fought this, finding it unneccessary. The present was good enough, stable, and in the back of my mind, promising. But alas, we submitted, and were employed. Here, it felt as though this mode we were in had no compramise, barring a return to a 'step by step' progression, 'where nature and whit carved the way'. This had no sight in mind, and so we lived in that essential form, of work. And we had done this before, but upon beckoning. In that early time of employment we felt that novelty and foresight, seeing time ahead. But in this, time felt as though this were all it was. Indeed, we held views that saw us some place ahead, marbled in those hidden colors of esteem. But very much so were these just dreams, and we begudingly went through our existence. The nature though of this way became almost self-fufilling, for as we more or less evened out in our deeds, and they felt less like burdens, the actually mode of being so employed felt not like something which in theory ought compell us to see something elsewhere and ahead; nor, in practice, was it so unfufilling or contrary to the goods which, on theyre own, felt not so much disturbed: and indeed they were quite good for me, what I liked.
 From the peak of that point to now, a similar thread has woven along, and that is namely the mystery of our expeirence, and why we care about writing, death, inquiry and the gods, the witcher at that; and this doubt brings in light from other pastimes and wonders, of girls and friend gourps, outings on the weekends, dinners, high finance even. And in that, there lies what can only be described as a maintained tranquility, a happiness which comes now from what is planned nor promied, but from what our choices create in us, to exhibit and imbue naturally. That is perhaps the greatest, but also discouraging admission, that the good we feel is not something we do for the sake of work or in spite of, that the experience resulting is one merely esteemed by its effect being one of causes born in commisery with work (or whats neccessary); but rather, what is good as an experience, purely on the basis of it's flavor and hue, is born from ations which are esteemed as so because of the effect they create. Work, by all acocunts, becomes this thing which, in a mature sense, you acquiese to, and in some sense lean on as something which your ordinadry pleasures corroborate with. For as children we have certain wishes and glees, but they get polished off as responsibility is introduced. As it were, the good of leisure and liberty are not totally encommpassing, as you lack the seen and or felt promise and comfort of a friend, of someone to trust, play with, see, look forward to. These are natural wants. But in our preservation of such liberty, which you hold and are equal to foremost, there lies a disparity between what others have become accustomed to, or accepted, and thus you have less of a place or tenure to relate and or connect. And one of the primary virtues, or at least manners in which one ought take, is not to let theyre liberty become something of a goal, as if it be rightous for you to be as you are but in that suffer in solitude; nor, and this is perhaps foremost, ought you let the esteem and or product of such liberty sprout promises of the alleviating or social sort. "to make our solitude more exciting and thus less lonesome, or to spark the sight others and by that render off your difference by making others more likened and or changed for you."

 One thought that's come to mind is that of our life, and its way, it's form, its manner. For an age it seems, with inconsistency bringing us away, we've not been just.  Through the age though this has never settled as something tenuable, either because it had us be so original that living independantly had no fun nor smoothness to mingle with. By common ways, and ones which we saw as fitting, for pressures of neccessity surrounded us, and perhaps as aid and guide for the good which we ourselvrs sought, 'for a home of our onwn', that we abided such process; but doing so with fidelity and succour for our fine experience, grew poor habits and inclinations; all, namely, sprouted by our worn and leary relationship with duty and things of appeal around.
 Perhaps the greastest of truths rest on a more neccessary factor, an element if you will; namely, the principple of being, the encumbance to live well and through no matter our situation nor feeling. For the future may not seem bright, or may feel dimmer than our vice or confidence curry. But we must still show up, eat well, claim our plenty. At any rate, upon this immutable deed, lies the fairest of insights, the moral of our reflection; and that is, namely, that of all things oppertune, for which staked upon oppertunity, advantage or relief, that so ought these be given actual meaning and substance; for our actions that come about, our intentions at least, only move and (re)position by such decree. And the truth of our time, the looseness of our days, is that the decree we've followed is soft and ill formed.
 It is known that a rich being can be tasted, easily and often, but that such tune gets drowned out by nature's basic commands: to work and, sometimes, be seated. My merriest of prinicples says 'that all I ought do, and what funnels in the measures of must, is all and only that which affords me, or cooperates with me, on that simple quest to live in full and constant comfort. Quality speckles such end with matters of freshness and vitality, but wonder and might too --we care not for a frequent fling with sugar and crumbs'. Law and custom are an odd thing here, for they may need you to profess your understanding of what is requested of you; so that in your liberty you are still becoming of one subject to standard. As per family, I find this to be something embellished from that merry living; whereby in patrimony and marriage you broaden your find: playing that tune in company.

The vice though is that you take pleasure, and usually form expectations, by the seeming virtue of your history with such tune, and by that very attempt. "A good beyond itself, but the idea of it: givig you confidence but also promise."
I simply lack the focus and diredction of moral standing. Which is to say, an informend and well fashioned state, as though against some begging force, and for some uncommon end.

Perhaps the deepest of soft virtues is this thing; for it comes rom true success and character, yet can get coaxed into loosing that basic moral sense, whereby there is something needing to be done, for which our satisfaction and anticipation rest upon; and instead, we think to highly of ourself, or feel our seld deserving of reverance or pity, 'for we are someone who tries the mightiest and noblest of things'. Being the one who's written these annals, it is known that the peak of our adolescence was in being frustrated with folk for not being in a way that made us cohesive: we were as such cynical. The peak of this adult forray, or completion of our self, is in our lack of expectation, but want of things, and feeling doubt as to theyre merrit and our reason for wanting them. It was as though, in our completion, where nature took sway, that we felt drawn to things and open to them: as though we could be whoever they wanted us to be: for the vein in the marble was what our practice had once manifested outside: so we could fashion such clay (so to speak) in appealing ways.
So the year has come about rather nicely, though with some hiccups. From the moment we asked Bella out we've felt off, and more or less deflated. Just hard to avoid.  One of the odd happenings over the recent years is similar to an even older happening, namely the innate, or at least customary happenign, of what you deem good; and it no longer requiring diligence or planning. Yet, in this natural gait, you often run into moments where something else is sought, or you don't so ardently nor sharply exhibit that nature; or, most notably, a mistake, from negligence or ignorance, happens.
 One iosight is that passtimes, be it work or company, buffer your time in being as you please, for it allows you to be not. Often we feel the need to force our experience, for moments that are not so naturally sharp have no where to go but into something resembling indolence. Which evokes passion or further ware. For doing nothing feels poor, and we envy those who have things, and feel ashamed that we don't. Yet, there are right and fair things to do. It is the mnetality though. Not that there are not things good in themselves, but in the space were talking, having something you can look forward to, or count on, remedies the frequent need to rest and let be.
 This all comes back to the recent years, where such things were not present, and so the precedent to be was laid upon me. Oddly though, this did not leave me empty and craving, but rather more reasonable and elite in our custom. The folly in this was of a neccessary and impractical sort, but solid no less. But, what I mean to say primarily, is that we became so much better that we did so much more; and this has become great in both the quanity and quality of our expeirences. Yet the flow of life could not be avoided; and no passion, planning nor industry could alleviate your need to rest. By this choice or that manner, we've no garnered company nor easy itinerary. And so consistently w'd reach points that had me feeling poor, or moving in contrary ways, 'to cease the indolence, or taste for doing something'. Trust is a huge part, as it feels like something is there. And I tread on this notion; for if motion is always what we seek, and expectation is but a promise of something to come, and thereby a remark of your insatiety and unease at doin nothing, then are such things of the utmost importance, or is this immutable need a symptom of something esle.
 What then may we do in our life. For things are so good, as are we, in heart and mind, that we have no need, or less of one, to crave and or affirm some road ahead. Were stricken not with idleness, nor heavily when we do. It is almost as if things are so well and stable that dreams and fancy are beyond sight.
 As rgards health, the only worthwhile remark is that of consistency, and allowing for good things to come to be by right action. Such actions need themselves be tended to, and not done prematurely, out of insecurity or wishing to move. Note that playing Diablo or anything for that matter is spending, and you cannot train so wholly when your empty. Indeed, training allows for work and other things to be less costly. But we still have an account, and you can feel it. By all counts we've flirted with the edge of natural movement; whereby some pushups even seemed laudible. We've done this with squats on two occasions, without much gratuity. Doing free range can leave me feeling a little sore in the neck. But by all standards this is our stiff body being brought out of its lowering stride. Nonetheless, exercise is the trickiest of things; not food; that is quite simple, especially if your finances are in check. Which they are, to be clear, as we are fine to loose a little, and working a little bit extra, plus your gst and stats, makes for a fair stability over several months. Great. And food is about carbs, as oil fills in the calories. Your physical stature, as remarked by your place on the floor and doing things frequently on that, requires the more obscure and demanding task of patience, adjustment, forbidty in principle and practice, and quelling doubt and inertia, yet also smartly and decently obliging the impulse and want to move. One element is that of priority, and allowing that compulsion to move to bear itself when it feels right, and allowing this to be a primary exhibition. For rest is then had, and lighter motion. We must ingest this fundemental thing. For principally, like work, it is needed. But also to introduce and sustain motions, for they may at certain times not be there. And allowing them to come into the fray rightly and well is near essential.
 The form of this is rich in bounty but ceaseless in demand. But, the biggest pitfall, which our pleasure and sanity lean on, is in over doing yourself while in such a state. For it offers such, but falls unber false principles and errors, but almost naturally, for there is no true resting state, merely a lighter one. And we know this in our humour and compulsion, to do or not, to sit or play. Consistency requires patience sometimes. But so is it worth admitting that our life is not to forgiving for this inertia coming back to motion, or incorporating the motion done. We don't really enjoy doing nothing. Nor is there much which is otherwise easy to do. We beckon to the winds that lift our sails, but do so without the calmness that such winds will come later, and that we could restore right now. There is less to look forward to. I think of a philosophy meeting Thursday nights, or soccer nearby on Mondays and Saturday, and some vegan/spirit lunch on tuesdays. Even just messaging someone. For my biggest issue with friends is that I don't have this drive to invite them do something. And for those who do, it is usally our over emphasis on them, and not sitting well enough to merely talk to them, and like them as I do. For interest does not stirr there either, but rather a procrastination-like passion, satiated by the excitment of doing something together, when in fact, a more near and direct conversation with them soothes our mind. What is right comes easy. For we see more, or are fine with it as it is. We seek not. And all of this sounds burdensome and not so fun or rewarding. But it may be. The right thing has to be there. Maybe the spiritual meeting is a hastle and you don't light up about it. Maybe practical philosophy is somehting your really look forward to.
I look at my life and admitt nothing but everything. It is in some sense hard but easy also, as you can say, for insatnce, that we have an emotional connection with Bella. It is mine, and even if she has one with other people, no matter. It doesn't even register that somenoe else is her friend, or she's talknig, for the emotional connection is all I see.

But emotion, or connection, is that thing, where were being ourself, as so calm and mightily upright, that we imbue what is deep about itslef, and how we take a liking to others. We hold ourself, and keep our personal relationships with us, as life steadily flows. We broke such relation with Bella, and I see this now. From our personal standing, were so absent as to permitt small things meaning something large. And if comparability or reason guide us, so may we spend time together. Had we the confidence and calm, we'd ask Simron to go to a movie. For it was just that, something to do, that I'd like to. Reason never stated that with Bella. At least, I did not really want to go, if only for our emotional want beyond this. Our relationship was satisfiny, and easy to fend off those spry suggestions or wants. Nothing else truly was on my mind. Perhaps it would have been, but not out of desire. We'd not want to go to her baseball game, but would feel fine doing so. But this is an absent refelction, as though we were parched and she were water.
Bit by bit our strenght returns, and we grow sense of our past tidings; what seems good, bad, preferred or not; and by that, what is a token of appreciation, but otherwise worth no grip nor misgivings.
 I see inside of me a man who's made a choice, or at least through stubborness and strenght, bent himself to actions and paths that have provided stability and cheer.
 Such ways, or leanings, have made him no friends though. Familiarity became a relevant term, as differences occur within all of us, but however latched, familiarity softens edges and bears a bond. Some warmth at least. In part this is all true.. But what I see, almost determinately, is that we really don't knnow ourself, and by some accounts, loose ourselves in the vapid possibility of things; yet such inklings oft come when we are but a haze. Not weak neccessariyl, but lacking any substance or form. For you cannot just succeed, nor do people just like you.  I look back at the great moments of development, the insights that bore further reflections, 'as if an organizing of some newly discovered stream'. Christmas comes to mind, or the accpetence of Holly; that of work even and our amiability to it. The mere permission to live (not) outside. In all of these time has gone on. And I think were a bit too hard, and by that currently untuned nor forgiving, of the feelings and pressures around at those moments. In the case of christmas it was deemed that this ardent life of self-regard and industry was too much and uneccessary. But this was not entirely true. The spring that followed showed that. It was moresoe our view of things and how certain elements weighed on me. Our writing had to not only reach but preach the stars. As did our industry have to create success and fame, or at least try. One worthy of the words well written, upon strides becoming of the cheer recorded. Our titles and deeds are in love and simplicity. Such a beautiful morning. Popcorn, painterly clouds, sun glazing over the top. It reminds me that there is a gradient to the day, like the tide, and it comes and goes, offering new specks here and there, sometimes taking different forms, andthrough a shift in time, be it the spring or something novel ahead.
 I will be meek and write this in conciliatory terms, for my spirit is pinched somewhat; so let us aid it. In the former case I see the morn, the balance of food, gaming and inquiry. Then the midday, where minor deeds and a some adventure are had. And the afternoon, where we settle in, finish our deeds, have supper, and look out to the evening end. Here, the sky holds the remaining light, dipping into the final blue. And I think of Baker, or a mere walk outside. And all pastime feels best here, as your most rested, able to be, at calm in night's quiet.
 I don't think it's enough to say, 'well, this kind of expeirence is subpar but fitting for rules, be it conditioned or elected.' Or, 'this experience is all I ever need; it is so fufilling and draws me to want nor see anything else'.

Two elements run primary in my life. The effects of excellence and the moral of a good heart. This latter ought be explained.
 For we often find ourselves, in our excellence, subject to the wares of cicrucsamstance, and by that, our liberties are interferred with. So we pine for a time or some propsect to remove us from such and allow our liberties to fully glow. A good heart tempers this sentiment, in all it's folly and shame. For we understand the deeds upon us, and how particular our efforts would have to be to abate them. In a word, substance creates things, and much of our immoral heart leans into the excitement and confidence of passion or ideas, but not action or determination. Dreams as it were.
 Perhaps the most troublsome beat of our heart is when we are in a waiting state, yet stable, for we have too little amends, or dedication, and thereby wander in our sights, feeling attracted to things, or noticing what others have, and from that feeling jealous. Only, we still live stabily, which perhpas remarks some blend of ill-integrity and sense in our position, as highlighted by our 'waiting'. For in that, it is as though we have plans, or some care and esteem to return and be in the good, in how we see things, and like at any rate. But in waiting, or not being there, 'as though the game hadn't begun, or we had not reached the field', we still live so astutely, but unoccupied. This leads to a high sense of ourself, as though were boldy wafting around, being gleamed by other people. Our heart is so solid, but not truly to invest; at least in certain things which attract me, and indiscriminately at that. Yet we find ourself more or less pinging for things, as though it would be so nice. And perhaps it would. But we lack that moral heart. Our waiting is a form of idleness, and the love made is one of childishness or ill-excellence. Liberty as it were. Speaking for myself, we are too little in motion when were doing so well yet waiting, and so things are appealling, for were moving not; and the want is not genuine, per your actual investment. But we have no where to go. And per our life, who cant really be faulted in lacknig the wisdom to go and be, happiyl and stabily, that in our unjust but happy ways, we could never really see or find something truly desirous. And because our 'waiting' had us more thrown by appealling things, yet we were still grooved for living as we deemed, the mathc was horrible, and we either ardoured and suffered, errored, or dug into our living. But this created much toil, and more or less blinded us, in some sense fairly but in other ways not, to living more fairly and well. For in that, things which we otherwise gleamed are all part of the scenery, and we don't have this wandering or fanciful wants. This makes it easier to have smaller yet solid relations with peopel and things. We've yet to really live well, stable and just, under wisdom, with some elective and managing sense, whereby we may form things solid and meaningfull. Fret not of the smaller yet solid things you've past or lost, nor forget the things you have. I can't even count such meaingfull things on both hands. And there is me also. Such is the mark and gleam of a man cheerfull and merry, full of hope and promise and liberty.
I'd speak to this notion of solidity and meaning, in that, of Matin, I find something actually quite meaingfull, moreso than Carli, and even further than say Max. But theyre all of relative size. That was the thing with Bella; there something small there, perhaps tiny, but it meant alot to. Almost out of relief and collectedness, I felt whole and pure in relation to work. For we had nothing with her for some time. I'd describe it as there being this meaning in my view of her, but things being so small that it could never sprout. Familiriaty made sway, and we naturally could speak to her more. Our light humour led to more meaingfull ocnversations. But deep in our dark holds and eager heart, bolstered by confidence when misfortune drove us from passing over such whims, we sought a more meaing. But the connection was still small. I failed to realized that. And indeed, I don't believe there wasn't something solid between us, as there is with Matin, or mojoi even. But the size, and complxion we'll say as to regard properotion, was not so as to humour your plea. And our overestimation that the solidity in question showed some path or interest in something larger
It doesn't hurt to have some sense of the day. For it would be nice if you could see something new, be it some thing to do on the weekend, or some game or show coming out. These things add variety and spice to your life.
 But without that even life is always changing, tilting towards the summer, or away and to the fall. And our life even, coming from or towards thing, having some sort of state or manner which on the good or bad end, is deepening or exiting.
 The point though is that despite this novel and or expected change, 'from bloom to doom', so consistency lay. We wake up in the morning, respect the days when this will be early and to work. We walk on days off before anything, and after work on such days. We find it poor to reach our days end and not go for a walk. Why should we be so tired and dreary into sleep? Sleep won't be as well in any case. And carved between is a general mode to the day, where breakfast, lunch and dinner are had. As are there times for leisure and walking, rest and play. That moment following bananas or salad is not exactly our busiest time. And indeed, it does not always please me to sleep or lay down, watching something which is perhaps unexciting. But such is the norm, and indeed, seeing more, novel or not, blends this quieter moment into whats come or is coming.
 On that note, the time of day influences us alot. For if it were winter then the last light would be in the afternoon. Or as spring comes along this blossoms into the evening. But summer sees the light last till what is normally night, and we are ready for bed. This brings with it a sort of scenario, whereby we may wander about in the finality of our day. On off days this can invite a little time afterwards, whereby we may eat. Which is fine, but perhaps we remark upno the lightness of such food. Take last night. Truly wonderful, but we were home at 930. Some bread was fine along with a salad. But we were up past 11. And this is not so poor, but we might take into account the sun setting into 9. We truly ought have our dinner before hand. As we may account for popcorn or potatoes following; yet doing so going into 10 is quite late.
 Its just summers nature; no different than the oddity of winter's short days. But we ought be privy to the rythm of a good day, and respect the matters around us. For I like an evening ride, or one of light. And indeed, this amounts to that late afternoon, where warmth has returned upon the suns angle, yet there is still volumes of light in the sky. As the sun further dips into the evening vibrance seeps in, as the sun is more direct. This is truly an evening ride. Afternoon ought not be batched together with noon, for this is the meekest of times, as the sun being so overhead reduces the color and contrast.
 So, given its a work night, we may go for a merry ride, near the brewery. But this is going to be around 9. And it would seem that all lights are out at that point. We may read, and or write. But it's best time we go for a walk and return home to bed, or quiet down at least. That being so, we ought have all our food before hand. One useful note is that of the relatively settled form of your midday, regarding food, and the natural resting point, whereby we settle, and perhaps into the beginnings of grain. The beginning of the day is a complicated point, but it is clear that once the morning is done, and training has ceased, and 3 walks usually otherwise, that we have our orange, play, and cocner ourselves little with moving further. That harsh condition of eating something prior to a 2nd walk is a clear instance of how even 2 walks comes short. What were trying to avoid there becomes quite satiable following that 3rd walk and orange. Indeed it depends on what you want to do, but it is clear that smoothies and salads are the following period. And indeed, it seems like our blend of starches and grain come following. Today for instance, we have 6 servings of grain. This is not a huge amount, more like a split between one mass serving. But surely leading into days end we'll have room for some bread. And indeed, I feel not for a walk right now, as it's hot, I've walked already, and were pretty tired. Not too rested. So I might just split my grain, go for a walk in the evening, than play, recover, write a bit, further our Age, and have some bread. Maybe we'll go for a nice late evening walk or stroll. Likely a walk going into the evening.
 Such is our days. And I reconcile our grief and doubt with the fact that all things far and ill mannered are not to be officiated away, as though some intrusion. The reality is were not moving. And in such lapse we have humours and passion. Memory serves, as does character and formation. But, in the past, such posture saw such whims as neccessary, as though our composition would always be a little uneven. As such, we'd humour such fancies, but only as much as theyre thought, and in some cases pleausre, soothed our need. We are so well though that we don't even need these things; that, and were aware of there ointment-like nature. I find it somewhat disturbing to be so callous and complacent as to dream of someone or something, take pleasure in the idea yet expect not, or have any reasonable sense to, yet, in a better state, such dreams are actually a source of despair, for were more aware of theyre folly. A truly warming and enticing thought is one of socializing; but in and where I see myself fitting in, where it is easy, worth looking forward to; where I may connect and be happy. Such brings order and heat to our day, and similar to work, irons out the mallodies of stiffness and past development. But I sit here more or less aware of our inertia; yet am not quenced in this ill-motion by either some promise or actual experience. This latter is the tricky thing, for porn and food often stand as such remedies. But I look at more filling things, yet are afar, or just are poorly concieved. Suggeetions of 'you could just do it Ryan', are quite unwelcomed; for you don't understand. And that is it you see, the dialectic of a moral heart. I am tasked and by that given an experience per the quality of our actions. But in standing to this, in as much as I have experienced and otherwise rememeber, 'to keep our infidelities from pulling us away', that so am I subject to the flame of a truly unordered and wandering mind. So, for technical sake, we'll say that eating enough is not simply about totals per day, but rather, not going too long without eating. And this aspect holds with it a personally driven element. Take sugar. If you have it the night before, then you feel hungrier in the morning; sooner that is. And if you don't feed yourself when your hungry, your body feels famished. Aeorbics and insulin could be explored in these resepcts. But just in general, there are ill effects from going starving/catabolic. You break down.
 So, your aim is to keep yourself from starving. You tend to keep weight on and grow stronger. On one hand you have the sense of this, whereby you ought eat when your hungry. Too many times have we failed to meet this. And there is the element of your bodily condition, whereby hunger ensues; but so in these latter years have we begun to famish ourselves more. On principle perhaps, or of ability rather. But this has lead to weight and strenght loss. Oddly, when your famished, you find yourself even moreso. At least, you don't tolerate being so famished, and the effect feels even worse.
 The key element is that upon famishment and thus loss, you find it harder to train and be, and thereby afford more stability in your metabolism. Moreover, it is actually harder to eat. Not so much that you cna't do it, but the level whereby enough is had becomes lessened, whereupon being full is reached sooner. And so it is easier to feel full and heavy. And practically this has driven us away from eating enough.

So life is a waevin, a web of motion. But in fact, is really just about that, movement. All sound philosophy and moral formation rests on this. For we are always brething, moving, about to, or in states of rest. Take a painter, who takes bright red then the darkest of blues. One is quiet, almost unremarkable, but still flows. The tamest of rivers, stillest of oceans, still have movement. Atomically even nothing is really at rest.
 And so life goes on, and the orchestra of it is what we call living. To be in motion is to live. And indeed, much of reflection comes down to understanding our characters and humours, or passion, for such things are odd motions; different than our breath, our duties, our pastimes. There the motives for these things, but the mystery also.
 And nothing is so mysterious than that of love. Everybody learns to talk to people in ways that are suited and effective. To show up, be cordial, ask questions; you learn this. And indeed, you reach a point where the only thing to say is what you want: but you learn to want the right thing.

Bringing our life and feelings into harmony is an odd thing. For so much has happened, from our move, to leaving Vancouver, to the years prior where wisdom had set in but not in our choosing. And before then, where work held our disdain, and before that, where despite things seeming well, we were quite bored, and, notably, indulgent.
 What I can say then is that at some point in our life we saw things a bit clearer, as girls, jobs, oppertunity, health even, were not these things so near and present, and a root of shame if you didn't just pursue them and grab them. Such things have become objects in my mind over the era. Yet, back in those days, and this was something which came to mind today, was that we had no self-pressure, no practice, nothing to hold us away from people or things; but we had nothing at all. The era that came was one where we defined ourself by the quality of experience, and more or less hoped, expected, esteemed our further time ahead as something prompt for the passions which accrued, given the personal-life nature of our duties.
 And so I sit now, down because of a girl, and similarly so about being seen, and on that count, seeing others. We feel uncertain about things, where we are, where were going; what guides me at any rate. And indeed, you think of those passions that helmed me an age ago, gave assurance at least, such things were in effect soothing distractions, as a moment of lack could look to them as things to come; and we thus moved along. On one hand you have the basic insight that such movement, 'of going along', was not stable or just; and it can be said that the inherent stability, if it were just, would have prompted the strongest of primary insights and adjustments. Easy to say given that we had not been there; and so what may have seemed futile in our ways within this lane of neccessity, could have bent us in different ways than we at the moment thought fair.
 In any case, we have more or less lived without these expectations; not so much in humility but in an embracing of our dearest goods. On one hand, things we want, as Peter Parker would say, became more open, as we felt less disposed to things who's value and esteem closed us off to such wants. As it were, these wants, which I can better describe now, are so as to rest in us oppertunely or in attraction; meaning, that the ability for something to happen was not squashed down as improbable; and things that actually do draw us are given a chance, or made towards. Indeed much our reflection and inquiry over the years, coming to pitch currently, is so as to notice the manner of our ways, and what elements and fashions are reaosnable and just, understandible at least; for we may see that some activity or person cathces our sight, and the only thing holding us back is lazyness or some other occupation; at least, we often find there's a heavyness or filled-up state to our mind, for which something new, and as is often the case, something strange and revealling, bears difficulty on our part in embracing. There's a nerve at least. And through our days, and those recent even, we've made an excuse. Cynicism, as it were, is rooted in the diminishment of such things; which comes to pass in youth, when one in love yet nervous speaks of the other's invalidity. As it was with Pam.
 Nevertheless, such things have come about, and we are in most ways more open, calm, substantive in our expectattions, and humble in as much as were not. Yet, in all of that, I see major areas missing threading; as though the recession of passion leaves us rather unformed nor directed. And life has come this way, in a monagery of ways. For the good and to the better there is no question. But I am concerned that our moments which at one point had a fools padding, are throwing you off without it. For it is important, or healthy in a way, to keep on moving. It's just the case that we feel slow and dull in our tracks; and things which our more engaged mind would see, peer upon us to the effect of doubt and shame. Some of these things would trouble the Gods, in seeking the most obscure yet delightful friendship; all by the cheer and harmony in your heart, as to speak so freely yet happy. "Without wanting, nor worry, no luster and grough." Part of being a man is in both remedying the minor pitfalls upon slipping, but thereupon settling in and being merry of your actual gait, your place, your happening; for such dear things come to pass then, but through a forward acceptance. We often find ourselves grieved with what were giving up; as though passion is tugging at us not to let her go. These are the hardest of stings, akin to that disparity of feeling even the slightest bit immature. For the development of maturity is so that you bring your errors and seekings with you; and you become merely more humble and able; which brings peace and confidence. But you don't neccessarily want the right things, nor have the resepect satiety from right conduct. Such friends, if they were, are not those who lack such conduct, or act and or speak to me without regards for conduct at all. Ignorance and vice are neither good models nor pressures.
 So the point is that I am not fundementally well, and given our relatively deep wellness and harmony of life and deed, that so are these dissapointments and admissions regarding things of fancy a real downer, and more or less a disturbance to our otherwise rest.
 Such is the point though, as you just made, that being mature is not merely a re-arrangement of your past self into someone better, yet of the same life. You ought actually do things different. And of that we are not; and such things in many ways come from disturbance. For passion used to be a result of unwanted effects, by labor usually. These threw off our general pace and excitement. They were in the way though. And I think the way to characterize this new age, upon the last where we were the object, and our integrity was to such, that now our object is of all duty, but via a commission that seeks to do so not because it is neccessary but because we want to. There may be accepted principles or facts that give merrit to this. For if we see this as the way life has to be, then harmony with that is something of real want; for you have the proceedings and according effects of the right and evident thing. We lived in a bubble prior, shielding our precious experience from the outside world. Our own world was a life of its own, with duty to boot. But we are not our own. In a legitamate way, we are taking the hand of proper duty; which is to say, duty that rewards the need of us. But in doing so, we form our being around this; rather than in deference, or despite, as we do well here as to marshal ourselves elsewhere. Our adult bound is to the place we shall not, and by our genail regard, care not too leave. As I see and further know, all things of relieving and or pleasing account live and breathe in this realm. Our aim is to excell in that, taking refuge in the fact that nothing is at risk of being lost, but instead reached through our proper proceedings. A flower that is bulbing sombers not over not being in a blossomed stage, and by that lacking fruit. It is right where it should be and pleased with that.

 But we stand little in the lands of sureness, and by that steadyness, as though, to quote Seneca, 'we had some condition, some manner, a prupose, a resolve, for which we accepted, poised ourselves to, and remained both humble and ready in it'.

Do other people have more stability because they see only theyre careers and friends. Such an expereince is in some sense less complex and confusing. For I don't know what really binds me within our proper state; which is within, as determined, responsibility and ownership. This is a privalged statement, as I've mentioned, where looknig after yourself is elected for some merrit, rather than being something neccessary. By and large we could say that, working or not, we could live more easily, and just let things move along. But this sentiment is baked with the fact that we have to work; which makes the tilt of our life rather suspect; for such efforts are by all accounts a world of theyre own. And our amends, allowing for the probability or fairness for such things to ever be absent to hide away, are so that we tenure ourselves to this form of life. Which in fairness, is not so objective and concrete in the amends, but rather the arrangmenet; in that, we must be provide our home and bread, and not much else. It is because we have to work regardless if this is given to us which makes the amends to work a priority; and given the nature of these efforts, living easily and by anothers rule, or emphasis at least, runs contrary to the effort, and so we assume the basic reason for its worth to begin with, for which our own effort of it is weighed against.
 In a way nothing feels so real. And indeed, those which did while we were catered to, were so that they in fact were but faded images, but allowed to be seen as real given our freedom. That we'd persist in that, and from there, allow such images to come along, 'toying with us as our blurred future included them, but effectrively hazed; for which theyre unreality was unexposed.'
 My thoughts, as it were, once held dread and grit over the impressions that seeped into our free mind. Odd that our diversion of this melded itself with a hazy sense of potential; that we had made something special. But it was things we cared about, within our fine and stable action. We feel this way still, but more grounded; to which kids starving in Africa or the media world of politics draws me not. In a way, knowing what I know about you and what angle you mean to take, and for good reason, what you lack is liberty; for in that, your freeomds are fair, evdidnetly as time goes on but also in your comission; a guilty consicence is the opposite of feeling fine in these respects.
 Perhaps the greatest blow upon us is the amends born from stubborness, amidst a literal attempt to do nothing, but also furnished in periods of doing nothing. There have been plenty of times where we were well. And a principle effect has become ever more present, where the stronger your habits and actions, the more fragile you get, for you do nothing to excess or short of what neccessary, for what you do is already so well. Inconsistency here, and perhaps leaning too far into the freedom given by our remarkable choices, lead us to leave aside more stabilizing things; for our natural gait did not need them.
 the biggest change in our life, which is a war that will have to go on, is that we are not reaching our head over the line of duty, to then live freely, and from there, see things from such freedom; as though we had time and means for fancy. My life has often lacked sense and wisdom, despite our strenght. We naturally were so at Harry Hooge, but fortune brought us elsewhere. But given who we were, with some minor caveots, we took not to the folk around me. They felt fake and fony. And we were able to see this and hold our own via our strenght.  But as it came time to choose highschools, we did not go to pit; which would have been to your favor, and would have held things you could engage with. But out of distaste, and a sort of security and confidence that came from it, I choose Westview.
 This notion of confidence, is one where you in a cynical way ignore something for the merrit of something else: the right sacrifice as it were. And Westview held soccer academy, which furnished this sense of ours with substance. When we arrived we were literally studying the planner; we were quite alone in that sense, but unawares of the fact, for we were on this proper line; going over the planner was part of the enthusiasm in this iniative.
 The complacency which followed is a mark of something that defines me to this day, and is quite hard to detail. But as it were, it lead to a point where we were engaged with more people, as we were less cynical, only nervous perhaps. Something was off about us, complacent, or at least par for the course, and in effect this engagement blew off. And so we returned to that point of confience, in doing what was right; taking refuge at least. Yet, whereas going to Westivew saw much ferovr for duty, but then saw it collapse into moderate oblige and comfort, 'for the esteem of school whithered off, loosing its grand status', upon this disengagmenet with friends and encumbant committment to ambition, we found ourselves seeped in dissatifaction and malady from such proceedings, both in where they came from and how they persisted, in passive and further engaged ways. As a result we were moving as proper as we should be, but with our heads down a bit, unexcited. The point being that we found ourselves less complacent and comfortable, perhaps out of the need of something to bear us, direct us. As such, we moved to Pitt Secondary, for the sake of our lives. And in that case we embraced the frivolity that once deterred me; and indeed, we made great strides there, but at an increasing cost to our responsibility and home life. We were seperate and reckless in terms of such things. And the result was one that's determined my life so far. As the course from this reckless gorunds could be to work and thereby afford to play. But the work that felt satisfying fell off, and we had not much in the play to warrant working too much; and our committment to reach so was not overwhelming. But we had nothing else.
 The moral of Westview was that you should not have gone, and that from your complacence came a situation that pulled you beneath your sufficient obligation to the purpose of your effort in such place. We could not just plod along, studying and then ngoing to post-secondary for it was the natural path. Less we did this extremely well we did not want to do it all. The progression in westview, where such things mattered, was so that we realized that if we just did this well or that thing, that we could be on that line, and continue to be. Not aimed or reaching, but steady. Such is hard to do though when you have the ground removed from you, and to keep yourself from being depressed, you must be ardent or reckless. Being one lost its initial novelty and fervour; and the oppertunity to go where life may return, or be different at any rate, came at that calmer moment, and was thus humoured. But our natural attitude made use of this point of life, in its tendency to paraphinilia and immoderation, and disregard at that, 'for celebrtaion'. For we were steady, but perhaps not as much as we needed to be, for the path was ending, ready to rewind and end up elsehwere. We were not steady for that, merely the day. And as fun accrued, so did our lack of place on such path become more evident. Doing well today had less meaning when the choice to move further was not adhered to. Yet this is the right thing to do, the good thing at least. But we were brought away, too far, yet not excceedinly embraced and driven for what lie aboot. Many dreams and assurances, born of weed and its sprouting of confidence, came to be, and in many suttle ways, influenced our confidence. Equal I'd say, to our happier days finishing the shcool year, but overlooking the progress that would take further; that so did the excitement and potential brought by weed create a sort of 'in the moment' confidence and focus, as though things would be all right. Yet time passed and only the obvious things had anything to say.
 And we just could not get back on the train, but hated the little camp we were part of; in how satisfying it was, and what we could even take part in. We had a car, but not the manners nor habiation for woman. We met up with Ashley, but couldn't give ourselves to her. Give yourself to me all day long, but I don't really like you.
 All of these feelings and mannerisms are not so defined, but the path is clear. And it lead to a moment early in college where I thought, 'I have no destination, no purpose, no end; and these efforts feel enourmous and unjustified: we cannot be steady. Were not happy doing so, as well as we can be'.
 What proceeded was a shift in our efforts, but also our views. We developed a new world of which nutrition and health were the center piece. These held me, defined our action, gave reaosn and purpose. And so I felt stronger, able to apply myself; which we did do the following year, returning to college. And I remark from this point that college was not for me, but we were not broke by this like before, for we had our new selves. And so we worked in tandum with that. Bunkers, painting, sushi.
 And I'd remark that from hereon out we worked, did well, but in that, adjusted as to make this more feasible. We moved in the following spring, to a new house, then several times more. Each though leading to a sense that we were no where. No longer was the future something you could ignore, as it was when you were at home, nor could you meekely apply yourself, 'getitng back on the train'. Instead, we had dreams and self assurance, but only the evidence and sense of being more or less stuck in work. That was all I felt. There was no natural nor oppertune development past this.  For instance, Maurya gets +2 happiness on the altar and theyre unique buildings, and then that of the villa and arean --certainly the later. They also get it on barracks and libraries. And again, it's like crit damage or attack speed in diablo: know what makes the build what it is fundementally; then, like in civ, with say wonders or this or that aim, you can bolt things together, and or accomodate otherwise.
I'll note off the bat that the step pyramid requires a intrinsic happiness yeild, while the mud hut simpyl can't be built on rought terrain. The hill fort, which is quite fantastic, requires rough terrain. The influence post has no requirment, but only 1 can be built. And it does give 2 influence during celebrations. So not too shaby. The food and gold one are not clear to me. This speaks to the balance in a non improvement/culture game, where you benefit from hill forts and diplo buildings, to the point where you may see reason to invest in the suzerainity for that purpose. It is by my count easier to put in hill forts in a city for you can build them, then it is to buy them in a town. And you wouldn't want to in the first place. Given that, you may be unsure where to put a city in your nearby lands. Where there is rough terrain there is production; and indeed, resources are easily grabbed by towns, and don't offer beneefits themselves; for they get usuable across the empire. By that count, barring unique buildings --mauryas gives culture from mountains-- you are looking for tiles that will support your production buildings, science, gold and food, and that of culture and happiness -which is ever so important. One note is the oddity of monuments and villas, which hold influence as a base yield. This is quite precious. There is experience required for me to say what future buildings will nicely fit, or can go elsewhere. But in any case, it is easy to sea that food, science and happiness can just be overbuilt. The intrinsics are not essential, so you can find thee according spots for such spaces. And the point, is that the land is most essential, in that, given fresh water, permanent resources for adj. and rough terrain, and rural space too, depending on your purpose, that so a city lies. And indeed, you can have as many cities as you want, but you must invest; and so good ones are those which you naturally wish to pursue, as a better settlmeent. The limit of such in terms of the resources required, is what maeks you quesiton whether something should be a city
 It is hard to manage your views when the changes from age transitions occur. You have less settlement limit, and most if not all the increases you get are removed. You start exploration with 8 and modern with 16. You can build El Escorial for an extra, and take corona civica; in the moderan age particular this is better, as you've likely already converted so many cities. One important note is of ideals, in say a city location, or just a worthwhile spot, and how you may progress towards contesting such thing. A independant surrounded by a bunch of reosurces warrants a take over, but maybe not right away, given the resources. Early game rewards haste, so getting less ideal settles out is preferred over a better one that will take much time. You have to weigh that fact. And at any rate, as your looking around the world, certain spots can be contested by water, be it against CS or other civs. One element to your strategy is that of alliances, or good relations at any rate. There is a triumph that gives 5 happiness per alliance; and surely those who your either a) the furthest from, or b) bordered in a facorable way, in that you would want no aggression from that side, and by that token, seek no expansion there, so is this prime for an alliance. Also, those who they'd go to war with are likely around them, and so if your on theyre flank, then besides giving up potential trades, your not in direct contact with that foe. For the sake of extra happiness, which in effect is settlement limit

And in this gait, we often loose that stiffer stance and engage them with suppleness, as though on the spot or passing by. Speaking more amicably levels this off, and your not left with that nervous longing nor cynical seperation. You merely be, and with plenty, as you truly make a friend; and all mixes well into a casual and probale harmony.

It seems an important note that the settlments you put down are the same regardless of time. So if you go over your settlement limit in exploration but mitigate it with happiness, or tmeporary settle limit even, the fact that you were just getting a temporary buff is not essential, as you still have the settlements. Certain settles may be more valued based on what they provide, ie. treasure resources. But the actual use of a settle and its relation to the coming increase in settle limit, which you may artificially reach through policies in the prior age, mean nothing more than the balancing for having those settles. They are whats important, as they give you land, production, scuence, which gives you space to slot resources, make gold buildings and industries, or to make wonders, improvements and slot grea works, or to hold more dominion, and by that count, have productiv and strategic access to taking others; or to literally concentrate your yields to, gather innovation and reach the stars
 Its part of the game that it will reset twice. In doing so, you need to consider that buildings of a similar type will be built over in the following age. And some resources are less reliable, for sure in some cases, such as wool, clay, rice, dyes, most of the bonus resources in fact. Things like iron, camels, incense, most of the city resoruces stay in place --though cotton also stays. It is also important to consider that wonders often can be built as though they were distrits, and that as the ages go on your going to have more specialist slots and more happiness to justify putting multiple in. So planning settlments with this future in mind is important.
 Cs can afford production on rough tiles with hill forts, science on tiles with natural happiness, culture on flat terrain tiles, a influence boost per settlement. Consider where there is rough terrain and forests, for these will likely hold your long term improvements; and consider what you may put on them. It is not so adventagous nor neccessary to get settlement limit from the expansion or military city state. Instead, you can get extra food on your gardens and baths, which are one of the few yeields that scale with the ages, as your growth keeps going regardless. And production carries over from improvements, and hillforts give +2. You ought consider where some great city will be made, and if a military CS is available. Secondary cities are often enough to warrant this.
Consider this question: why have 17 settlements in exploration? Your just going to be over when your in modern? One factor is this. Lets say your happiness accomodates you being that far over in exploration; say your at 15 limt and have an average of 10 happiness per settle. You can afford this. The question, is when I go into modern, and the limit goes to the stock 16, will I afford that? Cause maybe I am at 20, and I could afford that in exploration. That's alot of settles mind you, and indeed, one of the triumphs gives happiness per alliance. I can't speak to the happiness availability going into modern.
 This actually raises a good point, that one of the friction points of going into exploration is that we don't know much about gonig into modenr. What we'll have, if we want to keep our religion, if were surely keeping all cities as they are. What triumphs are we going to choose, given our expansionist or tourism view. Culture for instance may work well with the Ming, as your rewarded for having so many fortifications. But you also have other elmeents, in relics, wonders, CS improvements, and celebrations. Some of these happen naturally, but perhaps were not emphasizing relics, just what we can afford to slot.
So I mean to play as Tecumseh, who benefits from CS, in providing combat to infantry and ranged, plus 2 dominion per. This does carry over to my pleasant surprise. The shawnee are a great exploration civ as they have a solid warrior who gets buffs per empire resource, and they get +2 production per tundra, desert or plains tile --I hope this works as advertised. They also get +4 production on nav rivers, which is niche but pretty nice. They get the heralded 50 boon towards CS conversion, which is quite expensive. Siam has the ability to insta convert CS, which has nice but not neccessarily needed effects. Were converting them for dominion, but for the sake of victory the immediacy is likely not too essential. The CS benefit mind you gives combat score and production, plus the little boons. We may also slot in mementos that enhance these elements. starting with Greece seems essential, or at least heavily advantageous, to get extra combat on infantry and the CS boost. Theyre Parthanon is also quite nice, with culture and base influence.
