 I think it is not in our power per say, but rather something which we are the measure of, and that is the discontent we sometimes find, at feeling as though were not friends as we could be and would like. This does not need to trigger you so much upon seeing someone else theyre friends with, or in a moment where you seemingly are not. Things just have to be. And indeed, they were, and nice things happened, but we were irresponsible, and let ourselves make an error. It wasn't even a mistake, as we do like someone, but perhaps we'd have been wise to recognize the difference in age, how things were between us, the risk. More sense would have been nice.
 But many days have gone by, and we've gone from blocking out the grough, to feeling whimpered by what we lack, and unable to rid ourselves of such thing, to near calm, as though the past were behind, and the present was open to the beginnings of repor, humour, and then friendship.
 I think it worthwhile to especially remark our tamber when it came to our view of said person, for it did occur, as has happened with Matin, that our initial excitement with them reared a platonic interest; and indeed, some unease and confusion about this grew; and from that there dipped feelings of luster and grubbery. But as we spoke more, that confusion lessened, and we felt satisifed; needing not to see more. And I experienced this with Bella. We felt quite content. And I would follow the same advice you used then, that who she or anyone is talking to is in the sense of impressiveness and excitement not much so, nor in the sense of actual friendlienss and like not so significant: we ought not be moved as though were missing, of loss, and by that jealous and impressed, nor deflete, reduce, and at worst heighten ourselves.
 Now, my feelings are a bit inner woven and as such confused, or at least a little worn and hurt. But my head is up; not from confidence or hope, but from not fearing too look her in the eye. So heartfelt I am, so sweet a man, yet I acted a boy, and a grubby one at that. When I saw her today she was not this woman who brings fear in our minds nor grief; our emotion makes things out to be as though theyre precious and we ourselves worthy of shame; and too to our actions, that we be awful, rapacious, or at least repugnant and perverted. Mellow and droll I am, more or less pleased and bit by bit peaceful. It is quite nice that the ideas and want which swirled about have a place in our heart. Returned they have, from those up and down moments of prior life; whereupon its steadying, theyre place is nearer and sincere. That is quite nice. Such elations bring me over the hump so to speak, whereby the ware in by hips and tiredness of our eyes feel noticble, and work is upon us tomorrow. Your excitment will grow steadier though, and you will not feel so bad betwixt the confusion of friendship, platonic ideas without generous want. We lack folk of our own, people were excited to talk to, outside of being personal, or liking someone for theyre charm. Sparks make things fly, while things warm and nice may be professional. Always has this battered me, or at least brought much disorder and flair. Amon was literally on our mind as such during the winter months, and Mikaela too. People come onto my mind like this; were taken far enough, as gifted by our demeanor and strenght, but then thwarted by that which held up our uncertainty, 'that relief of having to truly be responsible, and make friends from there, and cease the stair and care from times other'. It is hard getting old. But I prefer being it than young.
Bordeom, something whichc omes not from our nature, nor in our manner of deeds, as often occurs or is to come, but in tired moments, where even being at home is unengaging, and see not, feel not, hear not. And fomr this there spurrs that all too evil of grievences, envy, jealousy, desire, and at that, somberness at the distance of such things which would so seemingly spark your mind.
 Much of our consolation over the years has come from understanding the nature of these things, why there pleasing, how to attain them, how natural the mean may be. But we so often look past our own irresponsibility, and how this tears us away from things that bring activity. Moreover, it brings with it some sense of harmony, as though our lives are similar, in that we are all bored; and if were not, its nothing for us to be shamed about; many other people are equal. And by that count, were not driven so much by what comes to mind, nor do we langor over the present stillnes. It is more often than not a common down to your morning, or, as it usually is, after eating; which may have its own insights.
 Theres just this feeling were doing something wrong, and in particular, we feel poor in reaffirming our place, holding perspective, not leting our mind wander into hope or abscence. But in many ways our heart is unsteady, and those things which brighten us feel at too much disease for us to merely be content; for they run away, or loose theyre form as something so nice and novel, but merely near and worth gratitude.
Such a great day. And one that is not so easy but more or less apparent in its good.
 It just happened, a real flow, without debauchery or whincing. Bella obviously is a center to this, as is its been through the days. What I experienced is a rather mellow harmony, one in which neither she or anyone was so special, but rather we were one, together, a team in a shared process. This allowed work and our life to be the focus, and for things to come and go as we were pleased with. Being able to be present, as though we were at one with our place, gave much rest to the prior whingings at other peoples interaction. We often felt jealousy and a motive to make people smaller, seem unhappy, and reduce theyre relationships. And this was not the case. By all accounts, our love for Bella is but an affection; and from whole grounds, we are through and throuhg, like with Matin. It has been ever so hard to remedy this, or come on top, without feeling ourselves enclosed to ourselves; but in that we don't believe. Yet we feel distraught, thronw, overly drawn but in that unsatisifed. And it was one thing to have such affection but feel it unoppertune, for which you accepted, and therein went through flow, and another to merrily be, not so affected, but at best aware of something you feel nice. Indeed, there is a balancing here, but the affected parts of me, where in moments we take pause, as though there is this motion of want or haste, sits now more minorly, and unassuming upno our natural poise and pace. Was so nice to speak with her, make nice, joke a little, to have her go by, make a facr or not, but it did not matter. This manner, this breathe and calm, marks a core condition, of strenght and rythm, where people are neither so poor as yoru envy is pleased to imagine, nor so elated and engaged as your afraid to be so. One moment comes to mind, where Bella and Paul were speaking, and they were just making a laugh of things, him saying this, and her saying something else; its the kind of yoshing, as it were, or poking banter, that we all partake in. She said this then left. And my feeling was, let this be so, full and true, but nothing was gleamed special, nor we absent. Were being ourswelves.
 And that is the mightiest of things, the sweetest angle which brings cheer and green to our heart, is that Bella is someone I see, but is not glued to I. And by that, we are me, being, ourselves and through. And from that, where she or anyone goes is not some thorn of abandonment, nor, in contrast, some curraotr of love. We are in action, of the flow of work and its existence in life; for which virtue is the mark of treading this path, further in grace and stride as your enamure grows. We like to glow sometime, but all do. And here lies our action. The past is not forgotten, nor is our past love and the souce from it so removed nor un-pertruding. But again, small emotions of an unassuming, though noteworthy sort, are not a deflation to me, but merely a mark of our form, the shift in our way. Much comes which is fair, real and of right fancy. So much I missed what is now fitting to be: the reign of luster and might that bodes itself by what is right to me. And so I like Bella no more than is pleasing or fair. And she can think of me highly or not, appreciate this return to pace. Or ignore me if she will, or I gleam it as such. It pains me not so, for I care for her similarly as I do for all things. Our affection merely piled onto her. And our encompassing and, in this particularly once-exagerated but now mannered case, we walk tall, holding the dryness from that enlarged love, while the drafts of work and company rear true. Sparks fly and we fashion them, which makes our pace ever more lighter and welcoming to thsoe who make our life tender and important. From me, to you, in my commision, a sweet might.
It is not lost on me that our life could be very different, both in terms of direction, had we gone to Pitt, or college right away; which is to say that we didn't move to Pitt and become rather reckles; but also in terms of magnitude, or bearing rather, whereupon little things hear or there, or choices that could have been witheld had there been more wisdom or sense, or even a light resistance to circumsstances (whose effects were far larger then presumed).
 For our life went through a stage, one which was dry and wearing. This transitioned into something of pure right, one in which I knew things were well, and all the coarseness that the time prior held bled away. But some of the wisdom, as would give allowance, and favor, as would insist on such permitt, carried over from that age and lead us down unfruitfull paths. Path which were uneccessary in theyre abscences: we simply had no life. There is something to be said about how well we partook in life when we had to, that this gave us a manner of confidence that justified letting things be for the moment. We did not know the good nor need for life to be present, and so given the dedication to our personal efforts and the parchedness of passion and remedy, 'as to soften the fatigue', we saw the means for an abscence of work as a fortune; and not something which was pained upon a constance of this, but an indifference given the confidence we had from our prior times. Working at Superstore laid the groundwork for this surely.
 It came to me the good from working, having a life as it were, and not letting this be some hinderance to good living. Nor, and this is foremost, was it clear that it was not something which good living was surrounded by, but the other way around; that good living had to come from a life. The pitch of our later 2022 was blossomed in this; and by all counts, those lingering elements of love and amends were softened, set in our ways, and not things which were avoided, but not bared up with a blend of hesitancy and haste. For we were moving, and had the mind to carry on, moving well, as respected the essentials of such motion, and the goods near and dear to me that awed in harmony with that; whatever came would be in commission, or from cirucmstances which we could be generous too.
A review perhaps.
 For one, our health is in standard shape. Not sagging by any counts, but struggling to lock in. Pitt Meadows yoga remains aloof, but we may make for it, on one of these coming days. Rec center yoga is more or less known and is quite effective. Soccer too. Though I mean not to go this week. Next week were off for 4, so a great day then. Our training practice remains the most precarious; oddly it is pushups which are giving me the most struggle. I've not much of the energy to run or do squats. In this I find a lack of Hatha as regards lower body to be absent. In part, our training is in fact holding its form. A mixture of foods not quinoa bring with me a sort of depletion, for which our muscles are overly stiff. And dissecting the root of this is hard, as there are surely many factors. My neck and upper rear back just feel quite tender. My shoulder has not hurt me though, but it may as we settle. Rows --which we got for free-- seem an elegant solution to easier pulling. I've no resistance to full bars, in fact doing them at the gym was overly nice. But we may use them. I find that our back being used is rounding us out nicely. Our plank/pushups feel overly pressured in our clavicle, and contributes to much of our ware. And indeed, our core training was going well. There is oddity in this, for the right moment is not always present at the right day. Were quite tired now, and so the prospect of training while were off is peculiar. We don't want to wait too long, but we also don't want to miss it. Warming up our shoudlers and plank, knee pushups, using grips and the block may allow for stronger pushups, and row bar is there. Perhaps some lower body spot drops could suffice, and render our legs well. The intensity of running is a bit beyond me. This week has been relatively hard; and indeed, I feel some ware, or at least tenderness in my neck, but there are parts of me which are really swell. I think we just need to eat more and right. Find some hatha. Further our bird. Let our practice go through. We've done core, training, and soccer plus yoga once per week, and it feels that the compounding of our natural gait and or seating, plus work, has held it thin. Almost to the point where its overlapping with our following off period, whereby we are not even done with what we did. The worry is that the coming work period is too close to when we work off the effects of the last period. So some pinching may be needed.
 In any case I've returned to this happy point in our life. On an upbeat we are brim with like and non concern. On down beats we are at least done with this strangling about Bella. Much to do with direction and goals, just cares and views overall, come to be, when we consider ourselves not as fine, or at least true, in our unobtruded path. For before, it was so that things were well and we were fine to let things go by, while we soften our attnetion with folly and vice. But now that the rabbits out of the hole, having returned to a point where content is bound is not entirely rewarding, or at least respectfull. Were not just trying to be happy as we were. And indeed, much inquiry and advancement of habit and activity bring this to full, as we recognize the matter in which our lack of vice exposes me to, in that work is tough, the future not consistently bright, 'outside of expectation or affirment', and that in this, our handle on people is quite appreciative but retreating, as our grasp is no longer fit for the manner were in. It is I, we, and in that love, custom and proceeding are brought through that. But our knowledge of these things are in many ways born of attitude rather than equity. And so at the dip of our tone, we feel darker and muted, for which those grips we had are missed, or sought at least. Which creates much confusion and enamure, as you are forced to content with an obvious truth that seems less so in your more open and eager ways. We humour this not, 'fine to be somewhat folly in our anticipation'.
So I remembering our days, recently that is, as it gives sense and might to what you've been donig, which erodes any need of further things; it also softens the feeling that there should be something worth seeking, or having, and that it is able.
 On that count, I feel resolute in our way to be so austere, purposeful and directed, cheerful and merry, in our place at work and deeds around. It feels obvious that you may be privy to other things, acquire them even, but these things, and our idea of who we'd be and by which manner we'd achieve, is different than this steady resolve. And I care for that, and indeed, am more open to things across life; to procure more life that is. It seems that romance, love, connection, and all things ambition and of high sorts should commend with that. Indeed, it seems wise to believe and rest upon the likelihood of such things through life, rather than this paused, fallible infatuation.
So the state is a term that more or less remarks all of society. Not civilization per say, as that is more about the elements in question; that there is a wheel, a potter, a road. But society is an agreement, a union, big or small. And the state is that which houses this and faciliates the rules and customs which the binding is centered on.
 Adams says that some have the view that there is no hope for the state, no future. This suggests something rather fundemental, that society, or 'the state', is an developing process, and is currently as such. For at one point there was no state, and then there became one step by step. The process of it being more or less utopian, or at least stable and prosperous, and just, keeps on.
 One note on justice, that we could say that the goods we seek must be so for some may find satiety in theyre own good, despite others lacking it. And the point worth raising is that such inequality is not likely to be lasting, as those who have less will flip the board. For a state is organized as to be effective, but in that, gratns further liberty and voice for those invovled; who over time will upend, or at least iron out inequality. And if the state is not so organized, or but absolute, and in effect from a point, in it's rule, then so will it not likely be so successful, or as fruitful. So for those in power, theyre grip is likely only temporary, or is unideal given a state they could be part of, had everyone been more able and invovled.
 All of this is worth speaking of for our own wellness. Much of our life is brought down by confidence and need of pleasure, rather than steady wants and behaviour. This occurs because we are not oriented to responsibility. So much has been lost or overlooked from this, and we've grown quite rigid and old as a result. Through our youth we found that our actual attitude towards deeds was paramount, as it lessened the impact and thus relevance. But it is clear upon growing up, that given the indeluable place of such duty, that we ought not try and minimize it so as not to be there, but to embrace it, direct ourselve in both amends and gratitude per its tilt, and from there, shed off the coat of confidence that sat there as a remedy, and in turn gain a free and natural harmony with things you really care for.
 Blending this though creates a sort of protrusion. In part we've lived to the utmost degree in wisdom but not integrity. And therefore, we have levelled off the effects and burden of duty. But we've not a friend, or room to be. We've no life. And we saw this some time ago, both in terms of works reconcilability, but our life also. I notice though, however well we are, that we have to keep on and hold our head up, for we've not gained a life. And so much as we surrender to the life which being grown up offers, so are we subject to the pressures that flow in upon our confidences lapse. Namley, the prospect of the world, or the state rather. In prior times things never felt so easy, and so in accepting that we were well enough, we found angst at giving up on the promises and dreams that would bring us away from work. But as work as has become our ground, so are we not so pleased within it, as to be distracted, or at least in a calm tune, and not thereby subject to either a. the presscence of alarming sentiment, or b. lacking a full grip of your own, for which confidence is based on. "A pure, right, principalled end. Yet all for us to hold too, rather than reach."
So there are two ways of living. One, being that of the good life, or one of self regard and flourishing, and then of amends, or duty rather, whereby, laudibly or not, you oblige and attend to smoe set of rules, all likely common and or civil.
 My experience in the former case has been that we can never be good enough, and that life keeps on, as those common rules reflect; whereby traidtion sets camp for what it knows to come. And indeed, you loose your friends, family, love, being in harmony with only what you own and yourself. Much is worth loving about this; not in what you lack but what you have. And indeed, as I once requested, if I had the means to be this way without any common rule then I would do so. One critique of this though, is that there is no one I know nor am I familiar with the quailty and or state of such expeirence had you been so frugal yet free; and would the element of flourishing somewhat depress you, whereby magnitude could be had, yet for ends whos abscence made you not feel in fact so free; or, that such ends were not in fact all so likely by your mere flourishing, and that they'd require more. As in most moments where this state of flourishing exists, amidst some rule, 'of which we call liberty', the promising and or hopeful effect, 'as though you were dancing and via such calm and steady motion, were confident in the steps to come, and as such what may be there', is in some sense but a form of confidence, or at least remedy for the natural pressures of the moment. For elation is a gripping sight, as though you can nearly feel the spot ahead, taste it as it were, hold it. While flourishing creates a sense of what may be, however likely, and that were happy enough now to meet it. Take our Sums for instance. It affords me a very real oppertunity, or action at least to partake in; it is clear, deliberate, and at least finite in the result; for a flat response is not even to worry about so much as we feel positive of the material; and if that is shown to be false, then our attempt was merely understandable, and now complete. It would be irresponsible though to imagine the response being so high-praising and or a source for my fortunes. The motion is different then when we see what we can do and what reflects the natural outcome, compared to overstating that. In both cases we don't actually know; in one, we know we can write it and share it, be it to a initially flattness, or later esteem or not; this is very much in our control; while in the other, it's as though were adding fuel to the flame of foresight, and upon its growth our expecations lie, and fervor at that. Flourishing then is equal to steadyness, in that your head high and upright, but moving as such along. The root, or form rather, in which our elations and exagerations come from is not as clear, but we may describe simply as a blend of impurdence and intemperance; as though we should know better than to enlarge the end which we otherwise see.
 That is all to say that a life of this sort is in fact complicit with all, but moves from this moment. Generally so from our rules being of a personal sort, and lacking any from without. We are influenced, and at any rate subject to common rule, so the domain of foresight and by that promise is present; and so in our steady state we are not simply occupied but also shown a far light. But our manner is as such steady.
 It goes without saying that how things should be and how we've been is quite off. For we could, by all ideal means, been so steady and by that flourished. And seldom has a chapter of our life gone by where this wasn't so. But we either ignored, dismissed, or regressed (using false confidence for a return) the common rule. In doing so, we made our personal embellishments a source for deference towards such rule; as though we were a kid who thought themselves unfit or misfortuned to work; as though it were an unfair sentence. And as this could not stand, the return to rule was a rocky one, which brought much doubt, staleness, and impulse. "Or, as often happened, the passion for leave of such rule, and eventual resolve to this."
 One basic notion within the fields of self regard are that your habits exist in relation to the world around you. If it is warm, then your practical choice of night clothing is essential, and if the sun stays out late then your balance of leisure and sustenance must be choosen with respect to that. And work is no different. Yet, it is not so much an incoming draft which you angle yourself around, but rather a weight. One is merely an angle which you must accomodate, while the other is a load, a force, a pressure, which you must bear. And it is not lost on me that living well in relation to this is not only achievable but prefered, and in some sense easier. For why not remove yourself from rule? It's easier aint it? It is because your a man, and are thus subject to the things that such rule provides; and if not you, then from some other, who you more or less become subject to. And one of the barest notions one can admitt to is that there life has till this point been a pendulum of temporary times and those permanent yet of despair. Our integrity has never had time to establish itself fully, and by that count, soften its glow to one which fits within that river of duty; for which the manners of confidence, pleasure, endurance, hope and promise may be fitted accordingly. Our hole life as a young man was so that these manners were fit to our time within dependance, where the freedom was present yet merely so; that, or we made our times of right amend as simple and void as possible, but to an expectedly worn result. And much of these insights I'm having were present in the three or so years prior. But the greatest advance in our life, morally, is that for an age we built ourselves on the wellness of great experience, but in fighting the common law, we thought to reduce it through an attitude that we similarly applied to our freeer goods. But this engagement was never entirely stable, as you never could consistently flourish in the prescence of work; at least, so much as your propiety was meant to elininate, or nearly void it's prescence; despite the work and effort having to be done, and increased temperance to afford lightness while doing so. And because there was a natural ill-rythm, so did our manners of confidence, reward, hope and zeal fashion themselves accordingly. Where, on the whole, we sought for relief of our duties, or to expand past them. Which more or less rose from our personal esteem and practice being thought of as remarkable, or at least subject to acclaim and thereby award. Twas the balance of our prior era, in adolescence as it were.
 Now, I find that our sparks of pleasure and confidence are held, however lightly, by hopes and enamures born of old. And that our view of life is one that still beckons itself to some far promise, some sight of a time or place in which things of a warming sort will surround me, as will acclaim and prupose; the latter being an ointment for the attentive life we life now.
 And I see how things could be different. Yet, I cannot remove myself out of this sense that, had we been more consistent then our time and work would be more stable, and less subject to grief and worry. The latter has more or less gone; and mind you, given the nature of our recent worries, ought we be reminded that we had many of a different sort for the initial year prior, 'and our days before that were not so different'. As for the former, the effect is one where we sit at home, or have some mind to go out and do something, or make a plan, manage and or appeal to our navigating the course of our personal and working lane, 'whereby we either keep to such path for sake of continuity and cultivation, or live as is afforded by such', yet in that we feel void of things elsewhere, as though somewhere something else was going on and we were missing this. Work is generally the source of this, where we imagine that people there are talking and regailing of theyre shared adventure. And even if theyre not, they have theyre own free time which is established and of fine sorts. While we see, as we sink back from our initative, that there isn't much else to do. Life is the heart of this, wherein there's something we have. And prior to working we thought much about having just that. A place of our own followed, and some recreation and leisure to top it. But we miss a friendship, to go out and wander with, to confide in, be excited for. And this feeling, this humour, is often folded into romance, when in fact it is just a yearning for love, to care about someone, to feel important and or special. Better put, it is about being invovled with something you find essential, but compared to work is pleasing. This talk of a garden has promsied such glow, similar to the nice company that yoga provides, or the compeition and fun from soccer. Work itself, as we feel less hidden, or in need to be, and along with that not so large and craving, that we may parsimonioulsy be, coming and going, doing what need be; and like school, where our place there is rooted in need, that so with people do we act high or low, but positivley no matter the sort. Growth occurs here, as does commradery and warmth of friends. Being ourself has never had time or support to be the mode we persist in, and channels for eagerness and expectation are laid. We were merely delayed though. Norms have returned. I just feel when there is nothing on my mind that what I do is poistion ourselves with what we have; and many of those things which I'd describe as nice and on par with having a life, are not so entirely mine, less I am there. It's when were back on our own time, and no one is available, that we think ourselves unstable. And recourse to the Gods or men, or prudence is but a shifty response. Too which we say, that there is not merely flourishing; for it takes a turn for, or forms inclinitations, to the worse when it naturally fails, or lessens. For you never seem to be so well, nor so devoid of things which are cured only by confidence or pleasure. These are not to be amended to in such excited ways as much as your flourishing is the true end. But what ought we do, given the inconstancy of such? For one, let the room for it breathe and over time expand. But foremost, and indeed this should be the basis for all things essential, you must keep the matter of rule, so as to afford a continuity to your flourishing, by way of your life persisting. It ought not be so that we live at best ardently as to achieve ambition, but in that fail to live, as flourishing is of the utmost. But we also musn't subscribe and in that abide to a flaky view of rules, whereby they are obliged here but not there, all in support of what gives us more room to flourish now. To abate the grief of lacking such flourishing is childish; to do so by some oppertunity, as though to earn some period of flourishing time, is unwise, for the return to rule awaits. A life, as to afford, and in a better sense, equate, to what we mean by confidence and pleausre, can be so as to mould such qualites and objects corresponding to them in such a formed way. That's what life is. For all these words, all this inquiry, all the confusion of living for some moment, only to realize that life returns, is so that not much can be said other than that things compell us, out of tranquility but also deed. And so we ought abide so much as our nature has been and promises to keep that way, and equal in turn as the source of compulsion means to remain. Will we not eat, need housing, require punctuality and good sleep? Will we not benefit from whole foods, being on the floor, exercising regularly, and avoiding stimulus and porn?
I can say without almost full definition, that confidence and pleasure are the result of needing someting to fill in what you lack upon un-living.
So I was thinking back to the fall, when we were at this point of indifference, and notably, upon that ease, or un-eagerness, became more open; and we really connected with Bella then. Repor and humour just came about, and I found it easier, or open, to ask questions about her. We were friends.
 But I think about the cause of this truly, and whether there is anything to it. For I look at that time, and it felt more like we were free, but upon an acceptance of things and inherent stability, relative to being at home. We were not truly alive, merely being, moving along.
 And I think the fairest insight is that is not exaclty how life should be lived. For we sought not as we had no stakes, and could merely be. And at any rate, however well we were stable, and as compares to now, that so was life to be gained, moved towards, sought. We felt this naturally, as the nature of our position became less stable, so we sought to change. The idea of caring not about stability excited me following our failure in this, and that did not go over so well.
 In many ways, our resort to that was about things being easier around me, so we felt not the work to be stable. But this is what life is, a persistent lift above the ground below us, where duty lies. But in that lift, comes life, as we see and are drawn. Its just a matter of our stability and who we know we are. Much of our life it seems that is worth remarking upon is so that we did not emrbace who we were in any lively we, but hid, or found solitude, as though the quality of such experience, hwoever swell, was incompatible with things around. And I think our response during prior times was what brought us dissaray. For nothing is really to be found or mirrored against. We spoke often late last year about the experience people could share, and how this was no shade upon me, nor some seperating force. This is bound in you being yourself, which is not, primarily, to be so elated or enthused for random others. Consume what you have: people are not. Breathe what you may: all are around.
So at the beginning of February, I went up to Bella, asked her out for Valentines day, she looked shocked, said she was busy, and we haven't really been the same since.
 That week prior I called off my move to Hammond, lost 1st months rent. One noticbel effect is that I did not feel like eating. A week went by, and I spoke with Tristan, telling him I liked Amon and Bella. Amon turned out to be married, which gave much closure in my mind. But we spoke of Bella at length. The possibility excited me most. And I thought about it for several days, going back and forth, finding moments of imagination about how I'd do it and she say yes; as though we were on the same page. I recall going into work the day off, seeing her, and thinking, we can't do this, no way. And the day went on and I felt a mixture of solemness but closure. I felt far apart from her, her no where near me; but this was how it was, and I should move along with that. Near the end of my shift I went up to her and asked about some test she had taken; we spoke long about it, laughed. I was being as I wanted then, talking with her as I like. It just felt like a lifetime waiting for this, or rather, that it would never occur. Some stiffness upon asking, as though it was odd for me to do so; some hidden feelings or doubt were lingering. But alas, we did so, and when she left I had the biggest smile on my face. I felt like she saw me, and wanted to see me more. I thought she'd be glad if I asked her out. I thought of us going to dinner. Our read was wrong, and perhaps action upon certain principles.
 The day followed with no glance. I to this day can't really dissect the consequence of this. For 3 weeks little was said, and then I felt like she was rather bothered with me, or avoiding me. So time went on, we went with our new move. And I found myself asking her how her day was, in passing, and she'd make coridial responses. But I just had this sense she didn't want to talk to me. So I stopped asking. One thing I'd note, given the better state of things now, is that this sense we got, that she was looking at the ground, nervous to make eye contact with me, or speak at all, may just simply reflect that we were not that close; and it was I who was looking at her. It is strange that we were able to go up to her and ask about her test, and her to respond so fully. That was where we were, and recently mind you. The months prior we had developed some rapor and banter, and this lead to more conversations, personal too. And I recall that much of the summer had gone by where we weren't like this, and I had made somewhat of a deliberate attempt to not get hung up on her, but let things by. Focus on me as it were, and not be so drawn out by her life, who she talked to, that she was leaving. A good mindset generally. But I recall one day she passed me near fruit loops and said something to me; almost as though our calm equinimity became more fruitfull, and we had room for repor. She even waved once, which is a nice thought; though troubling, as I find that wherever that came from is gone.
 In any case, I have more or less terrible about this from the day it happened. And you go through these motions, where you put her out of mind, see where she was wrong, or you, where the promise lies. Carry mentioned that she mentioned that she thought I was too old, and that it was somewhat (perhaps fully) inappropriate. Which has lingered in my mind, but at the time, gave me some thought that her reservation was about nerves rather than want. Carry even said that she told her that she didn't think it was a problem: she's a big girl now. And this sparked some hope in my mind. Which ultimatley is the problem with all of this. That I really just want to be seen, and however well or not I imagine her, it is not truly wanting or sincere. But I don't want to avoid her; and our natural stride sees us able to be seen and know her. Which we find much struggle when were too bent in a way that prevents this. Our life prior has made it hard to merely be; and the manner in which our life was, not entirely in our control, made such things somewhat hard.
 So following all of this, we felt either absent, like a shadow, to her and from me, which was impractical nor pleasing, and subject for much grief; but she did not see me, almost causally from our asking her out. And so I had a hard time seeing her, as though the blinds were closed, but in that, not seeing her at all was it's own deleting thing. It was as though I looked, not too hard but not too passive or soft, as if to bring us back. But this was terrible, and is more or less odd. In the past, with Holly for instance, we developed more firm views about ourselves and the world, which placed her outside. Whereas my take away from Bella, the feeling, was that I simply should not have asked. And this composure, or whatever it may be, did not lead, or find refuge, in this complete overhaul of our life. We simply remained, almost worn and scarred by the mistake. Some confusion too.
 Which is where I stand now. For some time, maybe a week or two, our natural irreverance has rekindled into something more amiable. Matin sees me; I look right into her eyes and with calm grace, say I'll see you. Were connected. But were not special. It's a sort of trust that removes this want to be removed from a state of abscence or aversion, but also not so eager, as to be wanting but unseen. Being so connected allows you to let things go, for your not seeking, nor afraid. You can just be, have been. And I feel this way with Bella. Not entirely, but were getting there. And that is quite a nice thing to say. I feel on the outskirts a little, if not bottom of the barrel. But there is a cup. We had our first rael conversation today, and I felt myself angeld towards this care for trust, and by that, peace and amiability; whereby passion and scorn are emptied. I still feel unremarkable though, as though were not terribly satisifed. Hearing her talk with Tristan and Derran unerves me, as though they are special. We don't feel seen. And when she talks to Nick, its as though he and her are in tune to one another's life. Its just hard to have this emotional satisfaction, whereby someone like Alex, who I connect to with Gaming, is different than Matin, who I feel more bonded to. Bella has always alluded me, as we have no real connection on some practical thing. And I always felt like I was hoping for trust. And in lacking so, I made that deliberate move to ignore her, or let her by. And we were solid enough to make common ground; where I felt so seen that she could have been fucked by every guy in town, and I'd know that I could still talk to her: for she'd speak with me also. This is not a given, and I feel that there is room for me to say something to her, but not so much that she'd say something to me. And this weird history, where things became sweetly amicable, went into discomfort and disgrace. So unfortunate, the fool in I, born of heart, yet fiddled in it's thump. And I fear not to say hi to her, or talk even. But were not that connected. And I guess I am unsure of our life as to feel like we can confidently be and allow things to go. There is this feeling like she is going away, like we'd never see her again. So much control and instability in my life; yet so much to carry, such a tender load.
I feel not myself, which is the point, that were letting worry and apprhension pull us to the side, and away from our path in life, which by all counts is lovely, of wonder and trust, might to and all things which once seemed of dreams. Little bits here and there, but we foremost have the charm and capacity, the peace, to be as we are, but in life, away from solitude and bordeom, but amongst friends and society, the world. It is our heading, our truth, our manner, whereby the balance of work and duty come to pass, and in all our means of fidelity, we don't cover, squawler in said solitude.
 Perhaps it is a matter of embracing the life which is upon you, one which is right enough for you to lead it well. You cannot fall on those things, commonly people, who would forever excite your mind, take your sight off of the work at hand or to come. It is imperative to know that who we are is not held back, we merely be. But there is still effort needed; the target, the skill, the will to lift is present, and we do so with virtue, in that we heed the appeal to the force which draws such oblige, but we also do so unapolagetically, counting perhaps on our consistency as so, whereby such constancy softens our time and lessens the impulse to leave, but also voids you of the ill-wisdom of actually leaving, whereby establishment is lost, and the estate of life and the insights which bear living in whithered away; all to the effect of built passion and confidence, as the indiscimrinate fact of this presses you against your abscence, and such manners of will that would have you conjure and dream of somewhere else.
 Much of our worry, our grief, despite coming from some action, really is built upon the history we bring with us, and, to be fair, how in being as were at certain points, whereby we had some sort of averions or angst (in a given moment), that or proceeding from there, whereby work, views, leisure, health, woman, friends, coworkers were experienced and promulgated as such.
Such deep inquiries it seems. For on one hand, you have your experience, and it is one that on mayn occassions is worth all effort and time, and given the form of it, and how differing forms are not but trivial alterations which you may fully assume, that so is the path per those occasions on of peaceful oblige.
 But you also have criticsim, or at least mystery. For you look back at your life, through childhood, youth, young adulthood, and you see how certain choices were made, how certain attiudes were had, values, persepctives, committments. Soccer for instance, was something I loved, but also done league wise with admittence or begrudgement. But like school it was a duty. When we could cease, or found the whim to, we did, and similarly we did the same for school. But the reality of then having to work was quite poor, as it felt all consuming. And we did not wish to do it fully, as to somewhat warrant the good which came from this; but doing it partially made little room for such goods, nor was much fufilling on its own. Steady perhaps, but relatively flat.
 And so I think of those days, from Sums to nutrition, to our time of confidence through Save On and Walmart, to the truly life altering establishment of reaosn and philosophy, personal driven values and views we'll say, and how this collided with that general need to work, but found aceptence; for virtue offered and thrived. This kind of stability though had no real legs, in practice that is, and was more of a balancing act, whereby we lived as we could under such amends, but then, seeing our ability to do so, we checked out, as though right amends could return. But we had no life. And upon seeing this, at least garnering a life more or less, that was to be fair little but our own, but was stable and upright, 'and our head accordingly high', that circumstnace and our will brought us away. Indeed, to times of great industry and kind, and insight at that; but also much wear, and this feeling that we were re-entering a race which we were not fit for. Yet reason prevailed, at least our adulthood did, and what was once cherrished but squalored over, as the weight of life pressed against our freedom and liberty, we achieved this in excess. So much so that things which were one rare, incongruent, or too ill fitting for me to feel calm in engaging, came more or less naturally. Not as we'd dreamed, but as life normally gives, and our sweet mind cultivated. A medley of people, habit, delight, and relief from rancour and ill-sightedness, blossomed amidst our working way. Our steady lane as it were.
 But we sought more, and upon seeing means to do so, realized, upon failing to reach, what emptiness we had inside, how much formality and commision held our sight and gait; and that with life being void around, as we felt in that moment, relatively, there was so much we carried to be as we were. And we've never been kind or gendered to live more or less simply in our ways. We never admitted a challenge nor lost sight of the truest good. Life has just been a bit messy, irregular, ill-fitting, unlucky in our decision, or discretion at least, and all in all, too far gone to entirely like ourselves, trust others, fall into your line, for which trajectory carries you with calm through your day. Such was the plight of Bella, who for all her worth, and our adjurnment of anything really that folly, merely company, that we fell back, and incurred the weight of life around me. Just a disater really. And not the time I needed it. We have felt this way on and off, and every day, a new one follows, and you see, realize, bear more respect and consquent fortuity to the impression of nature and it's manifest in life: confidence, room, liberty flow, and begin to fashion and take form, which creates, and at least brightens our mind, for the purer sight in front.
I fear that we lied, that we had false hope and genuine peversions, if not fancy, of several woman, who in thinking about them, aren't really people I admire in a whole manner of ways. They strike the part of me which seeks such, or is impressed by such; and we use the thoughts like smelling salts, aromas if you will, to soothe me in certain times, or direct oru thoughts away, or out rather, of idleness.
 And to this I saw okay, no harm no fowl. But our view of such people, who don't too much from those whose thoughts of mine are absent, or of scrutiny, or judgmenet etc. are all so in that we have some stance on them, some pitch, an angle, and our actions have been such that we treat them as so. Much of this has to do with indifference, or rather, some sort of mere cordiality, while we take them up in our minds, but not in life, liking them or not as we please, not offering ourselves forth. Little things are not the source of our discomfort or pain, but rather, our whole life, whereby it being lost, or at least obscure and held by me in ways that dont' faciliate much connection, so is there no room for little things to mingle; nor do you feel the probability, and at that varied and novel progress, of fuller connection. Just as people we do this, where a moment of calm and the prescence of sweet might, brings you out of cordiality and into personal matters.  Bella was the white whale in these regards, where this matter of our own inklings and ways, woven to some good extent based on how open we were, that so did this not weave with her. And indeed, there was always this portion of me, or better put, this area outside me that garnished some doubt and learyness on our part, as though there was not much of a weave. And Bella haunted my mind in these regards for she is quite lovely, or mature at least compared to some folk, who I more happily dispose in our mind. And at one point we stopped heraunging ourselves over this, and allowed our natural gait to persit, even if such nature was in parts closed, or ill set. And despite our enamure taking hold of us at a vulnerable moment, and this idea of ourselves in relation to this thing which spoke to our scarrs and protection, that so do we overestimate, out of giving little regard, 'whereupon exageration takes form, as a foundation', as to how little wrong there is, and how few areas around me hold that protection. Even Bella now, who despite having nothing to do with me, by counts explicitly, is not someone I shield our eyes from, or feel odd in trying to meet hers. A normal flair, or at least understanding has returned. And so she does continue to be a source for aggrivation or worry, in comparison namely, and feeling our own doubts or illness. But don't let this flip things inside out, where one manner of problem becomes the central force in you, as opposed to all those great things around, and wealth of good and fortunate ones at that; and, as a kind of positive note, the eveneness and lack of clumpyness in all the things that were once so, and brought you great reserve and worn formation, 'as though the awkward forces of life made your unerring principle overly persist'. There is no more drag. And indeed, the sweetest jewel in our mind is that of pure parsimony, where irreverence mixed with felicity bring forth calm and tender affection, connection, reason and understanding. A life infront me offers various forms of this, whereby we may bind to things through such parsimony; but as virtue is diligent in all matters of gruff and deed, so does parsimony find fertility in all fields and weather. We broke our golden egg; but think long and true, who you really are, if these words of mine have ever meant anything, lifted you, deepened you, formed and in consqeunce brought anything worthy of the name love and cheer; and remember what you thought, what you did and are experiencing, that love and wonder as born from parsimony brings all you need, and carries not but the taste of things, and in that, affords one the feeling of sanctity, a free mind, that lacks remorse or dissaray.
The basis of my life is strange. And indeed, when were just going, flowing, we notice what we've lacked, or been covering, or falsely planning on or seeing, when trouble and stress come. That, or were so ideal, or at least determined, that we fail to see what is around us, and perhaps the folly of our ways, the unreality of what we see.
 For it makes little sense to speak the words of virtue and reason, and affirm this, meditate on it, as though it were holly enough to make to feel full.  It is certain that our life is thoughtfull, and that we sit here writing endlessly about bread and sleep, our avoidance of porn, trouble upno remission; how to wake, walk, be, what were grateful for, what we enjoy, whats been good, bad. We lack very little knowledge or experience as regards things needed of me, and so we fret not nor affirm what is to come.
 But were tired, worn in the upper body, pinched in our left hip, a little dry in the eyes, like were dehydrated. One unassailable reason is the lack of eating, which we've made great leaps upon this recent time. Its as though your body doesn't process the food. Maybe it is just for meat or protein, or sugar. But this is from entering that state. Which by all accounts ought be noticed, or at least permitted, upon feeling the need to eat. You shouldnt endure yourself out of it. And allow this moment to be what it is. Proper.
I find it hard to be steady amidst our hopes, and as I afford some perspective, I feel this hesitance at adopting our new view; as though the thing which I had hoped for is being otorn away, or ceasing to exist.
 One element of friendship, a nice one I'd say, is that we often feel ourselves fretting over such people because we don't feel trusted, nor trusting of them, upno our leave. We wish to feel that had we left for a day, week, month, life even, that we could say hello, show are care and such. Thinking back to Mariner, we came in there with more eveness; and mixed with our might, we were privy with many, but not so drawn as to feel enamured or over-coonected, clinging if you will. And time could persist without us feeling unerved; we trusted ourselves.
Habit of mind, parsimony, the complexion and form of our way, as to bind, integrate, diffuse, and in that, accomodate and commission.
 A little bit of distance, or thought otherwise, and I see how our mind can be brought back to our main purpose, which is to flourish at work, and by that, do it well, live outside it with commission, and in other words, find peace, no remorse, no diversion or distraction. This is achievable. We do it in many ways. Porn roots us with a seeking effect, as do little strifes and awkwardness bring fixation or aversion. And our past is not so much unclear but a hard thing to bring in. For when your on your own and yourself, the world is either with or against you. But when you are in the world, your not with everyone, but simply who you are. There is calm and pleasantry with most, or a strangeness which is tolerable. But life goes its way. And it has many spots and holds, which marks our measure of regard, and by that lever for happiness and steadyness. For the monring starts and were all so well, but then we hit those ups, feel the need to get work done. And when more people come in were brought back up, but the work persists. And mentally we can see the transition ahead, to more open and free times, and physically were with some momentum. But were still slowing down, in need to eat, rest, bolster through that final end. And here we see the matter of our way, and others, and that is that were working, with stuff to do, either diverting our mind from it based on distraction or promise ahead, dreams even, or were focused. And being able to do this well removes the prominence of dissmay and longing, that were misfortuned, with a unceasing weight, and that somewhere else is fairer. And indeed, diversions which might please us become sparks to our mind, yet subjects for grief as they are not obtainable.
 The most mistaken thought, or under-represented, is that notion of what you know is true, and the maturity and sense that such thing is not so easily achieved, or so without priority, and that such achievement is in fact worth it, per the experience within the grounds of duty, but also in the broader complexion, whereby general and applied goods weave together. Being kind, catching up, sharing a moment, these are not poor and are in fact welcome. But they come and go, because your there. Our life is the center, the crown of importance. Our priorities in that along with taste make us more affable to other people. Indeed, conflict in oursevles creates this feeling of eagerness and energy, but with nowhere to go. But a course of reason and its application within duty, allows for commradery to form naturally, and not be so held onto, whereby want is exceedingly had, and a feeling of lost equally so. Were so grounded in our life, and light at that, whereby familiarity blooms beyond, that our life being so is the center, the core, what we have, and all other things are what we like, appreciate, are thankfull for. But we don't pretend such folk or promises are mine. Again, taste and custom make you more affable, or at least bondable to someone or something, but in seriousness the difference does not cause dissaray nor seperation, but in fact, brings one togerher in an accordingly real and deep way. Trivial and or casual humour and clammer are really diversion, but at the very least surface level. When we come from our self, living with a full habit of mind and action, we are not drawn nor elated by such laughter. If we do, its not a diversion; we don't lose sight of our way. And more often than not this is so with others; who by all accounts just have more similarity than I do. But any can be known deeply, or at least in a real manner. And you may think of them and see them as such. Nothing trivial is taking them away. For you may like talking to them, and will if you can or wish to. And that may mean something to you, for I am not afraid to be affectionate and drawn, for were bound to go our way. And in life and time going on, I am not afraid to live as though we were not going to see them for sometime, whereby we'd be clear and dear as if this wasn't going to happen; we fret not that this thing special wont return, or that theyre going our way, for we are on the path. It will keep things up. Trust is crucial, for they may leave and never see you again. But you have permission to be yourself, unflinching, unafraid. From Mariner, a unsteady but stable Pitt Meadows, and now a broken yet returning claim in Hammond, we are on such a path. And such way is one that is grounded in us doing what we ought to, with liberty to see and breather further, and by virtue, contain ourselves in the trying matter of such deeds. To persist.
So it is often said that we should not be gripped by things we desire but do not have. We may remember that things more near to us, or through parsimony, wherein the prescence of something occurs and is quite satisfinyg, compared to many matters of want, whereby the abscence inflates the nature of the desire --rather than being satiable upon interaction.

Trust built also, so your mind is free to wander and see elsewhere, for of that spot where you've been, a return is known; that you can at least."
Those fuzzy feelings, circling like sharks, and we don't want to have to sit on shallow water to avoid them. Much sense and ppositivty, relief, or at least experience and ease, and from there understanding, helps remove some of the unwarranted elemeents of this, and at least calms the natural side of things; for as well and good as affection it, it can be confusing and a little messy; such props to you for having this, so fine and dear, but life can bring us away, to either sorrow or recklessness.
 In any case, whether they be circling or not, it seems beyond clear that the line in life, where there is this complexion of motions and rythms that impress upon you the neccessity of amends but then signal the virtue, or at least means, to do so. But when we slow down, or lose clarity, naturally from sleep, fatigure or eating, or those uneccessary cankerous downers, that so do we fnid it hard to rest, and seek confirmation, or some promise; for we either have nothing akni to resolve, and want something to dedicate our mind to, or, we feel the heat of those unfettered passions or worries, for which we seek remedy.  In any case, I wish to say how things are, as this is ultimately helpful and in some sense needed, for it gives more direction to your motions, and keeps you pointed in your rest. May reason and life wash off those things which make this constance a neccessity, as to avoid despair or hazardousness.
 Food is of the utmost, as is exercise, or stretchng at least, and sleep paired with this, and in some sense crowned as the point in which those former elements direct themselves towards, or cater to.
 One simple rule is that eating is enough if it does often. The balance though is tricky, as you certaintly don't want to wake up and eat bread; nor is it much tolerable in our state to go 7 hours without eating. One effect from eating little is that it becomes hard to eat more, as it weighs you down, and your body just doesn't want it. You go into an immaciated state, and this causes much weightless, lethargy, poor sleep, depleted muscles and thereby stiff motion. All is ill from this. And indeed, there is not much to say about eating too much. Some times afford more room to experience the natural dullness, or at least lowness from food. It is hard to avoid. But work days are tricky, as they begin early and go for some time, and it is seldom well to eat nothing. One trick is to include kale with your mix, as for whatever reason it mitigates much of the langour that often comes from going into work following food. This element of our life has for a time been fine; but I have begun to notice the unwelcomed effect from eating at all; but given the neccessity of it, it does seem like we have to either accomodate the ill effect, or blunt it by some useful means; kale being a moderate end for such.

There is so much life, richness of might and character, peace and liberty, in bowing yourself to all that which flags itself as needing attnetion; and our regards as humans is so full of potential, but only as much as our oblige is made. So if your still following me, assume I have the introduction email set. Lets work on the findings/experiment.
I thought the best thing would be to explain how I reached the results I did, then we can consider the best way to demosntrate it
Putting movites/reason for curisoity aside, the first thing I did was, in esscence, do the fibonnici seuqnece, adding 2 terms together, and when I got to 5+8 -following 1123-- I added 5+8=13, but then I would add 1 and 3 together. See if you follow this. 112358134711. That inrigued me.
 But I realized that the issue was that I was 'summing' (as I call it) the 5 and 8 to 13 then adding the 1 and 3, when in fact, I should have gone 5 over from 8 to 4. If your adding on a iterating line of 9, then you can always add a double digit numeral together to reach what you'd otherwise go to through proper steps. 8 + 5, given a 9 hour clock/line, is 4, but if you go to the whole number 13, it always follows that you can just add the 1 and 3 and get 4. The difference is I kept the 13, added to 4, but then added the 3 and 4 together. This is not proper procedure. You have to add it on the repeating line, and just operate as you would to every nth play, as addition normally does on a cardinal ine. Only, the values repeat, so a binary line could be on the 100th index/term, yet still have the value of 1.
 In any case, when I made this swtich, the sequence became 11235843718988764156281911. Repeats. I wonder if you can calcualte, or create this sequence following this rule. I will paste these results, but I claim, and have found, and assert the proof by that rather than a inherent rule/predicative principle that I understand --that is our mysterious explanation-- that if you take any variation of double terms, from every combination 11, 12,13 up to 87,88, 89, 92 etc. that each will repeat in the exact same amount of steps as the other. And if you lined each of them up, say 11-99 down (vertically) theyre are clear symmetries. The standard set is 11,22,33-77,88,99. And clear symmetries and behaviours are shown hear. I cannot demonstrate this so clearly as they have to be vertically aligned. But alas that is one element of it. Again, I wonder if you can calculate say 3 random pairs, say 34, 72, 46, and confirm my claim, that they repeat in the same steps as one another. I assure you they do.
 Now, the 2nd era of this discovery came when I realized you could change the lenght of line/clock, and that the same behaviors would occur. So if the range/degree/clock lenght (as I say) was 8, so would the sequence of 11 repeat. Not in the same spot as 11 from clock 9 mind you. But, interestingly, all pairs/seqeucnes with any variation of starting pairs of terms, will repeat in the exact same spot as one another, as it does in clock 9. That point of repition is different as I said, but the set of runs/sequences within theyre according class/degree/clock, all repeat at theyre own respectiveyl shared point --per the clock. For clock 9 for instance, it takes 24 steps (I believe) for all pairs to repeat. Clock 8 is --i cant recall off the top of my head, but im making a point-- in 20 steps. Its not actually 20, but the point is, that however many steps it is, for arguments sake say its 20, that all pairs within 8 repeat there, while all pairs in 9 repeat after 24. The amoutn of steps does not scale mind you per the height of the clock. The 11 clock pairs all repeat in 9 steps.
 One little note is that different amounts of starting terms have the same behaviors and symmetries. So starting with 111 will repeat 111, and in the same amount of steps as 222 or 314. And if it takes 40 steps in clock 9 for all trios or 80 steps for quads to repeat in clock 9, so is there some shared amount of steps that all trios or quads will repeat at in clock 8 and so forth.
 That is the esscence of sums, in so far as this basic seuqneces are concerned. There are other areas I've uncovered, and indeed, remarking upon the symmetries is its own thing, and most indicative of the cause of these shared behaviors. But those are the results/findings given our basic addition upon a repeating/clock like number line.
