We are much, with much worth grace, and see more than all, which is from our liberty. And the happiness present is only apt to come; no matter if others are no so aimed. And I feel this thing, the thing which has been with me our whole life, but now is different. This beat, this pulse, this rythm and ornaitness that speaks to the treatment of our heart, and actions which measure up to its way. So long has wisdom brought me hear; as far as I know. But we have been off; for being me, this, was never enough, and cleverness and or shortcuts attracted. But we failed. And I see now, even upon what seemed like a blow to our heart, that it was just something fair amongst the reeds; something which is not even absent in any way that it was, just not so prominent. And I can sit here, on the even of the past, wehre Tolostay and Plutarch bring peace to my mind, that for heats sake, upon our own word, that we may listen and grasp, curratil and live on. And that as such, I may let this be, that what could have been or was may yet come to be, but not through grough or grime, but a way that is calm and fittnig for how it ever would be. Not much has changed; only that some clouds have drifed far and away. And alas that is living, for people and oppertunity come and go. And it is part of growing up to learn how to see this, feel it, earn more standing. One of the things I thought to myself, compared to our past times with other folk, was that I did not wish to be whereupon us leaving that I'd be afraid to return. That was the sort of relationship I sought with everyone. Our root hurries us to something soul, entire, complete, and those charming and with life bring us to that, and flurry us with mourning if we move away. "Regret is the feeling of this motion being by our own mistake; as is cynicms caused by other people moving themselves, while you yourself are without motion."
What is essential to our lifes? The fixed parts, the constants?
 We've been toiling recently due to something which brought attention to our mind. But this thing was never so satsifying, merely relieving, as I felt I could just be, 'as though peace had become the norm'.
 For it is weird and unwanted to withold yourslef, be hidden. Yet you don't always known how, and surrounding forces draw more precident.
 In any case, the loss of that particular peace is not to any large detriment. Just a reminder of what we really mean, where we go, how we are. As it felt easier to let our natural stride go. But perhaps it was all too comfortable for me, and brought up by the novel affection, and thereby attraction which ensued.
 But the point, and this is at least how I feel now, is that however natural you could be, there is still a fair bit to do, and just doing it under the warmth of comfort is likened to feeling alright that you feel so poor, when you do. It is kind of its own hiding, as though we can endure this malady together. People's minds are not so there though; and there is an odd imbalance of thinking that the harmony in your experience will come amidst theyre warmth. But I don't feel they seek such harmony, and are not in fact there so much. They are, but I feel your expecting them to be there more than they are, as to compensate for the solidity you lack. Indeed that is the described desire, as so much as you lack, 'and natural stride does not suffice, evidently per say the morn', that you long for something, or latch. A strange yet similar passion.
 And indeed, it can petrify me to look back on ourselves, if those or any passion are occluded or excluded (on purpose). But this need not be the case. Reading Tolstoy has shown me, or brought my heart to light, that the impetus for life is in your motion, your stride, your mix and blend of all things self and world. Passion is merely the overextending this, as is rule and zeal a tightening, 'affirmation beinga contrast to passion: a contrary, yet equally vying effect'.
 And so I live in the middle, rightfully and recognizably; for obviously Bella or whomever, or all that I further see, brings a sense of delight. But theyre often not there; and as much as we think they are or could be, the whole of our life, which by all accounts people are themselves embraced to, does not stay fitting or presenr to this over-looked appeal. All should be there, and forces of connection bring us closer together. But such road is long, and passion or affected views ought not confirm nor nourish expectations or understanding.
 On that note, we know that we work at a certain time, and thus sleep at a certain time. I have been experimenting with different variations of eating time. Recently we had been having our last meal around 830, preceded by an outing. This was nice. Yesterday though, I had our corn, edamame and lentils much earlier, around 2, and it was great. It fit right in; then we had bread about 4ish and this did not bring me to a sleep. I actually felt well. We had been resting so that could be part of it. And oddly, though mentally we were a bit tired and stiff, the thought of potaotes pleased me not; and I was not so hungry. But they tasted great and I felt well. Our sleep was a little tired, but good no less.
 It is a hard life we live. For in the slightest of motion it is all worth seeking, and harmonious with all of lifes more dragging deeds. You can't exactly underestimate the boon of having no problems or qualms. And socially this is strange; yet I still find that our demenaor has never left us for the worse. In fact, as it began, we merely felt hardstrung to be so harmonious. Our sociality was not so unwell. We just sought more per what we felt to lack. As though the comfort of liking more people, or better yet, being like, would lessen the workload, and task me with less effort. Which, by all accounts, is neither poor nor unfruitful; but is someitmes unclear.
 In any case, I mean to say, that of your life, how it's been for better or worse, that we may tend to it now in how it is, and be more sweet and welcoming to fair and honest appeals, but upon then, be somewhat useful and or material in our regards. For we are playing Path with Victor this evening; that is an anchor to that latter part of the day. And we are going to yoga and the gym at noon, and this anchors our morning and afternoon. We work tomorrow and the 4 days following; all short, so not as fatiguing, but up in the morning we go; and so we know the direction of our day, for the end is so fixed. And core training is quite nice on sunday, as are these warmer days inviting for the evening. The sun is beginning to earlier set, and for the moment it is quite cool. I should mention that our funds allow us to go to the gym twice per week, and that the weather affords restoration this friday. We'll be home but 830, time for supper, a short shift to follow. This weekend has been lovely, and indeed, I find that yoga or soccer are fitting, conjoined with working out. We are not so much advancing in our strenght, but continuing it, which does add to some refurbishment of initial grungde; and keeps our consistency up.
 The point is that were busy, and by no means unhappy. Work is quite nice. Remove the feeling of what you lack, or what could be or have been. Look at what is there. Clean is quite nice, and not so constant, and I feel placed in that level of respect of communication. Little seeps onto me which is negative. Taking a picture looking at the camera has created much better look, and so I feel less nervous about our eyes --as we do with our speaking. We have not let Bella go, nor forgiven her for treating me as she has, nor do we feel forgiven by her. That is ok. I accept that we are not so much friends, and that our affection is not something of curiosity or lingering truth for her. She is not a stranger, but not someone I am displeased with. I am at peace, able to move on, see the small amount of kindling there is to make even the tiniest of warmth. Practically this is not appealling. It also speaks to what there ever may be. The prospect of being friends is by nature an uneccssary one, as you just go and be, and familarity happens. It is removing ourselves from sense and our lives where such familiarity feels promising. And what then feels possible is not worth beating your head over. I dont imagine Bella is pining for Rick. And if she is with someone else, so be it. I woulnd not imagine anyone cares if she has a fling. Your just talking about yourself then. I like the principle we've taken that our life being something of action, is not so self-invovled as to satiate our lack of it. From the heart we should be. Our misguidance was just a bit to resolved and born of fanciful crevaces in our mind. Innocent sure and intentfully harmless. But weird no less. And so be it.
 Work is not lacking, in itinerary and attention, welcomeness and comfort. This is not some epitomy of my life, that is but to pass and bear its insight elsewhere. But that insight is there, turning me a little at the very moment, but further as our life carries along. The natural bend it takes, or may, only feels more calm and propserous.
Twas an important day today. My heart misses her, that smile, her laugh. But I dont grieve it, no longer. Our own humours and hues slink a little here, latch a little there, but in a calm peace, where acceptance, time and pertinacity lie, so the world seems even, light, unwaivering, and our mind is not so caught or elate, for high or low.
 And so seeing her talk with Anthony and Alonza, no problem. Having her pass me by, so cute in our perception of response, made me sore yes, but no problem.
 And my own view is that life is nothing that can afford to give you leninancy nor fortune less your honest. And being here in the right is all that is best to do; but it must be tended, resisting the sirens of contrariety, and your ill-fit grundge. You must go through this moments that in the past would simmer your exholtion, or grip. And indeed, life has come to this way, to where death and oppertunity are actually placed. Such is the life which ought be lived. And a little care goes along way. Our natural temper and hue brought us into contact with Bella, as has it with very many peopel in the store. And so forth to our little community around. We carry much but in many ways stress little, and this slip of ours is not much more than a delay in offering a smile. For we are free, truly, from this grips that came from lacking liberty. "What made up for having no freedom."
So there is this odd notion, something grounding, pure and true, but also ideal and on that count, a little mysterious and obscure.
 Simply, my feeling is that there is this impetus to life, this trial, and thereby triump, this sort of dedication to move along and flourish.
 I found that in attempting this that our parents, and being at home, was a bit of a hinderance, as I could not practically subsit as I needed. But I also saw people with heart and charm who, at one point, I thought would take to me because of our initiative, but in any case, felt as though we wanted them near. It felt so terribly hard to accept our way and merely be friends, letting things go. Yet, the path itself encourages this. And so the charm of Bella is not so much a loss, as our path remains. It only ruffles things and makes that path a bit harder to see and tend to. But were back, in motion, aware.
 I don't know what other people do. I find in some part that there are those who are young and have fun, but are bored and tired. There are those more ambitious, but they are occupied and generally regal. You have that mix of adolescence where responsibility is dealt, but the purpose is perhaps taken for granted; and of the path your on and succeeding, so do you take this as freedom to have fun; but perhaps of a elaborate sort. This does not connect with me on any level.
 And indeed, our life is perhaps just in need of an orient. For friendship is dear, as is love and fraternity. But these things dont seem to remove the ebb and flow of things; they merely make our constance softer. Yet when were firm in our place, yet perhaps a bit tired here or dry there, we a) consider fundementals, as to what is really priority, and b) what our nature is, our aim, what it means to be as such constant. For it is not always well; virtue being the spring which breathes liveliness into this constance, making it both supple and strong.
 I find, for one, that those who are as such well to do and making well, are not neccessarily within simplicity. Nor is there vastness, if even of a rockstat, so much more than a pillar of activity. Rest and life still settle in, and sure, the commradery and fun are a solid thing to hoist upon your messy and or succeeding life. And in part this is preferred to what may be less worth hoisting, 'or if your ability is off'. But there is a pasture, a green if you would, that is bright and shining, full of simple compleixities and fabric, yet roaring in warm fires and rich garnaments. Modern life provides this without being consuming. Things akin to trading are no less oppertune, but have less ideal natures. Not all of them, but the effort required is not slight. And part of the weight which lay upon us is more from what we lack in common and acessible things; which indeed spurrs us to situate ourselves more promisingly; while also making do with the position we have. Hence the remark on priorities. For the winds of love and lost are dragging us down no longer, leaving only a natural residue; speaking to the fires within that need directing and tending to. But also to our affirment, our pasture, our grace. And indeed, our mind may wander, or justly humour the space further ahead. We merely contain ourselves, as though a duty that requires at least some attention, to our fortitude and balance here.
One of the most precious principles in life is that of the truth, and that all classical and ancient literature and theory were not wrong in attributing some sentiment of virtue and honor, hope and reprie, duty and militiance, but also humility and grace, and the propsects and humour, welcomed love and brilliant joy.
 I think we've lived a life which is dishonest, deceitful, uncomfortable, inappropriate in a mischevous but also ungallant way --if you'd seen my thoughts. Nor have we been circumspect enough as to control our temper, mind and view.
 It is all an odd story. One which is hard to determine value in. For we may say that our youth brought us down, but our of stubborness we held on to what we felt was peeling away. But in fact did little with that. Are we noble, yet immature and misfortuned? For one brutally honest school of thought would say that we were weak, lazy, looking for excuses, riding on the passtimes and comforts which our complacence fed off of, and that we weren't so strong; for had we been, we'd make resoltions from such sort. On the other hand, it is all to human and forgiving to say that we did not know. And that it was surely not out of gallantry that we had no woman, nor some measure of proud cyncism that bore us no success. It was a social matter, of which I still navigate today. For there was something about the folk at EME that did not persuade me, of theyre worth and my inlcusion. And novelty, mixed with the prestige and or precipe of important things around, 'that surrmounted our absent view of such friends and nice things', brought me away. And for prospective sake perhaps this was solid, as any plan seen through could treat. But we followed through not. I reckon had we gone to Pitt we'd have been equally complacent. But perhaps with more friends, more siutation in life. Instead, we banked ourselves on suitable conduct, moderate attnetion and success. Not much more. Socially we enjoyed things which fit with this cozy and sufficient way. We did not really try, nor care, nor were we deferant. Just confused, committed out of fear and fielty, unsure what else to do. Nothing so reckless or outrageous drew us otherwise. But again, life was not overly fair, and comfort and free time were all I sought. As a child in this state grows, they admitt the duty and amend, forming theyre wants in contenance with that. While those, or just for all in general, theyre lingers a acceptance of such deeds, while we live our life surrounding it. But it is not a life, merely a negation and or meantime to our deeds. That was our folly, that was our way. As life did come, and it centered on health, sums, the beginnings of writing and literature, and then through confidence furthered into adulthood ability, communication, but also soltiude, feeling lost, the rancour of creativity and history
Today was a nice day. I heard something from Bella, and for a moment felt a little crass, but it passed and we went on. A manner of cheer underlined the early morning, dipping only as we became relatively tired. Challed up to our fatigue from yesterday. In any case, I had some emotions regarding Bella, that I no longer would see her smile. But this did not perturb me, or move me, for I saw others, felt who saw me, and was overall, not so elated or distraught over apparent highs of other people, nor our own. The day felt even as such.
 But coming home, Knew what we had to do and was rather orderly and at rest with it. And as the days come to an end, I feel more than sturdy.
 But I see the trial of virtue, that she may not always be there; and that in history's tale of treating her so, that you may not have accrued what is natural per being; as our being has been quite mixed, generally in contrast, or in aversion, to things contrary to virtue; but without much of a forward stride where finer things and company could gather. And indeed we have much; but I dont quite feel myself there. At least, the priorities of mine are not so established, that we are in fact more present and able to rest.
 One thing of late which has offered quite a boon is that of regular but merely enough training. Once per week has really aidedme in increasing strenght, structure and muscularity. Our self confidence is untarnished, and I find myself leaning in, midly mind you, to the impulsive self importance from appearing so good. Which I find unneccessary, nor needed per your continuity. Indeed, it is like a bulber fishes light which we lurtch at, 'as the promise of popularity and pedigree dangles her possibility'. Vrture would have you steady and stable in your self-esteem. For virtue offers one soul thing, better than even the most firm benefits and ambition, 'that offer the highest rewards of that vain world'; and that is, that you may be free, in liberty, and of grace, via both flourishing steps and unafflicted community --the opposite of which comes when you feel you've done something wrong.
 Her way though is a little obscure sometimes, and perhaps the trimming of her leaves and picking of flowers is not well understood. But the gait if you would, the merry, the gleam, this is the root of all things known to be good or to be discovered. And in many ways, memory plays a role here, in both alleviating feelings of stress, 'for pain succedes, as are bad days forgotten, and new ones felt not so bad', but also in noting the harvest from prior 'up' moments (as it were), to which we find in these staler moments a need for calm, right remedy, but movement forward. Fundementals in life bring more stability to this, and afford a more common slope, and elements which are more uplifting. Our life has come and dips that way.
 But I think, in fairness, I notice when were off tiltere, a bit off the road so to speak, or stearing in a unsure fashion. Were just more aware in this slower days, where novelty and or attraction are less prevalent. Paired with fatigue, and we feel slow, but then grind against the demands of virtue. Perhaps were just to unfortunate not to have comforting things around us, 'for when were not'. That, or were just naturally weak and palish without motion. Or regret, 'which stains all sense of fortune', is so as to blind you of what you have, and bear too much attention to what you don't. That is indeed our current state with Bella. I don't mind her lack of attention in me, but I am not sure where my own attention should go. And the little bit of attention I have for her, has nowhere to go, or at least as much clarity elsewhere to be so small.
What is liberty but the time and place to do as you please.
 Per the ways of nature, we are either unending in our pursuit of satiety, or are subject, or part of, a collective, which organizes theyre effort to better achieve this; and the further this hope of proficiency goes the more we become subject to. But indeed, one finds that beside conscription and any regulatory checkpoints infront of oppertunity, that we may do as we please; and if such pleasure is limited only to what we have, we are still enriched with the time and effort to make enough out of it. "The sun sets and not even Hitler would hold back our sight."
 Moreover, the tandum we find with our medial aspects of life, be it chores, work, itinerary etc. health even, that so upon harmony with these, 'where those elements of rising above challenge, softening the load, elevating the reward, justifying the purpose', that so are we not only free to do as we please, but to be graced with the brightest of things, for we are all the stronger, sturdier, open and tuned, upon our slightest duties being well met.
 What is genius but the exuberant remarks and or impressions that come from this, where the meagerest of things pulls our mind, swells our heart, embolends our eye. This life is one of marks and inquiry, parsimony and contribution.
 And love, oh such is she the sweetest of things, but often mingled with passions of an unwarranted sort. For she gives us so much, yet in our abscences becomes this holy grail of remedy 'for all that would satiate what we need'. While liberty and eveneess create this calm and open stride, one which goes where it can and wishes, but in that, lurtches not, grips little, and from there, welcomes what it attracts or draws, and is amiable, respectfull. In a word, true love is bound in trust, for you are not mine, I am not yours, we merely see eachother, and hold one another in high regard.
 And then virtue, the hardest of elements to produce, is merely the appointment of all this, the memory of her success, the persistence when she fails, the tender balance of rest and fundementals when she is slow.
So i'd say that I am not happy. Its our schedule; its just a bit full. I want more time to scooter around, feel our mind open to see, to look forward to yoga and its trip, its benefit.
 I am thrilled that our balance of core and training are treating us so well. But I am a little fatigued. Indeed, our sessions have become quite larger than they've been in the longest time; well, but taxing. And swimming adds more to this. Little things like a lack of free range, and no longer doing soccer, make us feel a bit more heavy. But it is our constant work that is tieing us down. Short shifts call that, and idneed they don't make much ware on the day; but having to get up, and be somewhat confined as you see so many days like this, tends to ware on us. On one hand, our rent is still high, and so we can't afford that ever so precious 3 day per week. And I have just made a change that will hopefully add more space in the week. For work is find, pleasant, but its the long stretches of doing it which wares me. Litte breaks in between will help well. And the smoothness of our training allows for this nicely. I think of a day where there is more to do, more room to afford it, and more ease in the deeds around, so nice. For our leisure is more than fine, and I am feeling this swell of satiety. But were over-done, a little confined, and at heart a little off, as we feel the weight of this and what it lacks: there is no reign for false excitement or esteem. We know who we are though; and not much is taken away, even if your unsure of things. And you find yourself the truth, of which lesser in size, but is there, fair and real. This brings comfort and peace.
Something which riggles about is this sense of impertuity, which is to say, that on a good day, a good feeling, with good sense of folk around, that not everything is perfect. You may find a moment that is overhwelming, or damning, or unerving, or pitying. And much of writing serves to mend these times, for they don't often speak too much, besides footing we lack. For instance, we saw Mo having this chat with Tara, and someone else was there to, and when I combined this with hearing him and Nick talk about soccer, or someone else, maybe Rohan, talking with Darren at the desk, I realized that this was not some over the top thing. By all counts, the source of our happiness was being amidst this flow. There may be something said as to why you speak with who you or do not, but generally speaking, our openeness finds itself wherever it may be. This whole misgiving with Bella comes down to a struggle in accepting this. Which in part comes down to us never actually wanting to just let things be, but feel important and impressive. She made me feel not; like I was not the center. But good riddens; this is neither true, nor treating. A core element is that there is a thread to life, and that our pasture of peace and happiness comes from threading it. There isn't much else, and remarks that notion of elementary school but as an adult. The idea that, 'if I had a girl, or money, or was impressive, or did this or that', feels more like someone who's mind is on far things, and fails to see that they are bound to theyre own thread. They are not so special. And indeed, I wish to be happy by living simply, doing as we please; and I care for work, as it is required, but is full of warmth and company, and perpetuity of this is something which makes me glad. Tuning ourselves to this, or making it our way, has been ever so hard; as our hope for things has never been so absent, nor our happiness so accessible without standards that blended well with work; for which we felt closed and aloof. We secretly wanted attention and reciprocity in love to furnish this isolated state. But getting in, breathing high and letting your arms touch the far walls, we are not so enclosed, begging, nor cynical and peering. It is a active moral, that doing what you ought relieves you from the hinderances that come from not doing so. Our yougner age afforded us to have such delights amidst doing what we shouldnt have.
 I feel a little bit of instability, but not so much. Bella's appeal and enamour, 'her outing of fun she has', is a critical blow to our confidence and absent-position, 'where we are not on the thread'. But this ought turn you away, and indeed, bring more reason and life to regularity, calm standard, industry and pleasure that is worthy and filling; and from there, things of a far or near sort, or oppertune, may be more solid and of substance, for we only see and attend to what matters, 'being in the mud of things'.
So, viewing wise, Game Of Thrones is sitting there, deepening like Red Wine. Star Trek is almost done, and getting back and ready for an actual run of it. Beginner servers is great: i blieve there are 2 more, and there is a library of hilarious videos. I also see myself getting back into Ark. We can always come back to Guild Wars --the crafting is a great through line. Battlefield and Diablo aren't on my mind, and for Path, I want my build to be defined so the scale is the only issue; it's actually very fun playing it, and me and Victor have a good time. Cold Rampage seems the goal, but we still have some grasping to do. Teen Wold was quite nice, and I just dont want serve our immediate interest. This second season is really nice and I'd like to sink my teeth into it. Tomorrow or the next seems fine. We'll surely play Path tomorrow, off day sunday with core, training monday, off tuesday.
 For World Cup, knowing who is playing who is great social currency; it gave me a little in with Nick and Mo, maybe Samir and the boys too.
 Music wise, Guild Wars is pretty much done. Elder Scrolls online is a heartbeat away from fueling my curreny peace in life, and bringnig our norm to a steady cheer. Mammals too and all things really just need a sorting, into a collectio. We need no slow, just the primary pieces.
 Friends per second keeps going on, and VGC is nice, as is Schreier and Unlocked. These are all good current things, with GTA coming around, and the Xbox closures coming up. But this year end for FPS is a good lead up of things. The old days raise theyre head also.
 Game wise, Kingdom Come is quite lovely, and each step I take it deepens its promise. THe look of it is quite swell, though it really takes its time. I am not sure if PC or PS5 is the right path, but I see a nice purchase of it ahead. Space Marine, despite getting me into the universe, and looking forward to the Total War game, which itself has sparked my eye for Turin, is nice, but the game is not my favorite, so less invested in purchasing that. Doom has been told as quite great, and some of the negativies seem fine to me. That is a good steam sale. Indiana Jones and Avowed are cheap rentals; one being this really cool adventure, the other a fun little rpg.
 I see alot of promise in watching great films along with Classics. We watched Terminator some time ago, but Aliens, AVP, Matrix, Jurassic Park, some lovely films like Rudy, Sixth Sense. The hobbit is one of those sweet little treats, which I've not often the time for. Phantom Menace would be great. Surrounding media would be cool also. That long form vid is a good pair.
 Show wise, Andor is a near target, and so many are avaialble on Prime, Apple, HBO. The dinosarus was really good --though a 123 platform is hard to find now.
 I will note also that we are writing our Sum paper. The outline of it is quite vast, and the switch from principle to volume holds the obscurity I need to clarify. I think it quite well. A prelimary email that states we found something and are looking for feedback, with some preface'd points that can station the rhetoric you'd otherwise use during the paper. I find this a far yet true promise, eager in my creative mind. The work has been well.
 And lastly, as for reading, there are in fact many essayists and writers; Thoreau may not be to my liking, but a man named Hazlitt was surely. We may add means to explore and save such pieces. Bringing Anna to the back grass has been nice, but our tablet could also do well.
For brevities sake, France is playing Paragruay, who then plays the victor of Canada and Morocco. USA plays beligum, the victor playing the winner of Portugal and Spain. The winner of this will play the winner of that prior bracket. Likely Spain vs USA, perhaps Portugal, and almost surely France.
 Brazil plays Norway, the winner of which plays the victor of Mexico and England. Argentina plays Egypt, the victor of which plays the winner of Switzerland and Colombia. Likely Argentina vs Colombia, perhaps the Swiss, and Brazil is apt to beat Norway; England and Mexico is a coinflip. Of those two teams, the victor between them and Brazil is likely to play Argentina.
 As a finale, its likely Spain or France, maybe Portugal, though I don't think they'd beat France. Mexico could beat England, and perhaps Brazil, but Argentina is likely to move forth.
What can we say, except for mixed emotions, feelings of loss; yet of regret, it's wofting away, leaving our heart and soul. But what's left is not so secure, nor certain. It's as though we are free to love, but unsure where to; and this brings back memory of pain that left us.
 In part, I am reminded of the way of things, of this perpetual motion, this constant state of flow, and that in many ways, all that is good comes from some abandonment of 'ignoring rules', and seeking and or delighting in that which comes upon things benig well. As though our troubles and oblige are forogtten. That, and ironing out the rought edges of our conception. The matters here are not what's essential, merely our form within things. Nothing is so pure, nor so special, nor are we high above, nor others below. Its this thing about our lives, lacking what we can hold onto, yet lacking also the rule which makes all things unneccesary. They just are.
Just to mould a bit of substance, one clear issue, or overestimate, is on our own view of firends; and not so much as regards other people, as thoguh we shouldn't feel so jealous based on what they have, but rather our solemness and critique, per what we feel like we should have and are missing.
 For most people talk about something. Age groups and similarities spur this. We talk with Alex about Destiny, Oliver about Soccer, Jacob about walks and the weather. So I like the idea of beginning with the principle. The idea is essentially to present what a repeating seqeunce is via the mechanism of clocks, or the reoccurence rule, then to show that this effect occurs in volumes, and within families.
 The idea of the fibinocci sequence is perhaps not formulaic, as it is literal, in that you start adding 1,1,2,3,5. The idea though of starting with those terms and adding subsequently is what needs clarification. It is hard to speak of 'add two starting terms, then the two foremost terms'. This idea is not so simply defined. 'Akin' to the fibinocci feels right but this whole aspect needs to be more straightforward.
 Comparing a cardinal/ordinary line with a reoccuring one seems useful, as it speaks to the clock like nature. The notion of a binary line, whereby the values are always 1 or 0, yet the 10th term may be so, per the index, but at any rate be of 0 or 1. Clarifying the objective value of 0 or 1 with the position is to our aid. Speaking of this clock like mechanism is the token to further demonstration. It needs to be clear and concise, and need as little elaboration as possible. One element that brings us further is the idea of linking the purpose of a point to its explanation/cause. If were speaking of adding on a clock, rather than outline what that clock is, use a method of clarity per that clock so much as a further point (which the clock serves) to almost complete the point of the clock at all.
 In esscence, were adding terms in sequence, as though going around a clock. I feel the idea is clear enough that a standard 12 hour clock need not be used. Though, this seems to be so that were holding off on the elaboration of ranges of clocks, and the letter system for double digit. Given that we are not introducing the assumed operations to begin, we can literally use whole terms, and perhaps use a 12 hour clock. The principle is no different.
 One element which I still struggle with, as though the aim of this whole process is unclear, that we still feel like we have to prove the principle before assuming that the volume of findings can be shown.
 One way to do it, is so far and simple as the principle is to show, that we could make a literal claim, that of such principle demosntrated, where it extends to, and that for demonstration purposes of that, we may instill our reasoning, nomenclature and notation. For at that point you are truly saying, 'this thing I just showed you, there is much more, but I need to present it in this way, and use these terms to refer to various areas/domains'.
 For it may be said, that of a starting state, whereby initial groupings of terms are added subsequently [and of this foremost sort], that doing so as though on a clock will create a point of repition, whereby the initial state is returned to. Within each clock, or rule of reoccurence, and within pairings of terms, ie. doubles, triples etc. that within each group the point of repition is the same. We call the range of clock a class and the lenght of pairing order. So within class nine 2nd order (doubles), every variation of starting states will repeat at the same point as others in the group.

So we start with more or less with an initial plea, that given a starting state, of two terms, and added couply in subsequence, that if we do so upon a reoccuring line, compared to say a cardinal one, that the starting state will return. The point can be made that this claim is not so absolute; but the starting states that don't apply have not yet been discovered; or are generally of volumes beyond sensibility.
 Given this, what we can do is alter the range of the line, 'adjusting the clock so to speak', and within any such range, change the extent of the starting state, and thereby degree to which it is added; ie. with two starting terms we added couply, or thirdly if there are 3. On top of that, per the range of line and degree of starting terms, we have the variation/combination of such terms. And within all of that, we recognize not only that at least up to class 20 and order 5 that every variation of starting state will repeat, but that, for each combination within an order, in a certain class, that each given starting state will repeat at the same point as all others.
 In reflection, what I find intriguing about all of this, is that to say everything succinctly requires that you say more than little. It may be vanity, or trepidation, but saying more feels safe, as you feel convincing. But the reality is, that we want to show how a starting state repeats using the reoccurence principle, how to classify the variation of these elemnents: class being the range of line, order being the extent of starting terms, and sequence/combination marking the variations of such states, or a class and it's orders. We then want to show the equinimity of repition, whereby all states within each order of a given class, will repeat at the same point as all others in such group.
 The idea that we are taking some couple or trio etc. of terms, and per that extent summing or adding that many --meaning foremost, and thereby progressing with the new addendum-- is it's own wording that could use shorthand. As well, understanding that triple and couples of class 9 repeat equally; but that this means that the couples of class 9 repeat equally while the trios have theyre own point of equality. This is in fact the distinction, or thing needing shorthand. The trios of class 8 don't overlap very meaningfully

Now that I've sunk back though, I think perhaps we are but a whisp, and strange as we are distant. And indeed, we are not in fact that far away. We work together well enough and are fair to one another. But our weird moves to reconcile, or at least be unhampered, go no where, and leave me with this perception that she is mad; which then, almost blatantly, but at least by our own view, impresses us with later action of avoidance.
 But the point is a fair and practical one; which I stand on, almost in the same way had I accepted her heart already being mine, and seeking nothing more. I care that way for Matin, more or less Tara, and I feel calm and fine to be welcomed and generous to carry, carli, Crisha somewhat, Joey, Alex, Andy, Tristan when he's not being a little shit, Max in commradery, Chenoya in her rather dull yet nice company, and many more; the list goes on, and even in are darkest glare, we see there is much more. And livening ourself to this relieves the grasp of such shaodowd, and allows us not only to find peace in the light, but life in, and from that, calm and due readyness, 'for we feel like we've won'.
 I think that perhaps the root of this tale is one in which we make the right amend. Which is not to maintain nor continue towards that root of company and fondness which we had; to trust eachother, hear one another out, but to merely be as you can; unafraid as we were in the past, and in that, feel open and unavoidnant (yourself). This girl is not overhwelming to me. And in treating this, our truest heart may flutter: for we are grieved nor stricken not but the pull of a thread to our actual tune. Were playing that now, confided by the notes which our harboring melody sung: such chords either are or feel apt and gentle to take part in our just procession. And life and love, weirdness and wonder, mystery and relief, come as the property of justice becomes reconginzed: like the feeling of a shirt fitting well. Such is the wind in your sails. Choppy have the seas been
So I found a pretty basic thought, and that was I feel a little off about people, unsure of my place, wanting attention, yet not always wanting to share, but in that, feeling weird that I don't, or jealous of those who do, feeling ontempt towards them even, and then a little sullen about ourself in that we have some want but forgo.
 Surronding this is an air of self confidence, which in unkept ways, interjects me into things, and otherwise keeps me shielded from the impression of feeling off or left out. Mixed in this is our own directive and aim, which brings our favor for such things out; as on one hand we find it less accessible, perhaps uncommisery; on the other, our mind is just elsewhere, so we don't have much care.
There is much more to say, see, do, gleam. More good days to be had, reflections to make, improvements to take. All in big or suttle ways. We may become more kind and gentle, but also calm and with right and loving perspective, of both your tenure and way at work, with the people day, with your idea of self, oppertuinty, progress, creation, goals and high amends. And so may much substance form around this. Had we not asked out Bella, not much would have changed. We'd be in the same spot, balancing along. I realize that much is in fact lost on us, in how we've come to be. The nature of this is so revealling, but also troubling. In part because it is hard to embrace the familiar side. But the other, having softened in how we were, is not itself a soul destination. It is more about a gait, and the sort of pairing of sense and ability, as to know what is right and worth expecting; not by rule but understanding, as you know what to say or feel about something; it becomes your nature, rather than some brace or scale. And much which I'd describe as the good life flourishes from here, or takes hold at any rate, and you find yourself remarking things with the farthest of folk. And indeed, not all become friends. But in part that is just who we are; and not all are so different. I have a hard time, as I suspect envy and insecurity, as it comes to the young, or those more bold and jubilent. The truth in them often gets obscured.
What is worth saying, when nothing is naturally being said, is that so much more is to come. You often are blind to this, or of the feeling that it is not. But it really just marks the day. And sometmies those are so well, that we pass by the fact (and our memory), that this is where things begin happening, where inquiry is made, books are found, trust and insight are carved and folded into your day. Where weeks become months, and years go by, where not a drop of pithy or shame is noted. Like Porn, who has left poor foundation, but at any rate lingers only in crevaces of our impulse; for it has been some time since we departed, and the drip of her past tenure is little felt. Such can be our life. And indeed, we've been young, poor in thinking or choosing, and perhaps all to clever and bright; for happiness has not been a stranger to me, nor has it been pleasure which has seldom grazed my side. Rather, it is a life which becomes unbroken, immutable, collective to the things ripe for our nature and circusmtance. Where life goes now so it could have been. And so I remind you not so much of what may come, but that in that coming it will be so, often, through your high and able hand. Such is the basis for feeling tall and standing, virulent, vital, and savy in your bending of all this. Were not laying tracks, but behaving as a man, and adding layers to us being so. "The leaf needs no will or exertion to blow with the wind; it's how he's made." And by all counts, we are ourselves a source of mystery and comfort, be it in literal masterbation, or the feeling of peace and ease. But by all counts, as men, beings, animals no like, what defines us and holds all backing to our acts and inquiry, is that of substance, which can only be said to exist and bare relevance by our particular placement in the world. Things to mend with, tradition to sing to, or perhaps differ; people to appreciate, heed warmth from, books to find, things to see, near and in your mind far. One's history is perhaps nothing more than the path they've taken in respect to all these. For one may have forgone post-secondary, for which theyre life has gone such. But we all do things. And the weight of this or that matter is not itself too important. For we may feel now or then this or that way about this or that thing, and that is but some honest remark; which on it's own, is it's own thing to understand --why things taste sweet at all, and please us in being so. But we may be observant, and upon that, magnificent in our discovery, of what it is we actually do, and of what were doing how it is based upon what things had been. And from there, we may make what is all too novel and esteemed, but often overestimated, and that is how things will be. For this is nothing more than the promise and faith, or perhaps solemness, about how things will be now some time ahead. "The future present."
Life is marked by the way you weild it. As it goes on and and, and you are like a substance, a fabrci, a jell, and it droops if you dont' bring it right. At any rate, it moves this or that way, and the fairer it does, the more spry you will be upon all things; and foresmot to those things which require it.
 I don't mean to speak of fundementals, here at least. I sit on the floor; that is a choice I made long ago, naturally it seemed. And indeed, I have felt often fine, and swell almost as such. But there is natural difficulty, as you find in any combination of exertion. Training for isntance in tandum with work is like this. And the point is a moral one, or at least of resolution, whereby you helm the seems as to be of great quality. For you may care little for weaving and fabric; but life is then boring, or requires ultiamtely some other form; as our tenure is of liberty and wellness, while the matters of profession and buisness require but a different sort of attention: but some no less. That, or we are either dull, or sunk into pleasures of a consuming or novel sort. And the point perhaps, is that so much as we are living well, that all that matters are the elements in our perview; things to handle and apply ourselves towards.
 A little idea came to me earlier, similar to that notion of choosing a few moves to do well rather than many. It came down to asking, 'what is enough, if done, assumedly regularly, but perhaps thats just a given'. The idea relates to exercise, in that we find ourself thinking that certain things are essential, or perhaps just novel; or maybe they are useufl if you can afford it. Swimming for instance has never been something we could incorporate despite its value.
 We work often, and indeed, the amount is not so much important as is our attitude. For stability, or harmony, brings with it true excess, where characters and worlds are open to us, as do we gander for sights and scenery, and sit calm in our general approach, 'feeling the mist of commradery and fellowship'.
 We also train, and for reasons barring certainty. It is one thing to say that our life on the floor demands this. It is another to say that having to work bids me do this. And in combination, that whether the floor brings more focus or not, that so is such might of mind and care something I desire, regardless of the means. And work being an allotment, and of the hardest kind, that so the needs and advantage for that blend itself with that motive for focus; as we otherwise find our mind swallowed by the brittle effort of work. And the floor is just an extension of that, no different than if we sought the stability to perform recreation outside our duties; or what is required in practice for anything. Floor sitting benefits our mental craft, namely in reading, writing, study, making things, viewing things short and long, investing our selves in general. This can be brought to further motion, in our scenic abodes, as is the pleasantry of other people as equal a sight. But it is less so, in our way, of working, followed either by social gatherings, where food, drink and gabber are served; or it is in recreation, namely some sport. There are social things that are more pleasing to me and fruitful, as is there recreation which is softer, and at any rate, of enough interest with affordable effort. "Hiking, for instance, is something that I don't extend myself to. Once in a while, but nothing more. And life, for me at least, need be lived in the time between."
 Generally, I find that our practices are quite easily met, and simple in theyre form and extent. It is the rising efforts that fair the most difficulty, as they are not defined nor concrete, nor easy to come by without an aid to such definition. What I find though is that life, when lived, flows naturally, and takes to the simple offerings of this sort. Saying that there is some form or manner in which such aids be brought by is near exhaustive, and not so neccessary. It is similar to practice, where in that case, we speak of bar work for instance, and how it is important and useful to do, as is core and running, but that the gains we need, in vain even, are achieved through a per week frequency, and not much more. I've instilled, or just recently established a yoga practice, in hips (for hamstrings and hip flexors), yin (often had leading into our work week), a flow session to emphasize downward dog, and warrior, to bring ease to our lunging. Prana is also being considered. The point of these practices is to instill and cultivate a prescence and standard of such movmenets; no different than the strenght offered from our training practice. This yoga practice is not suspect on it's own, but its accomplice of rising efforts, or minor ones we'll say that reflect less of a regiment, but rather a ordering, or better put funneling (via an aid) of our want and whim, 'as to move as we please or feel need to'.
It is interesting, and nice, that as we think about 'having something say', as though, were we not to, that it'd be because we were sleepy, or just too stricken to put out our thoughts, 'that they were all clumped in', that so when we do have thoughts and they come out free and smoothly, that so is it the same for interests, wonder, excitement, pleasure and peace, sense and security, confidence and comfort.
 In general, I see that the practice is there to instill and maintain our condition, and to serve as a reminder but also mark ahead. But this cannot be all, for we often have want of doing something, or, in tandum sometimes, with a feeling of need, as upon returning from work, and today for instance, we just did Chill, and it was nice; but we may then feel we need to treat our legs. And these aren't harsh efforts, nor much confusing. Theyre also not a practice, or something you have to plan or look to. It is like food, in that you know the pieces and slots to place things; our general view is such. And there may be neccessary matters, per a practice or training, or something clear point where this or that food is needed. But we may just look forward to doing chill. Active matters may garner less clarity in preperation, 'outside of practice', but we may still do it, if only when a moment to concieve effort and rise comes about. Such is the point of an aid, that it affords ease to that volition, and gives structure to it, so it is beyond a moment, but more akin to a sequence. The breathe most dearly benefits from this.
 And the points in which I need things are quite vaired, and although unknown in theyre limits of possibility, so are certain ones clear. Coming home from training, we often see need to tend to our shoulders and neck, and allow our body to rest, in the hips notably. A great point is that following work we often find need to tend to our legs; we may just want rest, 'for which Chill is nice', but we may also want a twist, and rub our feet. The point though, is that this is something we often seek following training. Less crucial it seems, but something between want and need: nice. And so what satiates our need following work may also welcome itself following our slightly different want upon training. And all things work like this. But we ought prioritize what those certain moments need. For we may use the morning sessions in the evening; but they should be formed for what the morning seeks. And indeed it is often not much. Per the aid, it is far more to do say a twist or a brief transition of morning seated, then to do this on your own. The aid brings focus, deeper breathe, plus a sense of clarity and comfortness: as though your actually doing something.
It must be girls, who strike my mind with so much fancy. Who else brings grievance? Do you really pitter over the ruckus and bantering of Mo and Paul? Do you feel lesser? Perhaps it is a perception, or sense, that if girls are invovled, that such thing is more value'd. I don't believe in any case that anyone has such a feeling or view.
What I'd remark upon food is that it is quite varied in what it can offer, and by all counts, is not the limiting factor. Indeed, such factor surrounds our fatigue; and so much as we are short of respiration, so does our diet need to change. For aerobic capacity allows us to make use of slow-absorbed energy, while being fatigued benefits from that which absorbs faster. The options are not vast for each. Potatoes are quite starchy, and indeed trouble us in theyre wholeness when fried. Boiling may better do, when strucutre is important. Bread similarly has this softening effect, yet is sometimes what we need. And it may be that we need whole bread, as in blue silver hills, or bread that is less fiberery, such as buns. Wheaty bread, such as that whole wheat from langley market, or the itlian soft bread foremost, is filling to a rather sullen degree. Quite unideal for any kind of rigor.
 In any case, it is clear, though sometimes put off by what happens to or needs to come prior, that leading into that days end, out of 8 usuallly, is prime for some collective of grain. Namely, split peas are soft and pair great with barely, and quinoa remains a delight. Earlier in the day we benefit, from a nourishment standpoint, of lentils and edemame plus corn. The practical effect of this is not so damning either, and indeed, when I think of the movement we should do prior to this, it is so that we are able sit more easily, and at any rate breathe more vibrantly during our digestion.
A root instance, or center if you will, to our thoughts, seems apt.
 Simply, if we have the view, and the kind of sense and regard, that people around me are there to be impressed by me and take to me (sexually or in infatuation), than we surely are coming from our own heavy self-perspective, as though all that there was was what sat around me, while we were the primary center. "As though the world were dark, and the only thing visible were from the light of me." Whereas, if we are moved and kept by a sort of place amongst all people, where we are not so heavy in our selves, but more open, giving, amicable, and from that, parsimonious and flowing with each and all, than our hold is not so seeking nor possessing. And one conflict that arises when theyre is debate over the two, is if we tend to the latter, then we feel as though we are giving up what we hope to possess by the former; moreover, we feel in that case that what we seek is somewhat owed to us, or natural to have, and thereby we feel envious thoughts of those who may possess them, and we feel pithy at our lack of trying. Further, we feel this sense of scrutiny and shame over ourselves, as though we were giving up this more challenging route for one more broad and gentle. "Why give up on the pursuit."
Nothing really matters more than the reign of our life, its view, our past, the path of it and how its come about and moves further. All can be explained by this, and much of our uncertainty seeps from it.
 One notion though is that the effect of such path, in the present, is that we feel exposed to certain truths no longer worth living by. That, or we see aspects of us which are unformed, and not taken at heart like other things. Vice seems to have influence over these elements, 'as if they are more persuadable'.
 The whole of my life, though a little obscure, can be described by a stature, a strenght, a kindness and cheer, but a seperation, distance, uninvovlement with things; and in this, many qualities of of such state came to be, in cynicism, aversion, a bit of selfishness, and high esteem. We found some soverignty in this when life became untenuable, and from there, we've been more or less happy, but relatively alone. And it was not because our inability to be social, but that we did not like many people. And one senitment that feels true, is that we felt quite detached and different from the whole of people, that those who we did like were not garnished as friends. We held an esteem and anticipation as remarked the whole, but were not calm and definite enough to merrily be, and in that, form more particular connection. We have and we did, but none of it every felt deep. The issue really, is that much of our confidence and expression came from our center, which was quite formatted as to be personally austere, but in that, outwardly esteemed. I found it easy to connect but not really to bond; or perhaps it was the other way around. The point, is that I felt that there was always part of me, the heart at least, which was hidden; which lead to a certain feeling of discomfort, and consequent to that, a lingering pressure that eventually moved me to somewhere new and less weighing.
 This choice though, or these choices, to remain untenured, lead to subsquent moments of similar standing; where connection would form but would not take. And all I can say, is that what has changed in the later part of the age is our fixing of principle and way, especially in the world of things. Our views of nature and god, government and war, health and liberty, money, and soon woman, came about. And what occured, is that we have found ourself ready in ourself, and not perturbed by the differences of others, in theyre contrary enthusiasms as mine. People expell what is welcomed to them; and how we like to expell ourselves, naturally binds. That, or theyre is humbleness and courtesy, general community too I find. And this is where all lives and swells, as you feel sure and free in yourself, to bond yourself with more people and in a meaningfull way; and of those more casual, it is not upon our exhaultion or confidence, but more fair and relaxed emotions and sociability. We are young in this, for we are so personally formed that surpassing the natural firmness (that contradicts the intertia born of solitude), that simply time has not gone by where this was so. An age it's been of being ourselves, but only to me. And gradually things do change, but again, nothing has ever stuck. Now I feel in a far reaching flow; one which is home to things which expell all feelings of loss of wanting, 'for some place other'. But we also feel in tune with oppertunities and care of substance, and general fortune. This is the novel swells of lifes natural up and down; but we are merely reminded, 'as though someone wise were in fact king, and we drew some pleasure by the grace and constance of having such crown.'
So Nature is a sweet and cozy address. Not too long. Similar to English traits, in that it is meant to be read bit by bit. Each part not being too long. And there's just new things to find here, more thoughts, embers of ideas.
 The American Scholar has always been a favorite of mine, but is not what I'd like to focus on. Some of the addresses are quite long, and I recall some of them not hitting me as I'd like. The Young American and Conservative feel like pieces that could offer us something. And for each, it could have just been the day when we read it. Theyre all quite well, and fairly different the more specialized essays. Theyre broader speakings, and thus hold more room for impression.
 The first of Essays is Self Reliance; which may be all to rewarding and consuming on it's own, but is worthy no less. When I read this before 'compensation' stuck out to me, as we were quite idle and looking for words that elevated our solitude. But the one of Love, albeit suspect of far reaching sentiment, may hold a branch or two of insight and inspiration; friendship even moreso. "I'd be happier if the latter showed me what we lack and what things could be than of the former. I don't know myself, or accept things so gratefully, enough to feel as open as love needs. Yet bits of it squirt out, and run on swirving and tired grounds: and the knot never takes." Prudence is an interesting one. Not something I feel the need for, but of interest on the face of it. Circles, Intellect and Art feel both relevant and potential for inspiration. As the idea of enthusiasm feels like this near yet unmeasured aspect, which could run quite complimentary to more personal acquintence. "OFt it is the mystery or obscurity of things which draws negative feeling, not so much what you actually do or do not have. Its the uncertainty of whether that is just." Intellect may align with our calmer and reasonable views. We mentioned that there is always a step ahead, new qualities to give light to, a way to see things and a form to have that breathes stronger, stands higher, all from an point of greater competence and ease. But so of our intellect, as regards more novel or basic pursuits, so may this bring out our mind, and afford a blend of umph and simplicitiy. Then art, which may tie all things together, combines the aspect of fufillment and expenditure, and thereby station in life and your manner of amends.
Theres this thing about pleasure, that despite not being so poor in some things, is in itself not worth much esteem. For it is not equal to 'what we like, or want to do'. At least that latter part is quite seperate.
 Pleasure seems to be in something you have, or consume, or dream about. It comes from our loins, our seeking heart, laughter to. And indeed pleasure is found around, but it is often hard to acquire. At least I find myself seeing things which would please me. And the perspective on this is hard to rightfully avow. For we may say, 'all pleasure is bad, our desire is off'. Or, 'these are amongst those pleasures deeemd worhty, yet we cannot obtain them. For we are either ill-equiped, under-develooped, subject to chance, or unable to spend the time and resources to do so. That, or given the nature of that pleasure, there is much around it which I am either averse to or uninterested in.'
 One of the troubles I've had in our adult life, is that we still live by our own, rule and stead that is, but also in experience and delight. And what happens is that what we truly like and wish for requires so much, 'however easy', that we feel less ingrained or enthused as our counterparts around us. It may just be age, as older people aren't often any different, and I find it easy to connect with them on theyre own occupied level. But it is yougner folk who have more enthusiasm and playfullness; within work this seems like a desired quality, but just in life to. Yet it is revealled to me that your just a bit too drawn to the gleam of it, per the pleasure, and similar to porn, or seeing someone beautiful, with someone else, there is one ember that sparks part of you that has a hard time keeping things un blazed. And as the fire reeps, you engorge that one aspect, a bit naieve and unfamiliar that theyre is so much more. For indeed, my life is not burdened by pleasure it lacks, but by pleasure we see and long for. We are well fed, but upon a smell find ourself starving.
It is a simple fact, when even the lightest intent is on my mind, or at least tamber if you will, 'as though every wisp of wind would pluck our tender string', that so we see all that is in front of me, and innate to this, are the things we ought to, which we have, namely in eating through the day, moving as to facilitate movement, and indeed, borders of regards, in when we sleep, 'be it on an off day or not', and likewise if we mean to game, go for a ride, get something done, like training. And what I find is that nothing is really sought from me when were in this tune. Much of the pleasure which we reach for, or feel somber about not having, enters someone elses mind, but not my own. Much of its ticket is to one who has nothing to do. And indeed, I feel that way sometime; but memory is a guiding star hear, as there is something to do, whether we know it, and so being swayed to do what is ill or uneccessary because your out of tune right now, is not so welcomed. Surely the string looses its flourish during the day; and part of learning is in fairing insight as to what a) you can do in such moment, b) what can strenghten the string as not to become flat, and C) what is neccessary, essential, principle to begin with, so that if we are flat, we at least know what to play, and may use our whit and whim, 'our humour and hue', to move towards something known and near. When were off though and unsure, or unchecked in our mind, than even the farthest away thing feels close, 'as one without breathe would see air on another planet as pulpable'.
One of the odder notions in life is that of oppertunity. For it comes with certainty as a child, as though we have no need to consider the reality of things, and can just dream as our trajectory permitts. But as an adult you find that certain things are not so accessible, and if they are, it does not excatly jive with other essential things, or preferred ones.
 Indeed, nothing is harder to describe than the balance one can have, in theyre grand but also personal duties, and how when blended whole, leave one feeling as though everything is dealt with, yet they have no work at all. It is a smooth life, one with pace, and indeed much comes about, in little relishes here, little efforts there.
 And I'd say that this life can be fruitful, but it is not contigent on it. It is parismonious, progressive, natural, and merely growing, as a tree does with sap, 'whereby it hardens, forming a wider shell'. And it feels that the basis for your stability, or smoothenss rather, determines wherher you really are free in your process. For if not, and your like a child who is given things, which is itself a temporary status, than it is hard to truly be pleased and drawn, for goods that flicker themselves from virtue, liberty and reason. Indeed, as morals come from the heart, and take fashion frmo our resourcefullness, 'as though our umph of morality was a problem we wished to solve', that so in our umphs of sums, treatment, the moon, or things of effort, or love making, so our time and attention is spent. But it comes from the heart, our interest, our way. And such movments, or beats, are most agreeable when they arrive from a balanced state. For it is not about grief or criticism that this or that motive is shouldered off, but rather, when it comes from an absent of things we hold preferred and true, then the pull we have outside of this feels like were being moved away from such things, and the condition which it invokes. For such a tune breathes and speaks of all things at once; for nothing is sought which cannot be, nor should be held back against. It is like a machinery to puts out what it can, and thus anything made is by definition a timely and welcomed good. And there is so much. But when the gear is off and something comes out, 'falling half way up the track', no matter what it is coated in, nor how much we feel drawn to it, 'given the nature of the track, and how it is we who remark it being on or off', that so do we tremor at the thought of consuming it, for we accept the status of the track which produced it, and thereby distance ourselves from the harvest of a straighter path.
My thoughts are quite well. I must admitt there is a slight intertia to my mood, regarding Bella, pleasure, the imbalance of our want and seeking people.
 It is strange, that you feel yourself somewhat imposed upon them, with infamy and valor. But otherwise, you feel eager and enthused, as though you can be present with them in a relieving or pleasing way. And in part this is true; but it ought be more natural, rather than forced. Constancy permits this to accrue naturally; as your not always going to be so buddy buddy with everybody. But everyone may be something, and time deepens all.
 In the case of Bella and I, as an assessment we are more than fine, comparitively at least. The pain that tugged at me and weirdness that fluttered about has generally dissipated. And I recall that much of our strife came in acquiesing to such state; for when we did, we were flushed with a sense of regret and jealousy; and so in response we ordained some sense of 'return to normal'; and this lead to that all too ill and fleeing sensitivity, of her care or lack there of. What I'd say now is that we are amiable. Not friends, but on par for things. There is a sediment, a toxin so to speak, that will take time and neutral action to dissipate; right now it collides with normal efforts. I find with Mikaela that I would in part like to ask her personal questions, 'deepen the bond as it were'. But I am not only in check but generally centered and unmoved, for which my need to ask, paired with the abscence of a moment to do so, compells me not to wait for one, nor fret that we are not. That is the difference you see; not to be in conflict or contrast to something, 'as though you are dealing with'. Rather, of what is called for, able and offered, you are fine and pleased to assume, but not thrown by some sense that there is nothing more. That is there with Bella still. And indeed, it is an adjustment to not being so void of her while also not being so endowed. We merely are. And in settling to that, where normal motion becomes the norm, we are fidgety, a little spurry in our embers, 'as though sparks from pieces clicking in, shedding off our excess'.
So I loo forward to this coming day. What rays may shine, what melody and mood will come to our day. What divets we may smooth out a bit, what thoughts may come to mind. Who may I see: Andy, Joey, Tara, Carli, Jacob, Andre, Emma. Oliver to talk soccer with, maybe Mo, Arun even. And it is so nice that something so naturally grieving, or at least challenging in its essentiality, is so sweet and nice, and soft in the areas commonly rough. In part it is me, but I am then quite pleased, as what brings me to feel well, beyond mind and habit, are our choices; and it is its own form of niceness that such things are known and regular (by theyre principle and action). I cant ignore this relatively clear thought, and that is, by our own grace and stride we feel sturdy and of cheer; yet we don't always exhault this to all people; generally only those were familiar with. Something became quite clear today, and that was that work is hard. You reach this low point, the dip as it were, where you feel hungry and tired, and everyone around you is a bore. Tired am I, and perhaps a fool to write. For what could I better garner than some rest, to allow my mind to settle, experience how it really is, and if firming is needed here or softening there, then to do so, but upon a more circumspect and rigorous state. Right now were weary, tired, spent.
 Yet I have clear thoughts, and enough focus to retain our path of the day. Perhaps were only weighing down further; but I feel this makes room for those truer parts of our mind to settle.
 For one, today was a good day. There was challenge, but rightfully so, for truth came out. Nothing negative. Something which came to mind, is that pleasure, or this sort of happiness in seeing people, is an ever fickle, and often overemblished status. We are not so solid or true beneath. Perhaps none are away from this. But something did occur, a sort of grace and honor of our duty and way. Not so it was deemed small, nor us stronger; but that it was itself true, soverign in its call to commisery. By that, it is our task to respond; but it is the fairness of the oblige, the understansding of who we are, which gives rest; for our appropriate fills in all. Time can allow this. But it is the confusion of who we are and what it means to be, that causes grief and gruff. And by all counts, when pleasure is wanted, upon labor and wearyness, and something pleasing is knotted in you, you see the passivity in which you experienced other sweets. When they are there then were fine. But we are not in fact so well, underneath. And we know this. No love can block out how we really are. It just gives room to look past it, or fret not if its on your mind; in particular when circusmtance would squeeze such aspects out of you. So far we've come to let it all sink in, but furnish ourself with more. We like the manner of health, our work ethic, treating people well. But this remarks the condition of our way, the amends we must make: the need to stand tall. But other elements come about to. We like to write and uncover, to experience and look forward to. And all manners of adventure and goodness bring me to see; and far off is a near shore of things that reflect where my fortune may go.
 Today was a good day. For all its worth, we did not act fickle, nor were broken by our despondance. It is hard to think when your in such a state; and indeed it is much easier in the first hour or so. But when you slacken, and notice more, it is hard to conciliate. And we take it in, seeing ourself, breathing air, peacefully I might add, into those brightest portions of me. All worry and lust, fear and comparison melt away.
If we add groups of terms together, subsequent in the range of such groups, whereby the furthest term is removed while the newest is added, that doing so on a clock will a) return to the starting state, and b) do so as all other combinations of terms of the same kind of group [range] and clock [type]. Never has a sequence of this sort failed to meet this criteria. The reason is unknown, yet my familiairty with to process leads me to suppose that by cutting off remaining value, 'per the clock', that by some nature this leaves us with what we have.
