The pistons in my heart, the steel in my mind, all to an end of grand quality, or perhaps chugging along.
 Often I find myself struggling to remark upon things; and I see it as though there was this mechanism, some kind of motion, as may reflect a tamber or hue, but also direction, oriention, magnitude, and that such was how any given principle, fact, memroy or value was defined.
 There are rods which have not been moved for a time. And an odd thing of writing, that it tends to only speak of things you don't know. For the Gods, there is little which unerves me or lingers fancifully, 'making me curious'. And so reiteraitng or speaking to some small aspect is a challenge, as the whole is at rest, 'like Victor in his tomb'. And this is a good thing.
 But what I find is that we are still lacking things essential, or fundmental. On one end you have the blatant fact that 'such regards' are not so needed, as reflects having little to say, and that it is life and experience we care for. The lack of helming this leads to a rather unflavored nor checked character to our desires, and we feel ill in our pleasure, want of things that are not by any adult or substnatial degree ours. There is a false freedom that occurs by anothers provision, and you feel fine to let life come some other day, while you sit here, at ease, but also idle, and in response, you feel more consented to remedying pleasures: insincere ones, of the mind, of falsity or concept. Porn is the harshest partner in this.
 In any case, the flipside of this is that our life is in fact oppertune; and we tend not to have the stability, or harness in life, as to establish our self in such desire, when we are idle, or, as in those cases of given provision, unable, nor smooth in how able we are, to tend to such idleness by mending ourself. For such a state as would come from mending is a flowing natural one, where our desire sprouts readily about. It is but the constancy of life which we may be out of tune with, and thereby, via the force of labor and deference (when our fortune is not ours), that we fall away from that felicituous gait. And indeed, our life is our own so much as our ability and dream to effect our desired outcome is ours to both aim for, adjust to, relish, and proliferate. Swelling below is that odd statement, whereupon anothers shelter, that you feel unwelcomed to care for yourself, in the way that your felicity requires. It is perhaps only our parents who elicit this. I find a comparable feeling also when thinking of friends, or any who were close with or open to, that of our excuses, wearisomeness or concern, that we feel reservations of many a quality in sharing with them. It is not, by our parents or any close to us, that we feel odd or unwelcome in pursuing what we want, but rather in complaining, or struggling to reach it. Perhaps the end is stated unclearly, and by those counts, our most charmed remark is that 'the fruits of felicity are not a position to reach, nor product to meet, but rather a dance, a stride, a flow of grace and prosperity: it is a form of experience, that merely captures the embers of its experience, and folds them in as textures of its identity'. When we say that our life is about flow, and that we mean to live well, rather than well off, that we are saying in that something more than that we care for a quality or manner of life, but that we don't prioritize nor relish a house, nor fanciful travel, nor the dreary mundeandness of common touring; but instead, we wish to write a paper on the repitiion of starting states when operated on a clock, as do we wish to traverse the geographies of various objects: clouds, mountains, paleontology, constitutions and government. And I breathe in an delicacy of wonderful sights, of the performed sort. Withcer, Next Generation, Blue Planet 3, early Easy Allies, Beginner Servers, Bardown: so simple and common are they dear to me. "The imagination flushed inside me from experiecncing phantom menace, or the coruscant night." We struggle though, for twisting our hips, unwinding our shoulders, 'resting our eyes', is an ever obtuse thing; no more definite than the moon; each being but an output, or texture, of our manner. Indeed, the root of modern philosophy is in tactifully, but stewardly, speaking of the way in which we live paired with the objects born of that, or essential in some cases. For work is our life in a way, and as such this can be seen. But it is a sport, a performance, a test which a good sleep and sharpened pencil can satiate, when we regard it as such. Short of this, it is something other.
 A province of thought could be that pleasure, or the comfort of our experience, is quite fundmental, and stearing of our attiude and amends. It can be quite closing if we most often experience struggle; and we bolt down, lube the edges, and then remedy however much strife we experience.
 In brief, we have never lacked an expeirence which was unsatisfying enough for me to feel like anything extrordinary was required to reach it. Nor did my adolescence recieve any peruading impressions as to what could elsewhere be received. I always felt enough to do what we liked. The nature of our duties though became less creative nor occupational, 'as passing time in French class sometimes felt', but became more laborous; and the people around became less of my friends, for we were not invovled in recess or sports; and I did not care for cars or music as they did; and girls were this euphoric siren which blended the nature of our attitude and deeds.
Two thoughts on my mind, one from last night, the other this morning.
 The former is about objects and sentiment, or rather manner in things, whereby you move in a certain way, for a certain ideal, as though bonded to the nature of the state, but you then included, or at least sprout objects, facts, principles to an extent. And these often collide; as you find yourself loving, but a person in that gaze fills ill put. Our view of things then change.
 The latter thought remarks that idea of elementary school, as though it were our duty, sufficeint, but also pleasing, as we could just be there, comfort ourselves as we can, but surround ourselves with friend and company. Yet, this is a very still life, as though nothing is ever to change or move, away from this kind of life that is. And we just bolster it up. As the nature of our duty is not in fact school but work, we have larger gaps to surround with comfort and remedy. This is a weird feeling most young adults probally feel. But then there is another way to live, where you are not so beholden, situated nor complacent to a position, as though it will always be there, but you press on, move with intent and pace; and not to some end, but in your manner, with objects and things on your plate: the texture of your manner and gait as it were. What comes to mind is Vancouver and how we oftne imagine it as this lighter, softer, warmer place than here in Pitt Meadows; and we often included notions of love, promise, gallantry, as though to make our position more pleasing. But were stopped, to some halting end, merely a fairer one. Were not living our life. And indeed, this has been our impetus for an age, and our greatest times, where liberty stood on our own grounds, that we saw perhaps what comforts we had, what friends were around; as were we thrown by love, and perhaps to an end which was all to submiting to mere position rather than life; and then in moments where life was being lived, but with nothing really but some other on your mind, for which they did not humour our proposal for further bonding. In any case, we felt that life would move on, and as thought clear, 'as though a promising or tender thought that came across our mind', we simply let it come in and warm us, but then pass us by, as we were living now, occupied, our mind suttle yet bent, all the while we tend to ourselves. If people are doing this then it is in theyre own way, naturally, and so whether we do it this or that way, or with these or those things, so we are part of the game. And such a game is an ever present one; with no lunches nor breaks so to speak, merely a tilting of the helm. The sun for instance, glitters our day, but then upon her set, offers a moment to relish her final hues, but then ceases her daylight, and suggests to us that we turn in for the day. We may listen or not, but per sleep, which we need, and find affiable in the dark, and in relation to all other fixed things that occur in the day, that so do we humour this tunr of light for something which we respond to in resepect to sleep and rest, 'and days end'. All is connected, and it would seem that the greatest of these moving lives is where this is so. Indeed, it is often beholden to propriotous goods that allow this; and we often get caught on intent, or an absent of 'often taken for granted pleasures and conceit', whereby our practices are not so robust or known, yet our momentum is per the fruits they more or less provide, keeping us to such strata in things, but without sure fire ground. Keeping there though, we see the things needed to hold us. Much of my adult life has been about a calming of this arrangment, so that our priorities are not so sturdy yet narrow; and instead, we may live high, but amongst all things, friends and company, pursuit and awe; and via practices which are strong in theyre heart and princiuple, as opposed to the past habits which were so defined and fixed, but only affored specific supports. Our training for instance, has always alluded me in being something suitbale and constant, but otherwise welcomed and sustaining. Now though, per all things, a single day of practice suffices, and we do very well. I find myself worrying little whether we look good; and I am trying to take my mind off the fact of whether we look particularly healthy or not. There is so much to do beyond the minor confidence or esteem in this; and the qualification to impress or want even to draw people, or feel included; such is a small point, and not to an end which your more complacent mind could see. Such is the trap of love; that it often says, 'turn off your pistions, relax your heart, loose your life and way, and just be with folk, coalescent to what they think and like'. This is its own way of being bonded and affable per the life that such strata invovles. Its no different then yours.
 I feel perhaps blinded by other people merely living theyre own form of life, and that ours is not in principle any more signifcant or special. Why this is so is that we are not in motion of ours, nor flourishing with it, and so others feel above me. Better put, when I am not so mobile or active in ours, I see others; and often they get clumped up, whereby alot of them feel joined, while I sit here seperate from that. Have you given thought to all those in Kamloops, or Vancouver, or at Superstore in Coquitlam or Walmart in Maple Ridge? What about every family in Pitt Meadows, or every employee. Were not so immobile that a province further is worth regarding. "Theres merely more land heeding the suns shine."
I left for Kamloops with a bag of gold that I did not know I had. We settled there, remained active and relatively astute, but the place of our life, its meaning, our activity, fell to ware. And indeed, we came to ourself in the following fall, writing some of our dearest things and making our set of Battlefield videos. We broke down also. It compares to how we are now, something we feel and have felt for some time, but remain steady, or off title perhaps; but back then, we had it in our mind that certain things were a certain way, and that we could count on them. But as is common, a moment of love broke me off, and had me truly looking at myself. I'll come back to this feeling, or this view of things that we've brought forward, but I wish to move past that moment, and say that the time that followed, albeit inclusive of things born of a new resolve, were relatively the same. And the idea was that we came to ourselves, but without the pretensions which offered promise or affirmation. One element was our health, and how we spent a great deal of effort, at least intention, on our aesthetique, or appearing healthy. It was seldom easy to just do what was enough. And indeed, this has become simpler over the years, but our tolerance for only doing what we need has lead to vulnerabilities to inertia. One slick bit of friction is that trying a little, as to make up for natural inconsistency or oddity in nature, runs up against this sensitivity to do even more. A little feels like not enough, even though it is exactly the solid amount I need.
 All that is to say, that we had a very tender and balanced view of things. I think we were still a bit unprepared for things to come. But indeed, having reached the heights of that some two years later, I can see that our previous sense was not so far off, but that it was merely too unrigorous for the deeds ahead. For what I've noticed is, that upon labor and the more fixed path of life, that you feel a tremendous amount of effort required on your part. And because of this, you find yourself not liking everything; as your too worried about yourself. It is an odd thing indeed, for my insight over time was not that you could merely connect and or reveal such cares you had, and from that, not feel so hidden and or disdained. Rather, you just learn how to be open for open sake. Sharing that we like yoga, eating healthy, things like that which in some shape or form reflect what is essential to me, allow for us to bind with people. It has nothing to do with our response to pressure; these may be shared, but theyre so near and specific, that our relation needs to be such. But, we still do yoga and care for health, as we do games, and these things connect you so far as the depths of such eleemnt fit into the depths of the available connection. Too often we imbued these pressures, but then let our enamure and excitment, or buzz, carry us to be eager and enthused with people. But this was not really a source of connection but satisfaction on our part. And indeed, the flipside has occured, where tending to ourself without such flaunting or vanity, has me not so tailored to that satisfaction; which often flees away, as much of it is born from us being so eagerly there. But it keeps not. But, in being more steady, we form more meaningfull connections; not ones that reach, or mirror that other kind of buzz, but ones that you trust, where you feel free and ready to be yourself, known in your heart and principle.
 When we started work last year, we softened into this mindest with a fair bit of ease. But not with all. Certain people just did not come to sight, and in part it was because we were still so focused on ourself. It was a bit of a stale and rigid process, where we knew not to be so eager, and at worst, admitt and or humour expectations from it. But we felt not so fufilled as such. We quickly became affiable and close with some people. But our effort just found its groove; and who was easy to talk to we did, and who wasn't we did not. And we felt off about this, naturally, and we were perhaps eagerly courteous. As though to smooth off our sense of seperation, so I could just proceed.
The primary thought, of our life perhaps, is that we tend to ourselves in a great deal of ways, and via our time as children, we do this at pleasures perril, for we sanction ourself off; or, as our adulthood has shown, make it merely a higher bar for us to be present with people. I've learned the hard way what happens when you reach that point, connect, and perhaps in a state that reflects the charm of that threshold (a high point of excess); but then upon our personal lapse, we fall either alone, or make haste ahead, 'as though to keep what we feel like were losing'. This happened when we were suppose to stay home for two weeks during March, and we had just started talking to Holly.
Early in the year, near its start, we had resolve to content ourselves with work and let life plod along. We found ourself rather pleased and with company, and all that stood in our way was this drowning sense, which our own place would mitigate. Upon reaching that place, I failed, and fell into a iron stalemate. We did not eat for a week, and felt some oddity of lostlessness. For I still sought to move, yet it seemed so far away. But by all counts this plea was not so fundmeental, but one of prefernece; as though 'sure, we'll stay for the summer, we just need this change of scenery. Yet the summer was not important, and in fact, only drew us because our life was fair. But it was not exactly bounding; nor in tune with many of the things we felt some larger change were required to meet. It was simply strange to feel so still and idle, for the prospect was one for mere continuity; yet we felt so unable to be continuous now. Such was the fabric of our live, merely wanting to improve, but loosing the strands which held it up.
 I recall this feeling as I was walking with tristan near the bus loop, and that was this sense of being where I was, present as I wanted to be, but without the rule, the standard. We have always held true to ourself; perhaps just not well enough; though the foundation which exhibited itself in Vancouver still remained; and its elements can be more or less described, and indeed influenced us in our latter time at Kamloops, to an extent during last years spring, and seemingly to a rather steady and comfortable flourishing in this early year. But I personally felt stopped; as though remaining at home, yet with the intent to leave, which by all counts was a fair aim for oru interest in being present, yet ourselves, made our intent for ourselve rather troubling. It is a similar feeling when your PC breaks or performs poorly; and had it been at a state which was an improvment you'd feel fine, but it being a regression makes it hard to swallow. What occured though was that we humoured the thought of not being ourself at all. For the response, as lingered with Holly during Covid, was one, where given the halt in our 'ideal change', that in remaining where we were, that we'd have to turn into ourselves in order to mantle it. True, we could reach the moderate stability we had during our iniative to find a change in place as to allow it to be improved. But this felt unappealling nor tenuable. It was a spiritual whiplash. We choose not to do that, but instead, humoured the position in which our stability offered us to. You see, everyone is themselves; and when theyre tired or busy have not much to say, nor are open and malleable for connection, or communion --beyond what is crystallized in the depths. Now I have historically had a hard time being in such place, for we held so much worry and or practice, that we barely poked our head above. And when we did, we found ourselves unstable, as though we were walking for the first time, slipping all over the place. That, or we just didn't have the momemntum or fluidity to make any real substantial effort or union, given our slight excess. More or less we have grown; and further by the day. Hard it is so see how easy it was. But sometimes our enthusiasm for having such excess was misplaced; as starting last year, we found ourselves excited about being open and able about our loves, but not our ways; and this latter sits much closer to the line of union. In part, those loves are what you bring forth; and we came from that.
 I recall rather fondly the month of Decemebr; or better put, the time following Christmas, where we played Dragons Dogma and Baludrs Gate. Something to note, is that despite our comfort from Bella, it wasn't all too substnatial, nor was it rested on meeting aynthing more. By all counts it was a novel change from someone who, like Morgan, was a deafening spot, or one that brought more inertia than movment; but second, is that it was just nice and pleasing, as it is with Alex and Andy, Joey and Oliver, Chenoya to and the gals, and Victor. The point, is that our resolve was one where we could be ourselves. I think in part, as we felt when moved in here, 'and looked at ourself in the mirror, all sexy and hot, but no where to go', that we felt some simialr kind of promise; as though we coudl have Tristan over at our house, and we dreamt deep down that perhaps Bella to, or, further, Amon. This was reaching outside of our contentment and ease. For life was clear during those months; for Christmas brought joy, but we then felt like it was time and oppertune to move, and we then played Baldurs Gate. We felt solid, and able in being ourself. But like all things, we did not pay much respect to how things wuold naturally settle. Perhaps we would have felt this way regardless, and that it was in many ways but an acceleration of your eventual want to ask Bella out, or feel lost without it. Feeling down just prompted this, as did her saying no force this realization of ourselves, that we are lost.
I wish to do a bit of a critical analysis, of the reason to move to Vnacouver, our finances, as may speak to our need to, or rather haste to.
 What comes to mind is meetups, as theyre are so many across the land. The walking group and John Henry speaks to me, as I love the area, and the bout is not much of a hike. The practical philosophy group, perhaps niche in its kind, is a definite gem of things; for it is in person, I believe thursday evenings, and just a solid thing to go to. When I dream of the best day, or greatest life, it is one where, with the setting sun, you go to such thing. And you may scooter there and back, or transit a little. It reminds me of going to PT class, and how we'd stop far back and walk across town.
 As for our finances, we are pretty equal in our gait. Were working 3 and 4, which brings us just over 1200, which is ample. We are spending some money, perhaps a little too much on food. We've bought Kingdom Come, which was a short yet sweet experience, and we bought Ark, which has been worthile; as I've learned that being friends with someone, like Justin, is really about keeping in touch, and you can always say hello. We have many things from Amazon, all relatively small. Most are going back soon, though our big water cooler needs to go back before the 26th.
My mind gets caught about Bella somtimes, and in all reality it is merely about our own energy, our own vigor, and how sometimes it feels too unsettled around her. The soul fact is that we find ourself trying to be eager and enthused, as though to elevate us; not something which continues through the day. But when she is there, my wish or comfort in being so lessens. And on one hand this may evoke false or exagerrated feelings of views about her, as one who evokes this lethargy. On the other, it really just speaks to how you are with any person who you don't know, and how your naturally compelled, or moved, to be less eradict, compared to how you are with Andy and Joey, rather than Hazel.
 I find our time rather ambivolent. But this is a good thing. Wounds are healing, and foremost, our handle on things is becoming firm yet suttle, nor are we so swayed. Principle to this development is this removal of our sense, or at least less rigid response, which ellicits this feeling that other people are more important and that you are not. Perhaps it is just the buisiness of the day which throws me sometimes, or slackens our ability to fit in. Remaining calm though, which happens quite easily when it is not so busy, settles everything in. And something I find very oppertune, is that Bella, being a unique member, is so as to be somewhat difficult to talk to. I spoke with Anthony today, as do I feel genial with Hazel. The point is not how we are, as though this should anchor you, but that you are free, at liberty. Were not so amazed by what other people are doing. I think in part they are there, as though some side of theyre life, but that where they are is not so satisfying. However well theyre life is around this, it is carried with theyre work; and whoever they are with at work, so theyre work is there. This is not so important though, just something I noticed. Especially so when you are friendly and medial with all people. This is brought further by being part of the store's day. And again, its not abaout anchoring; this is the moral. In that, you are kept, as though to feel inevibtaly secure. While a more liberal and sturdy approach, that does not grip, is merely with, unafraid, bringing our true self. The time keeps on and we all leave. If theyre are jokes to be had, I dare say I care not for any who have them. For those who I am closest with, it is my least favorite part. And time just goes on. Max even said, 'i'm a shithead'. That is what makes them less adult like, in theyre complacence to theyre shit. As in all things, eyeing down and trying to define what something is merely firms the distance you are from yourself; which indeed, requires its own kind of form, but only that which allows you to be free, not compelled, not ignored, nor sheltered from. We are theyre through and through, to all. And appropriatley as things meet. Which is the case for Bella. As we are not so strange and unfamiliar, as we are with Hazel or Anthony. We have a weird history. And it is not for me to ploy nor be coy in wishing for or lamenting about us being friends. But our freedom may exist. Like a wet towel the water rings out.
I don't know if there is any real truth or right. I am not defering to optimism or uprightness either.
 One notion is that things are not as easy as any moment may make you feel they are. Comparison is not a useful tool here, despite revealling something about ourself.
 In any case, it feels at the core of things that our struggle, or uncertainty, lies at that point where things are well, we are free and fine, but we feel somewhat seperate from things pleasing. Our whole life the extent of this has reached far and wide. Whereas now it is almost near to me. But the insight, or reflection, is that this notion of things being well, is true, but that you should go forward and make your dreams come to be, or engage in pleasure, looks past the point that there is still much to do, and that such things are not so easy. In fact there the most challenging of things. Not constant in theyre toil, but in theyre adherence. Which by all counts is a sign of progress, where you do these things naturally, and flow with such manner in your stride; whereby there is less doubt and more shine ahead.
One quick though, an impusle if you will, but we feel like were part of the world or were not, and in any many ways it comes down to interests. There is a bit of overlap everywhere, but as Tim says, there are different worlds
So just doing a bit of Tinder research. At first glance, I realize that our pictures are not that interesting. We may look well, but its just a portrait. Were not doing anything, out anywhere. So be it.
 So Keenan has a well worded note about being on two wheels or mid movie marathon. The heart of this is not informative but elicitive of a vibe. He says he's looking for great sense of humor, down for something serious or just have fun. I feel its important to say something like this
This next guy, beside his fashion, has 'after work vibes' baked into the image. You can barely see his face, not the greatest impression.
So Adam has a nice picture, but its in a mirror, and he's looking at his camera, head tilted. So these 'mirror shots' are unconfident. I recognize that we don't take alot of pictures, and its as though were just meeting the foramlity. But if we look at the camera, smile well, have good lighting, and show our nice face, then I think there is some charm and confidence. Who responds to that I dont know, but it doesnt have to be everyone. Someone who is sweet, less superficial, but can appreciate strenght and kindness, I feel we are along those lines
So Sean is the first real guy. My first impression is that you don't look to heavy into someones eyes, and so I feel that bodes well for us. Also, people have multiple pictures, and I dont know how much that mattaers. He has a personal description, which is polar opposite to a 'hey just lookin around'. Some aspect of being personal feels fine, though I often tend to think of qualities we have rather than interests.
So Trevor has a very clever and witty summary, which is kind of funny, a little confident and bravose, but feels effective. Jokes are hard to pull off. I find the best ones are one liners amongst more serious things. Again, mirror shots are a little pathetic. I find that if we take better pictures then we will realize the confidence and straighforward charm we have. Looking at 5 or 6 profiles, these are all ordinary dudes, and in similar age range. Its an ecosystem for sure, but no one is getting 1000 more likes that anybody. It that point, you trust your profile, engage with platform, see what hits. Its great practice for us to do this hear where you shortcomings are exasterbated. Well learn, be more confidnet
So Simon is looking for love, and it is clear, that per your intent, you say more meainginfully, as your serious
Richmond has a generic summary, saying 'I want to meet someone who enjoys good conversation, and is up for spontaenous adventures'. I'd say if your looking for something casual, then make a mere remark of that, rather than be corny. Otherwise dont mention any of this at all. By all counts this is not a website for you to browse, see who interests you, then start up a conversation. Its a swiping service. Who really goes through the profile before swiping? Really? By all counts it would serve you to make your profile as though someone already swiped, and wanted to learn more, or were checking.
I find that sweet might describes me the most, that I am kind, mature, confident, strong, but also sweet, very funny, easy going. Being flawed is an odd thing to admitt, but something no less.
Sean has the best picture I've seen. Not saying I want to fuck him, but I immediatley like him more than the dude without a shirt, or everyone who is in a mirro. He's looking at the camera, a calm yet generous smile. Respectable
Captainredbear, learn to spell. And dont say you dont have time to do anything so your here. He mentions he's an old soul. Feels like a line, which makes me think that a) if were putting a line then let it be good as so, or b) make it not so much of a line, but meaningfull.
Zack mentions he has not time for a relationship but is up for fun dates. I am unsettled on the need or value of mentioning this. Matches just generally happen, and it is quite hard and obscure. I see that there may be two kinds of pictures: here is me, here is what I offer. Seems odd that you'd earn anything with the former. But maybe there are people just looking for other people, not neccessarily a sugar day, or anyhting finer but of that domain.
I find that most people have a rather unfocused or directed picutre, while others present themselves more firmly. They do this with a broad stance, or show theyre muscles. I simple smile. That is me being me. Maybe words can illumintate what is behind the smile.
Two thoughts: were really smart, very confident, mature, sweet and kind. I have alot of friends but am seeking something to bond with, care for, live meaingfully with --for however long. Not here for/lloking for flings. Not against it thought. Looking for something with some substance, someone to text good morning to.
I cant speak for woman. But, one prevailing thought, a principle truth, is that however similar people are, it is like school, in that we handle our grades, attendance and effort ourselves. So how people are received on theyre profile, and how people like other peopels profile, at best has shared tendencies per some shared kind or quality, but they amend themselves indiviually. It is weird and strange to see how any of these people heed anything at all. It is possible that someone who goes on 10 dates misses a 100.
A few points for the weekend.
 For one, Tuesday and Wedensday are work, which is great. Then only Friday. Week after is BC day, then 4 4 hours, which is a strain sleep wise. Ive noticed that incossitency, as we experienced earlier in the week, makes me feel tired. This monring doing some arm floats really aided me, and showed how tightness, as we felt (greatly mind you) on Tuesday. So were still carrying that with me. Were fine, buta little slow. And I dont want to eat so much. We can mention that, having 2 smoothies rather than 1. We've got plenty of berries and milk, and bananas. Some avocado and kale would be nice also. Lets find some soft ones, and cucumber to. Right now, I dont need big bouts of grain, but lighter food; still plenty though, but more gracefull.
This is perhaps much, but I truly love the sun, her rise and set, as it fills my heart with peace; and I am such a man as to have a heart which may be peaceful
This idea has not risen in relation to us moving afar, but rather compares itself to our wish to move near Laity in the near future. Indeed, that hope is based on the relation to the north fields and proximity to east maple ridge, which the fall colors elicit. And this is fair and fine. But I also feel quite settled in our spot. Awyn is an annoying little rat, but very unprolific as so. Only in our grumpy moods does he evoke anything in me. Nev is great and there is no one new moving; no one has at leasat. This could change mind you. Though, these elements are not so determining. It is really our neighbourhood, our environment. The cage will come down soon, and I find the little maze of streets, from hammond, to wairsely down to 203rd, through the Jordan area, across near westview and that lovely backroad, to the homes down by GMC, and old hammond at that, to give me a nice space to be. Pitt Ahtletic is close, as is far 203rd, and cutting through laity and MRSS is not too far. Going down 218th is not so far a route.
 There is something to be said about making do where were at, and rather than look for, or humour the wish for something new and different, we make our scenario more pallatable now.
 We currently make 1200 working 35 hours every two weeks. Removing that extra 5 would help so much, as a 4 day week is so much harder than a 3. And there is almost no room not to do that 4th. There is a stat coming in September, and 2 more the month after, then GST in october, so there will be room to even out our work load. But, the question of worth to me is whether there would be reason enough to stay, committ, and in effect cease your want to move to Laity, if you stayed here for 6 more months, on a far healthier work schedule, room for more food and training, balanced between Maple Ridge and Pitt, rather than only the former. There isn't so much to put up with; Amon and husband would not really overt this from me. Its more about the good I could gleam. One little thhing that has helped is the Church parking lot, which has given me somewhere close to walk to. There is just so much beauty on this 207th street, waling northward in particular, and going up 107th has a fair bit of ease and fancy. Going to Riverside is always nice, and is not too far. Hammond is still fair, and will get even fairer. There is just something comeplete about the whole area. It can feel small when I am not willing to walk the slightly larger distances to things --compared to the immedate paths of 49th. And we are a bit far from the fields and such views. But I find a moving pace accomodates these by more local rides, whereby there are whole manners of views and angles and roads to go. Or we have enough time and energy to go up the bridge, to Pitt Ahtletic, up 203rd, or the Pumpkin trail.
It is worth noting that much of our wish to move to Laity is so that I can easier explore Maple Rdige. The contrasting state is one where I can still go out there, and given our freer coin, we may bus more liberally (as can we train). And this in part equals that wish. Indeed, it would be cool to live further northeast, closer to the fields, closer to Maple Ridge park and silver valley. One point though, is these are ultimatley excursions, and we are trying to live great lives. Similar to work, we've made a home here, and it is working well. I think the hammond stadium being closed off has delfated much of our appeal in it, and this will soon change.
So, as you know I've been looking at places for some time. There are many which are more affordable but not in the ideal location. But I more than likely will be here for a month or two more. I do like our place though, and was wondering if I signed a lease, if I could lower the price. 800 would be that price, and I understand if that's not feasible. I'm not rushing to get out of here otherwise, but it will happen sooner or later. I would sign a longer term lease though for that price and would be quite happy to keep living here.
So I've thought of a fairly lovely way of describing the starting and advancing states. Some thanks to Gp.
 For one, you may start all talks and establishments of first principle, with a (7,7), as to work with a 12 hour clock, as its known, and the first succeeding state is (7,2). If I were at liberty, than I could make a podcast because I wanted to, join a group or organization for the pure moral sentiment, or try this or that, or study.
 What is our aim though? We think perhaps it is an ultimate, and perhaps sentimental ideal, of proper discourse, and that it is less so about us being heard, but actually imparting what we believe to be the thing which can affect change. Much of our reserve, or auseterity in thought, comes down to our own ignorance of how things are operated, but also in deference to how it is pithily viewed. I actually think that if we could sprout a more reasonable perspective and conduct regarding government, war, death and the gods, that some sort of improvement could be made. In part, as unclear or decisive as this progress or benefit is known, then we rest on our knowledge of things, and how the way they operate is not so monolithic, but quite localized, varied, calm. Odd things come from odd connections with one of the many branches in the higher strucutre, or between to individuals who cross paths.
 I find myself though, similar to sums, or our study of anything, our health even, leaning into steadyness, and letting these things be; were confident how they are and that they'll be, but the manner in which they do seems to come from our liberty, which is brought by nothing more than the harmony in our deeds, and the sweet rigor in our stide; to have such thoughts, work on them, and bring us to act. Sums has become this in the recent past, where the idea of sharing it, though lined with some procrastination, has been moved on with deliberate intent; we've been learning what to write and say as though we were sharing it, and by all counts, the composition of our technical thoughtt has more than doubled. We also told Matin about it, quite well so far as we could, and the idea came to mind that we'd share it with Justin. The ppint is not that they offer some reward or prospect, but that by our liberty, we thought of the effort on the whole, tended to that, and through clarity, felt eager and at ease to speak of it. That is our sprouting line. And indeed, I find that the actual amend to email it is a small yet mountanous task, and one that could perhaps use its own development in composition. But I also see, that such a thing is pure liberty, rather than something which we are otherwise happy to just do on a whim. Its that feeling of gambling, or taking bets, that your happy enugh now to concived a reward for trying something; but you fear not if you don't get it because your happy. This disconnect here is that your not so compelled to do it so well; but in contrast, you also may do it well enough, or at all. And these feelings come and go, as we are more bent towards this latter motion, where the quality of the piece is more emphasized, as we are not so ambivolent about the possible reward, yet at the same time a little callous in our excitment. It feels more like a steady pursuit, that is not riled up by some esteem or remarkibility in the work; and so it is not some shot that we are clearly oppertune to take. It feels like we have to do it well. There is an underlying current of promise, but it is more interwined in the subject-matter and experience, rather than glory. `
